articles.title: Automated Opportunistic Bone Mineral Density Assessment at Low-Dose CT Lung Cancer Screening: Incident Vertebral Fractures and Mortality.
articles.abstract: Background Low-dose CT (LDCT) for lung cancer screening enables opportunistic volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) assessment, but its prognostic value is unclear. Purpose To evaluate fully automated LDCT-derived vBMD for predicting vertebral fractures and its association with mortality in individuals who heavily smoke. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis included 55-74-year-old individuals who heavily smoked (≥30 pack-years) from the CT arm of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST), a multicenter randomized controlled trial of LDCT versus radiography (participants recruited August 2002 to April 2004). Automated SpineQ software (Bonescreen) was used to measure thoracic and lumbar vBMD (normal, ≥120 mg/cm3; low bone mass [osteopenia], 80 to <120 mg/cm3; osteoporosis, <80 mg/cm3) and vertebral fractures (Genant scale). The outcomes included 1- and 2-year incident vertebral fractures and 6-year mortality (active follow-up to 2009). Poisson and Cox models were adjusted for demographic variables, available comorbidities, and baseline vertebral fractures. Results The NLST included 26 722 participants in the CT arm, with 21 856 included in the present analysis (mean age, 61 years ± 5 [SD]; 12 854 male participants). The 2-year vertebral fracture incidence (n = 18 211 participants with 2-year LDCT) was 0.9% for those with normal bone mass, 2.0% for those with low bone mass (adjusted relative risk, 2.07 [95% CI: 1.70, 2.53]), and 5.9% for those with osteoporosis (adjusted relative risk, 3.40 [95% CI: 2.69, 4.30]). Mortality risk (n = 21 447 participants with completed follow-up [median, 6.65 years]) was associated with osteoporotic vBMD in men (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.24 [95% CI: 1.02, 1.50]). Conclusion Fully automated opportunistic assessment of spinal vBMD predicted vertebral fracture risk and was associated with mortality in men after adjustment. Individuals with osteoporotic vBMD who heavily smoked had a 2-year fracture incidence above the 5% treatment threshold according to current osteoporosis guidelines. Clinical trial registration no. NCT00047385 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Bredella in this issue.

articles.title: Intended Thrombectomy for Basilar Artery Occlusion with Mild Deficits: Evidence from a Multicenter Prospective Registry.
articles.abstract: Background The role of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in basilar artery occlusion (BAO) with mild deficits (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score < 10) remains uncertain. Purpose To compare the outcomes of EVT combined with best medical management (BMM) versus BMM alone in individuals with BAO and mild deficits. Materials and Methods Consecutive eligible patients treated at eight stroke centers between September 2023 and March 2025 were enrolled in a prospective registry. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score of 0-2). Secondary outcomes were 90-day excellent outcome (mRS score of 0-1), death, and early neurologic deterioration (END), defined as a four-point or greater increase in NIHSS score within 72 hours. Primary analyses followed an intention-to-treat-like framework with inverse probability weighting (IPW). As-treated and per-protocol sensitivity analyses were used to assess the robustness of the results and the impact of treatment crossover (EVT after END). Results Among 401 participants (mean age, 64.9 years ± 8.9 [SD]; 278 male participants), the median onset-to-arterial-puncture time in the EVT group was 402 minutes (IQR, 271-583 minutes). After multivariable adjustment in the IPW-adjusted data, EVT was associated with higher odds of functional independence (odds ratio [OR], 1.55 [95% CI: 1.17, 2.06]) and excellent outcome (OR, 1.48 [95% CI: 1.09, 2.03]) and lower odds of death (OR, 0.65 [95% CI: 0.45, 0.77]) and END (OR, 0.35 [95% CI: 0.20, 0.61]). Subgroup analyses demonstrated EVT-related functional benefit in participants with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not in those with NIHSS scores of 0-5 (P for interaction = .02 for functional independence); however, in participants with NIHSS scores of 0-5, EVT was associated with lower odds of END and death. Sensitivity analyses accounting for treatment crossover showed attenuated functional advantage for EVT. Conclusion In participants with BAO and mild deficits, EVT plus BMM was associated with better outcomes than BMM alone; however, functional benefit was observed in those with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not those with NIHSS scores of 0-5. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry no. ChiCTR2300075711 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: ESR Essentials: "Gadolinium-free" pediatric neuroimaging-practice recommendations by the European Society of Neuroradiology.
articles.abstract: Gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCA) have been central to magnetic resonance neuroimaging, enhancing diagnostic sensitivity and accuracy, in both adults and children. However, their increasingly widespread use has raised concerns, as evidence exists of gadolinium retention in brain tissue after repeated use. This paper outlines some updated strategies to reduce GBCA administration in pediatric neuroradiology, based on both recent literature and the authors' clinical experience. This paper, therefore, should be considered as a concise review of the main literature data and the opinion of a group of experts in the field, based on their daily practice in large institutions. We mention those most frequent conditions where the usage of GBCA often represents a longstanding, albeit "not strictly evidence-based," common practice which can be critically reconsidered. The use of GBCA in pediatric neuroimaging should be considered carefully based on each case scenario, evaluating if GBCA may provide real and substantial potential benefits to patient management and outcome. KEY POINTS: The use of GBCA in pediatric neuroimaging should be carefully evaluated by the pediatric neuroradiologist on an individual basis, and it should also be supported by specific literature data if present, so as to balance risks and benefits and to improve patient management and outcome. Possible alternative strategies to the use of GBCA may be considered in some cases under a close relationship between pediatric neuroradiologists and clinicians. Prospective development of new sequences is needed to improve unenhanced MR imaging accuracy and expand "Gd-free" examinations.

articles.title: Agentic AI Systems in Radiology: Design, Applications, Evaluation, and Challenges.
articles.abstract: Building agents that perceive and act on their environment with a degree of autonomy has long been a focus of artificial intelligence research. This pursuit has become far more practical with the emergence of large language models (LLMs) capable of using natural language to integrate information, follow instructions, and perform forms of reasoning and planning across a wide range of tasks. With its multimodal data streams and orchestrated workflows spanning multiple systems, radiology is uniquely suited to benefit from agents that can adapt to context and automate complex, repetitive tasks. In radiology, LLMs and their multimodal variants have already demonstrated promising performance for individual tasks such as information extraction and report summarization. However, using LLMs in isolation underutilizes their potential to support complex, multistep workflows where decisions depend on evolving context from multiple information sources. Equipping LLMs with external tools and feedback mechanisms enables them to drive systems that exhibit a spectrum of autonomy, ranging from semiautomated workflows to more adaptive agents capable of managing complex processes. This review article examines the design of LLM-driven agentic systems, explores representative radiology applications, discusses evaluation frameworks, and outlines key challenges, including error cascades, tool-use effectiveness, and integration with health information technology infrastructure.

articles.title: Retrospective AI Search for Missed Pulmonary Nodules on Emergency Department Chest Radiographs: A Multicenter Brief Report.
US Markers in the Noninvasive Assessment of Hepatic Steatosis in Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Background Attenuation coefficient (AC) is an established US marker for assessing patients with liver steatosis. However, improvements in diagnostic performance are warranted. Purpose To evaluate the diagnostic performance of AC, normalized local variance (NLV), hepatorenal ratio, and their combinations for liver histopathologic steatosis in participants with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Materials and Methods This secondary analysis of the prospective Innovative Liver Elasticity, Attenuation, and Dispersion Ultrasound Study (iLEAD) (June 2019 to March 2023) included participants with biopsy-proven MASLD who underwent multiparametric liver US; AC, NLV, and hepatorenal ratio were measured. The diagnostic performance of each imaging marker and their combinations for determining steatosis grade were assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with the DeLong test, and reclassification improvement was also assessed using the category-free net reclassification improvement (NRI). Results A total of 102 participants (mean age, 52 years ± 16.1 [SD]; 51 male) were evaluated. AC showed the highest diagnostic performance for determining steatosis grade across all grades (AUC for grade ≥S1, 0.93 [95% CI: 0.87, 0.99]), compared with NLV (0.88 [95% CI: 0.77, 0.99]; P = .47) and hepatorenal ratio (0.85 [95% CI: 0.71, 0.98]; P = .30). Four models were constructed for identifying steatosis grades: model 1, AC only; model 2, AC plus NLV; model 3, AC plus hepatorenal ratio; model 4, AC plus NLV plus hepatorenal ratio. Models 2-4 showed no evidence of a difference in performance from model 1 for identifying grade S1 or higher (AUC, 0.93-0.98; P = .16, .15, and .07, respectively), but an improvement in risk reclassification was observed for model 4 (NRI, 1.18 [95% CI: 0.54, 1.77]; P < .001) compared with model 1 (reference). Performance was similar across models in identifying steatosis grade S2 or greater (AUC, 0.89-0.90; all P ≥ .47) and for grade S3 (AUC, 0.89-0.90; all P ≥ .72), but an improvement in risk reclassification was observed for model 3 compared with model 1 (≥S2 steatosis: NRI, 0.58 [95% CI: 0.20, 0.94] [P = .002]; S3 steatosis: NRI, 0.71 [95% CI: 0.26, 1.14] [P = .002]). Conclusion Liver US-derived AC performed better than NLV and hepatorenal ratio in determining steatosis grade in participants with MASLD; when these markers were combined, reclassification of steatosis grade improved. Clinical trial registration no. NCT04012242 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Case 355.
articles.abstract: An 8-year-old girl presented to the pediatrician with headaches that she had been experiencing for the last 2-3 years but that had become intolerable in the previous 8 days. The headaches were described by the patient as not having any lateralization and mainly involving the frontal and occipital regions. The headaches were rated by the patient as being an eight out of 10 in terms of pain, which prevented her from sleeping. Analgesic therapy proved to be ineffective. The patient had no photophobia or phonophobia but had increased fatigue alongside developing nausea without vomiting. The patient did not have any dysphagia, ataxia, vertigo, or elocution issues. Previous MRI performed in a provincial hospital showed a mass in the posterior fossa that was displacing the brainstem. However, being unable to get an appointment to see a neurosurgeon in a timely manner, the patient presented to the emergency department of our university hospital due to worsening symptoms. In order to exclude an intracranial origin of the symptoms, brain MRI with contrast enhancement was performed (Figure).

articles.title: Case 351: Thalamic Dementia Secondary to Dural Arteriovenous Fistula.
articles.abstract: A 76-year-old man with a medical history of diabetes, hypertension, and dilated cardiomyopathy developed new symptoms of confusion, repeated falls, and urinary incontinence over the course of 3-4 months, which worsened over a 2-week period, leading to presentation at the emergency room. His partner reported that before this, he had no memory or movement disorders, but now he was experiencing memory lapses, such as forgetting his mother's recent death, and functional cognitive problems, including an inability to remember how to perform tasks that were previously simple for him, such as dosing his insulin with meals. At presentation, the patient was awake and alert, oriented to his name and location but not to the date. Full neurologic examinations, including of the motor and sensory systems and cranial nerves, were normal. There were no signs of meningism, no fever or leukocytosis, and no history of recent travel. Serum electrolyte panel and thiamine levels were normal, and he had no history of alcohol or drug abuse. Initial evaluation included noncontrast CT of the head, the results of which prompted multiphasic CT angiography of the head including parenchymal phase imaging and admission for observation and monitoring with serial noncontrast CT of the head. The patient's symptoms worsened during his hospital stay. He also developed facial twitching, increased drowsiness, and seizure episodes. He was therefore evaluated with noncontrast MRI of the brain and then digital subtraction angiography with external carotid artery and internal carotid artery contrast agent injections.

articles.title: Expanding the Value of Lung Cancer Screening through Skeletal Risk Assessment.
Ultra-high-resolution 5 T MR neurography: first steps.
articles.abstract: Magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) is an established technique for peripheral nerve assessment, enabling high-resolution visualization of nerves and simultaneous evaluation of adjacent musculoskeletal structures. Although optimized 3 T MRI remains the clinical standard, whole-body 5 T systems have emerged as a potential intermediate platform between 3 T and 7 T imaging. Direct peer-reviewed evidence for peripheral MRN at 5 T remains limited to a single pilot study of the inferior alveolar nerve, with no prospective validation of the brachial plexus, lumbosacral plexus, or limb nerves. Physical and engineering studies suggest that 5 T MRI may provide greater signal availability than 3 T while presenting less severe radiofrequency-related challenges than 7 T; however, the relevance of this theoretical balance to peripheral nerve imaging remains unproven. The additional signal available at 5 T could theoretically be allocated to higher spatial resolution, greater acceleration, or broader anatomical coverage, but these potential gains have not been validated against optimized 3 T MRN. Potential applications include the evaluation of entrapment neuropathies, traumatic nerve injuries, inflammatory neuropathies, peripheral nerve tumors, and the implementation of quantitative approaches such as diffusion tensor imaging, T2 mapping, and T1ρ imaging. Furthermore, artificial intelligence-based reconstruction, denoising, and acceleration strategies may improve the clinical feasibility of ultra-high-resolution neurography by reducing scan times while preserving image quality. This narrative review examines the limited published evidence, physical rationale, technical requirements, preliminary institutional experience, and research priorities for 5 T MRN.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence for Rupture Risk Stratification of Small Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms (≤ 7 mm): A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Small unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIAs; ≤ 7 mm) carry collectively significant rupture risk, yet conventional scoring tools (PHASES, ELAPSS) perform near chance-level in this subgroup. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the pooled diagnostic accuracy of AI-based models for rupture risk prediction in small UIAs and compared performance across algorithmic architectures. Prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251142915) and conducted per PRISMA-DTA/PRISMA-S standards. MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched in October 2025 and updated on June 2026. Eligible studies applied machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), radiomics, or computational fluid dynamics-integrated models to small UIAs. Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was pooled via a three-level random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Knapp-Hartung correction; heterogeneity was explored through multivariable meta-regression. Bias and reporting quality were assessed using QUADAS-3 and METRICS, respectively. Ten studies (2019-2025) encompassing 5409 patients, 7057 aneurysms, and 62 models were included. Pooled AUC was 0.793 (95% CI 0.754-0.827), with sensitivity of 0.713 and specificity of 0.780. Conventional ML achieved the highest AUC (0.827), followed by statistical models (0.779) and DL (0.741). Meta-regression explained 76.2% of variance; statistical model family was the sole significant predictor of inferior performance (p = 0.002). Nine of ten studies carried high risk of bias. No publication bias was detected (p = 0.186). AI-based models, particularly conventional ML ensemble architectures, demonstrate moderate-to-good discriminative accuracy for small UIA rupture risk stratification, meaningfully surpassing conventional scoring tools. Multicenter prospective registries, pre-rupture imaging protocols, and explainable AI frameworks are essential to support transparent neurosurgical decision-making.

articles.title: Imaging classification of pancreatic cystic lesions: a radiologist's guide.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic cystic lesions (PCLs) are increasingly encountered in clinical practice owing to the widespread use of high-resolution cross-sectional imaging. These lesions comprise a heterogeneous group of entities ranging from benign cysts to pre-malignant neoplasms and invasive cancers, making accurate characterization essential for appropriate patient surveillance and therapeutic management. Imaging plays a pivotal role in lesion detection, differential diagnosis, and assessment of malignant potential. This review presents a practical imaging-based classification of PCLs founded on lesion morphology, relationship to the pancreatic ductal system, enhancement patterns, and associated imaging features. Using a stepwise diagnostic approach, pancreatic cystic lesions are categorized according to their increasing risk of malignancy into non-neoplastic cysts, serous cystic neoplasms, mucinous cystic lesions, and cystic degeneration of solid pancreatic tumors. Characteristic imaging findings, relevant differential diagnostic considerations, and imaging features associated with increased malignant potential are comprehensively reviewed, with particular emphasis on the role of MRI and MR cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) in lesion characterization. A structured pattern-recognition flowchart is proposed to facilitate routine image interpretation and enhance diagnostic confidence. In addition, a practical reporting template is presented to promote standardized assessment and effective communication within multidisciplinary teams. Emerging techniques, including diffusion-weighted imaging, quantitative MRI biomarkers, radiomics, artificial intelligence, and molecular analysis of cyst fluid, are discussed as promising tools for improving diagnostic accuracy and refining risk stratification. By emphasizing readily recognizable imaging features and a systematic diagnostic workflow, this review provides radiologists with a practical and clinically applicable framework for the evaluation, diagnosis, risk assessment, and multidisciplinary management of pancreatic cystic lesions.

articles.title: US-guided Hydrodissection for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: An Early Career Perspective.
Photon-counting CT in Bariatric Imaging and Body Composition: An Early Career Perspective.
Arteriovenous Malformations as Neoplastic-Like Lesions: Molecular Underpinnings and Implications for the Interventional Radiologist.
articles.abstract: Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are high-flow vascular anomalies traditionally treated as congenital structural lesions with embolization or surgical resection. However, recurrence after embolization alone exceeds 90%, underscoring incomplete understanding of their biology. Next-generation sequencing has identified somatic gain-of-function mutations in KRAS, MAP2K1, BRAF, and HRAS as drivers of sporadic AVMs. Confined to lesional endothelial cells, these mutations activate RAS/MAPK signaling and support a neoplastic-like rather than purely structural disease model. This has therapeutic implications: MEK inhibitors, particularly trametinib, have shown angiographic and clinical responses in refractory AVMs. Interventional radiologists can obtain draining vein liquid-biopsy samples during embolization for molecular genotyping; embolization may increase circulating cell-free DNA yield. This review summarizes the molecular rationale, targeted therapy evidence, and integration of genotyping into embolization workflows to enable combined treatment strategies.Level of Evidence: No level of evidence assigned (Review Article).

articles.title: Low latency and generalizable dynamic MRI via L+S alternating gradient descent and minimization.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dynamic MRI reconstruction often requires accurate, fast, and low-latency algorithms that generalize across multiple applications, sampling schemes, and rates, without problem-specific parameter tuning. Existing methods either lack generalizability or require extensive parameter adjustment. PURPOSE: To develop generalizable, low-latency MRI reconstruction algorithms based on low-rank (LR) and low-rank + sparse (L+S) models that are accurate, fast, and require minimal parameter tuning across diverse dynamic MRI settings. METHODS: We propose a novel Alternating Gradient Descent and Minimization (AltGDmin) approach for L+S matrix recovery from column-wise undersampled measurements, and extend it to a 3-level hierarchical L+S model for dynamic MRI. A few-shot (FS) learning modification (AGM-L+S-FS) is introduced to enable near low-latency reconstruction with per-frame processing time comparable to or faster than scan time. A simpler LR-only variant is also evaluated. RESULTS: The proposed algorithms were validated on 6 prospective and 12 retrospective dynamic MRI datasets, covering cardiac, speech, and abdominal applications, with Cartesian, pseudo-radial, radial, and spiral sampling schemes. Experiments demonstrate accurate reconstruction, generalizability across datasets and sampling rates, and low-latency performance. Detailed comparisons with state-of-the-art LR, L+S, low-latency, and unsupervised deep learning methods show superior or comparable performance. CONCLUSIONS: Our AGM-L+S-FS approach provide generalizable, fast, and low-latency MRI reconstruction across multiple dynamic MRI applications and sampling schemes, without the need for problem-specific parameter tuning.

articles.title: From Free Text to Research-Ready Data: A Reproducible, Reverse-Audited Pipeline for Structuring Breast Mammography Reports.
articles.abstract: Exported PDF mammography and pathology reports contain rich phenotypic and molecular information, yet they remain underused for research because converting them into research-ready variables is labor-intensive and error-prone. We developed a rule-based pipeline (PyMuPDF text extraction with section-aware regular expressions) that structured 615 source PDF reports into a verified 299 patient cohort (mean age 52.4 years; 290 female, sex not recorded in 9) with molecular subtype available for 286. An independent, deterministic reverse audit re-extracted every field from the source PDFs and compared it with the structured table across four validation layers, observing no discrepancies and confirming internal reproducibility rather than absolute accuracy. As a secondary, hypothesis-generating analysis, we used LASSO logistic regression under nested cross-validation (preprocessing and regularization tuned within training folds) to test whether report-level descriptors predict tumor biology. Predictive performance was weak throughout: HER2-positive versus HER2-negative attained the highest out-of-fold AUC 0.614 (95% CI 0.526-0.710), the only endpoint whose interval excluded chance, whereas triple-negative (0.511), four-class subtype (macro-AUC 0.519), and axillary node metastasis (0.455) were at or below chance. Incremental value benchmarks showed no gain over age or BI-RADS alone, and calibration and decision curve analysis indicated no clinically meaningful net benefit. These exploratory findings are consistent with evidence that pixel-level radiomics is more informative than report text; finer-grained NLP- or LLM-derived features remain unexplored. Under compatible report templates, the pipeline yields a reproducible, auditable structured breast cohort from text-exportable PDFs, motivating image-based radiomics as a reusable asset for multicenter research.

articles.title: Multi-Level Cancer Classification with FlexiFocusNet Using a Novel Nigerian Computed Tomography Imaging Dataset and Standard Histopathology Data.
articles.abstract: Reliable and generalisable artificial intelligence-based cancer image analysis remains challenging because of data scarcity, population bias, and the need to capture both local morphological details and long-range contextual dependencies. Many existing deep learning approaches rely on single-scale feature extraction or isolated attention mechanisms, potentially limiting their representation of multi-level spatial and channel information across imaging tasks. To address these challenges, we introduce FlexiFocusNet, an engineering-driven deep learning framework for multi-level cancer classification across heterogeneous medical imaging modalities. The architecture integrates hierarchical feature extraction, multi-scale attention fusion, transformer-style self-attention, and feature refinement to combine fine-grained local features with global contextual information. FlexiFocusNet was evaluated on a newly curated Nigerian computed tomography (CT) dataset for binary and three-class cancer classification and on a standard five-class histopathology dataset to examine its performance across imaging modalities. For binary CT classification, the model achieved 99.30 ± 0.49% accuracy, 99.62 ± 0.43% balanced accuracy, and an AUC of 1.000 under five-fold cross-validation, with 98.04% accuracy, 98.09% balanced accuracy, and an AUC of 0.999 on the independent test set. For three-class CT classification, it achieved 98.36 ± 1.05% validation accuracy and 98.01 ± 1.12% balanced accuracy, with 98.83% test accuracy, 98.52% balanced accuracy, and an AUC of 0.996. On five-class histopathology data, FlexiFocusNet achieved 99.92 ± 0.05% validation accuracy and 99.89 ± 0.06% balanced accuracy, followed by 100% test accuracy and an AUC of 1.000. The consistently high performance across the evaluated tasks indicates effective feature learning across different classification settings and imaging modalities. The study also contributes an underrepresented Nigerian CT dataset, subject to applicable institutional data-sharing requirements, providing an additional resource for research on cancer image analysis and geographically diverse medical artificial intelligence.

articles.title: UNICAL: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Learning with MRI-Derived Synthetic Amyloid PET for Alzheimer's Disease Classification.
articles.abstract: Limited availability of amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) motivates imaging-informatics methods that derive complementary molecular-imaging representations from routinely acquired magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). We developed UNICAL, an uncertainty-aware multimodal framework for Alzheimer's disease-spectrum versus cognitively normal classification that combines a self-supervised three-dimensional MRI encoder, Contourlet Wavelet Stationary Radiomics (CoWS-Rad) engineered MRI features, and MRI-derived synthetic 18F-florbetapir (AV45) PET. CoCoLIT generated four stochastic PET realizations per MRI; their mean and voxelwise variance were used for uncertainty gating before probability-anchored transformer fusion. Synthetic PET was validated in 228 paired OASIS-3 MRI-AV45 examinations, achieving a mean per-examination voxelwise Pearson correlation of r = 0.864 and strong cortical-composite SUVR agreement with acquired PET (Pearson r = 0.954). In the OASIS-3 development cohort (813 sessions from 811 participants), participant-grouped five-fold cross-validation repeated across 20 seeds yielded AUROC 0.868 and expected calibration error (ECE) 0.061. The OASIS-3 development endpoint used the manuscript's AD-spectrum reference standard, whereas ADNI3 used AD-versus-CN research-group labels, providing cross-dataset evaluation on a related but non-identical prediction endpoint. Without retraining, feature refitting, threshold optimization, or recalibration, the frozen framework was evaluated in an independent matched ADNI3 cohort of 261 participants (87 AD, 174 CN), achieving AUROC 0.836 (95% CI 0.791-0.876). ECE increased to 0.089 under external transfer, indicating that calibration was more sensitive to domain shift than rank discrimination. Ablation analysis and K-sample sensitivity supported the contributions of uncertainty gating, adaptive weighting, modality dropout, residual correction, and the K = 4 synthesis configuration. UNICAL therefore provides an uncertainty-aware MRI-derived multimodal representation for AD-spectrum classification that retains substantial cross-dataset discrimination while remaining distinct from acquired molecular imaging and not replacing amyloid PET as a clinical biomarker.

articles.title: Improving Coronary Artery Stenosis Segmentation Performance of YOLO Models Through a Dataset Expansion Strategy Based on Local Focused Augmentation.
articles.abstract: To address the problems of the small size of coronary artery stenosis regions, strong background interference, and limited high-quality annotated data in X-ray coronary angiography images, a dataset expansion strategy based on local focused augmentation is proposed. The method uses existing annotations of stenotic regions to crop local images centered on the lesion regions and adds them to the original training set, thereby increasing the proportion of lesion regions in the training samples without requiring additional manual annotation. Experiments were conducted using the YOLOv8 and YOLO11 model series, and the applicability of the proposed method was evaluated under different learning rates and batch sizes. The results show that local focused augmentation improves the F1 score under most parameter settings. Further validation on the public ARCADE dataset showed that the precision, recall, and F1 scores of YOLOv8m-seg, YOLOv9c-seg, YOLOv11m-seg, and YOLO26m-seg were all improved, with the F1 score of YOLOv8m-seg increasing from 0.3868 to 0.4045. The proposed method can enhance the learning of local features of coronary artery stenosis and improve the segmentation performance of small stenotic regions without modifying the network architecture.

articles.title: Fast Multiparametric ASL MRI via Multi-Dimensional Acceleration and Subspace Reconstruction.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Multi-post-labeling delays (PLDs) multi-echo times (TEs) arterial spin labeling (ASL) MRI enables simultaneous quantification of cerebral blood flow (CBF), arterial transit time (ATT), and blood-brain barrier (BBB) water exchange, but requires long scan times due to the combination of multi-TEs, PLDs, and repeated control-label acquisitions. A five-dimensional (5D) acquisition and reconstruction framework was developed to enable accelerated multi-parametric ASL. METHODS: A coordinated undersampling strategy was designed across in-plane k-space, through-plane k-space, TE, and control-label measurement dimensions, achieving a combined acceleration factor of approximately 28. Reconstruction was performed using a Kronecker-structured subspace model that exploited low-rank correlations along the TE and control-label dimensions. Sparsity regularization was applied in the subspace coefficient domain, and temporal bases were estimated from a single fully sampled middle slice. The framework was evaluated using in vivo echo-time-resolved ASL (TASL) datasets from eight subjects. RESULTS: The proposed reconstruction outperformed a matched compressed sensing (CS) reconstruction across all echo times, yielding higher structural similarity index measure (SSIM) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), with the largest improvements observed under severe undersampling (R≈28) and at late echo times. Higher-fidelity CBF, ATT, BBB, and intravascular transit time (ITT) maps were obtained, with the greatest gains observed for BBB and ITT. Test-retest reliability, assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), remained comparable to fully sampled reference data. CONCLUSION: Coordinated multi-dimensional undersampling combined with Kronecker subspace reconstruction enables highly accelerated multi-parametric ASL while preserving image quality, quantitative parameter estimation, and test-retest reliability, supporting clinically feasible acquisition times.

articles.title: A Multicenter Ultrasound Habitat Radiomics Framework For Diagnosing Tuberculous Lymphadenitis And Stratifying Rifampicin Resistance Risk.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate an ultrasound-based habitat radiomics framework for the hierarchical differentiation of tuberculous lymphadenitis (TBLN) from non-tuberculous lymphadenopathy, and to noninvasively predict rifampicin resistance risk using an independently collected cohort of patients with confirmed TBLN. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, 618 patients with superficial lymphadenopathy who underwent ultrasound examination between January 2022 and December 2025 at four tertiary hospitals were included. Among them, 530 patients with definitive diagnoses were used for diagnostic differentiation and were divided into a model-development (training) cohort and an external validation cohort, while 236 patients with confirmed tuberculous lymphadenitis (TBLN) were included for rifampicin resistance risk assessment. Based on standardized B-mode ultrasound images, we developed a 2-stage ultrasound habitat radiomics framework that first differentiated tuberculous from non-tuberculous lymph nodes. Rifampicin resistance risk was assessed within the confirmed TBLN cohort using nested cross-validated out-of-fold predictions. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA), and model interpretability was assessed using SHAP-based methods. RESULTS: For differentiating tuberculous from non-tuberculous lymph nodes, the habitat-based model demonstrated strong discriminative performance, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.83 in the training cohort and maintaining consistent performance in the external test cohort. Using nested cross-validated out-of-fold predictions within the confirmed TBLN cohort, the habitat-based model achieved an AUC of 0.83 for predicting rifampicin resistance, outperforming conventional radiomics and demonstrating superior clinical net benefit. Spatial visualization revealed that high-risk habitats were localized to specific intralesional regions, underscoring the importance of spatial heterogeneity in both disease diagnosis and drug resistance assessment. CONCLUSION: Ultrasound-based habitat radiomics provides an interpretable and clinically applicable framework for hierarchical diagnosis of tuberculous lymphadenitis and for rifampicin resistance risk assessment in an independent patient cohort, supporting precision imaging-guided management of tuberculosis.

articles.title: Development and Multicenter Validation of a Hybrid Radiomics-Deep Learning Model for Risk Stratification of O-RADS 4 Adnexal Masses.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate an artificial intelligence-driven hybrid model integrating ultrasound radiomics, deep learning (DL) signatures, and clinical predictors for differentiating benign from borderline/malignant Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System (O-RADS) 4 adnexal masses, and to evaluate its utility as a radiologist decision-support tool. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter study retrospectively enrolled 653 patients from four centers (521 from Center A [training, n = 405; internal validation, n = 116]; 132 from Centers B-D [external validation]), and prospectively enrolled 126 patients from Center A. Pathological results served as the gold standard. Radiomics features were extracted to generate a Rad-score using machine learning classifiers. A transfer learning-based DL model using convolutional neural networks produced a DL-score. A hybrid model integrating Rad-score, DL-score, and clinical predictors was constructed. Diagnostic performance of models was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). In the prospective validation set, six radiologists interpreted cases with and without hybrid model assistance. Diagnostic differences were assessed using McNemar's χ² test, and inter-reader agreement by Cohen's kappa. RESULTS: The hybrid model demonstrated good performance with AUCs of 0.88 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.82-0.93) and 0.86 (95% CI: 0.78-0.92) in the prospective and external validation sets. Model assistance significantly improved accuracy and specificity across all readers (p < 0.05), with inter-reader agreement improving from kappa 0.49 to 0.73. The model stratified lesions into low-risk (4a) and high-risk (4b) subcategories with consistently distinct malignancy rates across all datasets (4a: 4.5%-16.1%; 4b: 75.4%-97.1%). CONCLUSION: The hybrid model demonstrated good performance for risk stratification of O-RADS 4 adnexal masses and improved radiologist performance across experience levels.

articles.title: Monitoring Remyelination and Its Association With Disability Improvement in Multiple Sclerosis Using APART-QSM: A Longitudinal Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Conventional MRI has limited specificity for myelin quantification. IterAtive magnetic suscePtibility sources sepARaTion quantitative susceptibility mapping (APART-QSM) quantifies myelin-sensitive (χdia) and iron-sensitive (χpara) susceptibility components, but its value for longitudinal assessment of remyelination in multiple sclerosis (MS) remains unclear. PURPOSE: To characterize longitudinal χdia in MS and assess its associations with clinical characteristics. STUDY TYPE: Prospective, longitudinal. POPULATION: One hundred forty-five patients with MS and 65 healthy controls (HCs). FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3.0T; 3D T1-weighted, 3D FLAIR, 3D DIR, and multi-echo gradient-echo imaging sequences. ASSESSMENT: APART-QSM generated χdia and χpara maps, with susceptibility quantified in lesions and non-lesional regions, and the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) assessed at baseline and follow-up. STATISTICAL TESTS: Chi-square, Mann-Whitney U, Wilcoxon signed-rank, Friedman tests, linear mixed-effects models, linear and nonlinear regression. A p value < 0.05 was considered significant. RESULTS: One hundred one patients with MS and 20 HCs completed follow-up after a median (IQR) interval of 1.0 (0.8) and 1.25 (0.2) years, respectively. At baseline, white matter lesions (WMLs) exhibited lower χdia (0.0131 [IQR 0.0087] ppm) and higher χpara (0.0058 [IQR 0.0049] ppm) than corresponding normal-appearing white matter (NAWM) (0.0191 [0.0088] ppm; 0.0036 [0.0038] ppm; both p < 0.001). Over 1 year, χdia in WMLs increased (0.0122 [IQR 0.0069] vs. 0.0152 [IQR 0.0065] ppm, p < 0.001), particularly in ofatumumab-treated patients (0.0114 [IQR 0.0085] vs. 0.0158 [IQR 0.0081] ppm, p < 0.001). Greater increases in χdia were significantly associated with female sex, ofatumumab treatment, relapsing-remitting phenotype, and EDSS improvement (all Bonferroni correction p < 0.01). Δχdia showed a nonlinear decline with increasing disease duration (effective degrees of freedom (edf) = 1.83, p = 0.002). CONCLUSION: APART-QSM may enable longitudinal monitoring of remyelination-related changes in MS, with declining Δχdia over disease duration potentially informing individualized treatment strategies. STAGE OF TECHNICAL EFFICACY: 2.

articles.title: Spectral-spatial Modeling of Neural Couplings in Functional Connectivity of Motor Networks.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Functional neural connectivity reflects coordinated interactions within brain networks in both health and disease. Phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) is widely used for this purpose, but its pairwise formulations overlook spatially distributed, spectrally correlated structures in neural activity that arises from complex brain circuits. NEW METHOD: We developed a spectral-spatial generalized linear model (SS-GLM) to characterize the high-frequency response as the integrated outcome of multiple low-frequency phase sources across channels and frequencies. Our method also utilizes a regularization strategy to mitigate predictor collinearity and spurious effects for stable attribution of network-level coupling estimates. RESULTS: Validation was performed using both synthetic data and human motor network recordings from 25 patients with Parkinson's disease undergoing deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery. In synthetic analyses, SS-GLM accurately recovered ground-truth coupling configurations under multiple plausible scenarios. In real data, the framework revealed coherent cortico-subthalamic coupling patterns across distinct motor tasks that aligned with clinically effective DBS contacts and their anatomical organization. COMPARISON WITH EXISTING METHODS: Conventional pairwise PAC metrics, such as the modulation index and GLM assess interactions in isolation. In contrast, SS-GLM jointly models distributed predictors and yields spatially localized, spectrally specific coupling estimates that also achieve stronger correspondence with clinical stimulation outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: This work offers a principled and extensible framework for advancing functional connectivity analyses, with improved interpretability of network-level interactions, enhanced robustness to confounds, and broad potential for future applications in systems neuroscience and neuro-engineering research.

articles.title: Distinct neural patterns of valence and arousal in the developing brain: A representational similarity analysis of MEG.
articles.abstract: How children and adolescents encode the affective meaning of visual stimuli remains poorly understood. A key reason is that valence and arousal are inherently correlated across affective stimuli and thus confounded in the categorical contrasts mostly used in emotion research. Here, in a secondary analysis of a previously collected MEG dataset, we dissociate the contributions of valence and arousal in emotional processing by applying partial representational similarity analysis (RSA) to magnetoencephalography (MEG) data from 57 typically developing children and adolescents (5 - 18 years old) viewing pictures from the Nencki Affective Picture System. Source-localized responses were first estimated on a volumetric grid, after which we tested, across regions and time windows, whether similarity in neural activity patterns tracked similarity in valence or arousal ratings while controlling for their shared variance. Valence emerged as the primary organizing dimension of neural representations in this sample, with effects detectable in frontotemporal and salience regions within the first 100 ms and sustained over time in the lateral prefrontal cortex. These responses formed a distributed representational network that progressively engaged higher-order evaluative regions. In contrast, arousal contributed transiently through a distinct network that only intermittently overlapped with valence-related activity. Together, these findings indicate that valence predominantly structures affective representations in this pediatric sample, whereas arousal exerts a weaker and more limited influence. This work provides an initial characterization of affective representational structure in this sample of children and adolescents, that if replicated, may inform future reference framework for identifying deviations associated with conditions such as autism spectrum disorder.

articles.title: Characterization of the hemodynamic response function in default mode network subregions for task-evoked negative BOLD responses.
articles.abstract: While the hemodynamic response function (HRF) of the positive blood oxygenated level dependent (BOLD) signal is well characterized in the functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) field, studies investigating the shape and properties of the negative BOLD HRF, often observed in the default mode network (DMN) regions, are rare. In this study, we first investigated whether the duration-dependent scaling assumption for linear systems theory holds for the task-evoked negative BOLD response (NBR). Then, we obtained the shape of the HRF from each region of the DMN, using an in-house developed robust iterative deconvolution technique. Our results demonstrated that each region of the DMN represented a unique HRF, which was not only substantially different from the HRF of the positive BOLD signal, but also different from the HRF extracted from the other DMN regions. We assessed the consistency and variability of regional HRF estimates across six task-fMRI datasets collected within the same study cohort. When comparing the HRF across DMN sub-regions and across tasks, our results demonstrated a generally higher inter-regional variability compared to inter-task variability. Furthermore, our performance correlation analysis illustrated that the HRFs in the DMN sub-regions extracted by our iterative FIR method were not significantly related to the task performance. Altogether, we demonstrated NBR scales linearly with task duration, introduced a robust HRF extraction approach to obtain a distinct HRF for each DMN sub-regions, which were different from the HRF of the positive BOLD signal. The results suggest there is possibility that each node of the DMN might have different underlying neural and/or vascular mechanisms that evokes different NBR-HRF.

articles.title: Visuospatial attention modulates audiovisual temporal perception: Context-dependent associations between prestimulus alpha lateralization and perceptual reports.
articles.abstract: Audiovisual temporal perception depends on the timing of sensory events and on preparatory attention. We examined how visuospatial cueing affects explicit synchrony judgments and sound-induced flash illusions, and how prestimulus EEG relates to these perceptual reports. In Experiment 1 (N = 39), participants judged beep-flash synchrony across auditory- and visual-leading stimulus onset asynchronies (SOAs). In Experiment 2 (N = 36), they reported flashes in fusion and fission conditions across SOAs and corresponding references. Experiment 1 showed a Cue validity × SOA interaction, with more synchrony reports on valid trials at -100 and +50 ms. Cueing shifted the point of subjective simultaneity among 21 participants with reliable fits. Trial-level posterior alpha lateralization was associated with synchrony reports as a function of Cue validity. In Experiment 2, valid cues reduced raw fusion reports at -100, -50, and +100 ms. A Cue validity × SOA interaction persisted for reference-adjusted fusion scores, whereas neither raw nor adjusted fission showed a corresponding interaction. The association between reference-adjusted alpha lateralization and fusion reports varied with Cue validity and SOA, although a direct comparison with the visual reference did not establish an illusion-specific association. These EEG-behavior associations were stable after accounting for temporal progression, preceding trials, cue side, and an ocular-sensitive EEG proxy. Together, the findings indicate timing- and context-dependent effects of visuospatial attention on audiovisual temporal perception and identify preparatory posterior alpha lateralization as a correlate of subsequent reports.

articles.title: One-Year Outcomes and Additive Risk of Restenosis After Rotational Atherectomy Plus Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty for Calcified Femoropopliteal Lesions in a Japanese Population.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate 1-year clinical outcomes and identify predictors of restenosis after rotational atherectomy and drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty for calcified femoropopliteal lesions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, single-arm study included 241 patients (178 men [73.9%] and 63 women [26.1%]) treated with JETSTREAM atherectomy and DCB angioplasty at eight Japanese centers. Mean lesion length was 16.5 cm, 28.6% were chronic total occlusions, and 91.3% had PACSS grade 3/4 calcification. Primary patency was freedom from restenosis (duplex ultrasonography-derived peak systolic velocity ratio >2.4 or occlusion) and clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR). At 1 year, 220 patients (91.3%) completed follow-up. RESULTS: One-year primary patency and freedom from CD-TLR were 85.5% and 91.3%, respectively. Exploratory multivariable analysis identified hemodialysis (HR 2.70, 95% CI 1.27-5.77, P = 0.01), chronic total occlusion (HR 2.85, 95% CI 1.39-5.83, P < 0.01), prior endovascular therapy (HR 5.08, 95% CI 2.48-10.4, P < 0.01), and popliteal artery involvement (HR 3.62, 95% CI 1.76-7.46, P < 0.01) as independently associated with patency loss. Patency declined from 94.1% with ≤1 factor to 38.1% with ≥3 factors. Neither severe nor nodular calcifications were associated with patency loss. Among restenotic lesions, 54.8% were occlusive, and shorter than baseline lesions. Angiographic distal embolization occurred in 37.8% and remained unresolved in 3.3%. CONCLUSION: One-year primary patency was 85.5%. Exploratory analyses suggested an additive association between clinical and anatomical factors and loss of patency. These findings require confirmation given the single-arm design and limited number of patency-loss events.

articles.title: "CLEAN-UP AV": A composite interventional technique for treating Perianastomotic Arteriovenous Fistula dysfunction with balloon angioplasty: A 10-year outcome analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate long-term outcomes of a standardized interventional protocol, CLEAN-UP AV, for managing perianastomotic segment (PAS) stenosis or occlusion in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs). METHODS: This retrospective single center focused PAS angioplasty cohort from a tertiary referral practice analyzed 553 AVF angioplasties performed in 457 patients over 10 years. The CLEAN-UP AV strategy incorporates: advanced Crossing techniques, Lumen gain with appropriate balloons, treatment of the Entire circuit, Anastomotic dilation via optimal Access, No residual waist, procedural Ultrasound guidance, and postprocedural Pharmacotherapy. Angioplasty was performed using either U or V configuration technique: U angioplasty referring to angioplasty performed from artery to vein or from vein to artery and V angioplasty referring to sequential balloon angioplasty of the arterial and venous segments, including the anastomosis. Technical and clinical success, primary and secondary patency, adverse events, and predictors of patency loss were assessed. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 94.4% of procedures. Kaplan-Meier estimated 1 to 5 year primary and secondary patency rates in technically successful cases were 78%, 70%, 62%, 61%, and 58% and 89%, 84%, 83%, 80%, and 80%, respectively. On multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis, radiocephalic fistula configuration was an independent predictor of superior primary and secondary patency while hypothyroidism and high-pressure balloon requirement were independently associated with inferior primary patency. Major adverse event rate was 1.6%. CONCLUSION: In this single-center retrospective cohort, angioplasty performed using the CLEAN-UP AV approach was associated with high technical success and favorable long-term primary and secondary patency for perianastomotic AVF dysfunction.

articles.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Hemodialysis Arteriovenous Fistula Dysfunction Using 2D-Ultrasound, Elastography, and Vector Flow Imaging.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic value of multimodal ultrasound-including 2D-ultrasound, sound touch elastography (STE), and vector flow imaging (VFI)-for the identification of functional and biomechanical abnormalities indicative of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis or occlusion in hemodialysis patients. METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 37 hemodialysis patients with AVFs, divided into normal (n = 20) and dysfunction (n = 17) groups based on digital subtraction angiography (DSA) or clinical/ultrasound criteria. For the dysfunction group, AVF stenosis was defined as >50% luminal diameter reduction on DSA, and occlusion as complete absence of flow. For the normal group, dysfunction was excluded by clinical examination (thrill/bruit) and normal duplex parameters. All patients underwent 2D-ultrasound, STE, and VFI examinations. Key parameters measured included vessel diameter, elasticity (kPa), blood flow velocities, turbulence index, and wall shear stress (WSS). Statistical comparisons were made between groups. RESULTS: No significant differences were found in vessel diameter or intima status between groups. However, the stenosis/occlusion group exhibited significantly lower mean blood flow, peak systolic/end-diastolic velocities, and WSS, along with higher resistance index and vessel wall stiffness (STE-mean: 30.35 ± 11.65 vs. 20.7 ± 7.52 kPa, p < 0.01). VFI revealed reduced blood flow velocity, turbulence, and WSS in dysfunctional AVFs (all p < 0.01). CONCLUSION: Multimodal ultrasound integrating 2D-ultrasound, STE, and VFI provides a comprehensive assessment of AVF structure and function, detecting functional and biomechanical abnormalities associated with AVF stenosis or occlusion.

articles.title: Region-specific associations between dual-Layer spectral detector CT-derived carotid plaque parameters and white matter hyperintensity burden in patients with carotid atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) exhibit region-specific characteristics. Whether dual-layer spectral detector CT (DLSCT)-derived plaque parameters associate with WMH burden region-specifically remains unclear. METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled 213 patients with carotid atherosclerotic plaques who underwent carotid CTA and brain MRI within 30 days. Seven DLSCT parameters were measured; WMH was segmented into juxtaventricular, periventricular, deep, and juxtacortical subregions. Multivariable linear regression assessed associations with total WMH burden (FDR correction). Nested models evaluated incremental value. Linear mixed-effects models with region-by-parameter interactions assessed region-specific associations. RESULTS: In the primary model (Model 2), Z-Zeff was significantly negatively associated with total WMH burden (β = -0.205, 95 % CI: -0.299 ∼ -0.111, FDR-q < 0.001). Adding Z-Zeff to the clinical model significantly increased explained variance (ΔR2 = 0.070, p < 0.001, ΔAIC = -15.09), whereas conventional CTA parameters did not (ΔR2 = 0.001, p = 0.938). Significant region interactions were observed for Z-Zeff, age, and LDL-C. Z-Zeff was negatively associated with all subregions, strongest in periventricular (β = -0.254) and deep (β = -0.172) WMH. Age was most strongly associated with periventricular WMH (β = 0.436). LDL-C and diabetes were associated only with periventricular WMH (β = -0.111 and -0.221, respectively). CONCLUSION: DLSCT-derived Z-Zeff was independently associated with WMH burden in a region-specific manner, with the strongest associations in periventricular and deep white matter, and provided incremental value beyond clinical and conventional CTA parameters. These findings support Z-Zeff as a potential imaging biomarker linking carotid plaque composition to regional cerebral small vessel disease.

articles.title: Measuring prostate cancer lesion size on serial MRI during active surveillance: A multi-centre observational study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess the intra- and inter-reader reliability of measurements of prostate cancer (PCa) lesions on serial multiparametric MRI scans, and to assess how lesion characteristics and measurement methods influence measurements over time in an international two-centre setting. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty patients with low- or intermediate-risk PCa undergoing active surveillance were included. A total of three MRI scans were evaluated for each patient: one baseline and two serial follow-up scans. Five consultant radiologists from two institutions independently measured the size of the index lesion at each time point by four methods: maximum diameter, biaxial diameters, ellipsoid volume, and planimetry. Measurements were repeated after a four-week 'wash-out' period. Variability was assessed using strip plots and Bland-Altman analysis. RESULTS: Graphical presentation of inter-reader and intra-reader reliability enabled examination of variability between methods, readers and reads. Variability increased with lesion size and was greatest for lesions with poorly defined margins. Smaller, well-delineated lesions demonstrated greater consistency over time and across readers. Estimates of percentage change showed greater variability than absolute measurements, particularly for volumetric methods. Small differences in the underlying absolute measurements are amplified when expressed relative to baseline values. CONCLUSION: Serial MRI assessment of PCa lesion size is subject to substantial variability, particularly for larger lesions and lesions with indistinct boundaries. The benefits of consistent readers and measurement methods warrant further confirmation in larger prospective studies to support reliable clinical decision-making during active surveillance.

articles.title: A cascade deep learning network for simultaneous prediction of dose and linear energy transfer in proton therapy of prostate cancer.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Prediction of dose-averaged linear energy transfer (LETd) may facilitate LET-aware evaluation of proton therapy plans. This study developed a cascade deep learning framework for simultaneous three-dimensional prediction of dose and LETd distributions for conventional dose-based optimization (DoseOpt) and LETd-incorporated optimization (LETOpt) in prostate intensity-modulated proton therapy. APPROACH: A total of 150 patients with prostate cancer were included, each with DoseOpt and LETOpt plans. Planning CT images and anatomical structure masks were used as inputs. The cascade network transferred an intermediate latent representation from the dose prediction pathway to the LETd prediction pathway. Stepwise, multitask, and anatomy-only LETd (only-LET) networks served as comparators. Model performance was evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. MAIN RESULTS: All dose-predicting models showed high spatial agreement, with cascade Dice similarity coefficients of approximately 0.93, 0.96, and 0.95 for the 50%, 75%, and 95% prescription isodose volumes. No significant differences in structure-specific dose errors remained after false discovery rate correction. The cascade model achieved the lowest global LETd MAE for DoseOpt and LETOpt, 0.108 ± 0.025 and 0.111 ± 0.025 keV/μm, respectively, significantly lower than those of the multitask, stepwise, and only-LET models. Structure-specific LETd performance was endpoint dependent, with favorable cascade performance for several CTV and organ-at-risk endpoints. LETOpt primarily redistributed LETd while largely preserving dose, and the cascade model reproduced the principal plan-specific changes, including reductions in rectal and rectal-wall LETd. Mean inference time was 0.505 ± 0.020 s per patient. SIGNIFICANCE: The proposed framework enables rapid simultaneous prediction of dose and LETd for predefined planning strategies from patient anatomy without requiring a precomputed dose distribution, supporting LET-aware plan comparison and providing a basis for future LETd-guided biological optimization.

articles.title: Short-time deep-inspiratory breath-hold pulmonary perfusion SPECT/CT in interstitial pneumonia: a vascular dimension that stratifies risk independently of the GAP score.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Risk in interstitial pneumonia (IP) is assessed routinely by the Gender-Age-Physiology (GAP) score from pulmonary function and the tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) on echocardiography. This study evaluated whether the percent perfusion defect (%PPD) on short-time deep-inspiratory breath-hold (STDIBH) pulmonary perfusion SPECT/CT carries prognostic information that neither captures. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ninety-one consecutive patients with IP who underwent STDIBH perfusion SPECT/CT between 2012 and 2023 were analyzed retrospectively. The primary endpoint was a composite major adverse event (MAE) of all-cause death, acute exacerbation of IP, respiratory-failure hospitalization, and initiation of home oxygen therapy. Association was assessed by Cox regression and discrimination by censoring-weighted time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. RESULTS: MAE occurred in 66 of 91 patients (72.5%) over a median follow-up of 45.9 months. %PPD was associated with MAE after adjustment for the GAP score and antifibrotic therapy (adjusted hazard ratio 1.2304 per 10 percentage points, 95% CI 1.0568-1.4325; P = 0.008), and, in exploratory analyses, for TRPG and the GAP score together (1.2058, 1.0314-1.4096; P = 0.019). It showed no significant correlation with TRPG (Spearman r = 0.164; P = 0.140). Time-dependent discrimination did not differ significantly between %PPD and the GAP score at 6, 12, and 24 months, and adding %PPD to the GAP score changed the Harrell C-index from 0.692 to 0.719 (difference 0.027, 95% CI - 0.009 to 0.107). %PPD was obtained in all 91 patients and the GAP score in 68 (74.7%). CONCLUSION: In IP, %PPD measures a dimension of risk that the GAP score does not capture, and exploratory analyses suggest that echocardiography does not capture it either. %PPD is obtainable when the GAP score is not. Its discrimination did not differ significantly from that of the GAP score, and adding it to the GAP score did not significantly improve discrimination.

articles.title: A Combined Clinical, Spectral CT, and Intratumoral Radiomics Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Gastric Adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: Lymph node metastasis (LNM) significantly impacts gastric adenocarcinoma (GA) treatment and prognosis. Preoperative LNM prediction is challenging, necessitating accurate models to assist clinical decisions. We aim to establish and validate a model integrating multiparameter dual-layer detector spectral CT (DLCT) imaging features and radiomics scores from venous phase images for preoperative LNM prediction in GA patients. We retrospectively analyzed clinical, pathological, and imaging data from 275 GA patients with preoperative DLCT scans, categorized into LNM-positive (173 cases) and LNM-negative (102 cases) groups. Intra- and peritumoral DLCT metrics, including iodine concentration (IC), normalized IC (nIC), and effective atomic number (Zeff), were assessed. Independent risk factors were identified via logistic regression. Radiomics features were extracted from venous phase DLCT images, with the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) used for radiomics feature selection. A combined model incorporating clinical data, DLCT metrics, and radiomics scores was constructed and evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Intratumoral venous phase nIC and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA 19-9) were independent risk factors, forming a conventional model. Five radiomics features were selected for a radiomics model. The combined (CA 19-9 + venous phase + radiomics scores) model showed superior predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.91 (training set) and 0.83 (validation set). Calibration curves indicated a good fit, and DCA demonstrated a favorable net benefit across relevant threshold probabilities for the combined model. The combined model, which integrates clinical information with both multiparameter DLCT features and radiomics scores, offers a clinically valuable tool for preoperative LNM prediction in GA patients.

articles.title: TACMRN: Triple-Attention Contrastive Memory Retrieval Network for Brain CT Report Generation.
articles.abstract: Brain CT report generation aims to automatically produce diagnostic reports from 3D brain volumes, reducing radiologists' workload and enhancing clinical decision-making. Despite recent advances, existing methods often struggle to effectively capture comprehensive spatiotemporal features from 3D brain CT data and fail to leverage crucial medical knowledge accumulated from prior cases. To address these challenges, we propose a novel triple-attention contrastive memory retrieval network (TACMRN) that mimics the cognitive workflow of experienced radiologists. Specifically, triple-attention enhancement (TAE) module decomposes the 3D attention into spatial position, spatial channel, and temporal channel branches to efficiently extract fine-grained spatiotemporal features. Multiscale contrastive fusion (MCF) module captures differential features between abnormal and normal images across multiple scales, enhancing lesion perception. Moreover, memory retrieval enhancement (MRE) module introduces learnable memory slots to store and retrieve general medical knowledge, simulating radiologists' reliance on prior experience. Extensive experiments were conducted on the public CTRG-Brain dataset. On CTRG-Brain, the proposed method achieved 0.597 in BLEU-1, 0.503 in BLEU-2, 0.441 in BLEU-3, 0.391 in BLEU-4, 0.291 in METEOR, and 0.540 in ROUGE-L, outperforming all competing methods and achieving state-of-the-art performance, and ablation study validated the effectiveness of each proposed component. The proposed TACMRN provides an effective solution for automated brain CT report generation. By jointly leveraging TAE, MCF and MRE modules, the method substantially captures fine-grained lesion features and improves diagnostic accuracy and reporting consistency. This work offers practical value for the automated radiology report generation, potentially reducing radiologists' workload and accelerating the doctor's diagnosis process.

articles.title: Incremental Prognostic Value of Ascending Aortic Perivascular Adipose Tissue Radiomics for Short-Term Mortality After Surgical Repair of Acute Type A Aortic Dissection.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate whether radiomic features derived from ascending aortic perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) provide incremental prognostic value beyond conventional clinical predictors for predicting short-term mortality after surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD). In this retrospective multicenter study, 241 patients with ATAAD who underwent surgical repair were enrolled and divided into a training cohort (n = 180) and an external validation cohort (n = 61). Radiomic features were extracted from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) images of the ascending aortic PVAT extending from the sinotubular junction to the origin of the brachiocephalic trunk. The best-performing radiomics model was integrated with independent clinical predictors to develop a clinicoradiomics model. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, DeLong testing, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. Age, neutrophil count, creatinine level, and maximum ascending aortic diameter were identified as independent predictors of 3-month postoperative mortality. The random forest algorithm achieved the best radiomics performance. The clinicoradiomics model achieved superior discrimination, with AUCs of 0.935 and 0.855 in the training and external validation cohorts, respectively, significantly outperforming both the clinical model and the radiomics model (all P < 0.05). SHAP analysis identified multiple PVAT radiomic features among the most influential predictors. Ascending aortic PVAT radiomics provides complementary prognostic information beyond conventional clinical predictors for short-term mortality after surgical repair of ATAAD. A clinicoradiomics model integrating PVAT radiomics with clinical variables improves postoperative risk prediction and may facilitate individualized risk stratification.

articles.title: GPT-4o-assisted restructuring of emergency head-and-neck computed tomography angiography reports: evaluation of automated vs. manual processing strategies.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare perceived quality, perceived clinical interpretability, interrater agreement, and processing time of four reporting strategies for emergency head-and-neck CT angiography (CTA): automated processing (AP) reports, manually modified (MM) reports, GPT-4o-A reports (generated from findings section of MM reports), and GPT-4o-B reports (generated from findings and impression sections). METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, we evaluated 102 emergency head-and-neck CTA reports using subjective Likert-scale ratings of perceived report quality - no assessment of diagnostic accuracy or clinical outcomes was performed. Four report types per case were evaluated by three radiologists and three emergency physicians. Radiologists rated perceived accuracy, perceived completeness, and perceived text quality; emergency physicians rated understandability and perceived potential harm on 5-point Likert scales. Interrater agreement was evaluated using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC 2,1). Differences among report types were analyzed with Friedman test and Wilcoxon post-hoc tests with Holm correction. RESULTS: Radiologist agreement was high for perceived accuracy (ICC = 0.909), perceived completeness (0.927), and perceived text quality (0.875); whereas emergency physician agreement was moderate for understandability (0.662) and excellent for perceived potential harm (0.967). Report type significantly affected all outcomes (all P < 0.001). GPT-4o-B received the highest radiologist ratings for perceived accuracy, completeness, and text quality, all 5.0 (IQR, 5.0-5.0), whereas AP received the lowest ratings of 2.0 (1.0-2.0), 2.0 (1.0-2.0), and 3.0 (2.0-3.0), respectively. Among emergency physicians, understandability was highest for AP and GPT-4o-B, both 5.0 (4.0-5.0), while perceived potential harm was lowest for MM, 1.0 (1.0-1.0), and highest for AP, 3.0 (2.0-3.0). Processing time differed significantly (P < 0.001): AP 21.0 s (18.0-25.0), GPT-4o-A 271.5 s (198.0-336.0), MM 311.5 s (245.0-387.0), and GPT-4o-B 338.5 s (268.0-414.0). CONCLUSION: GPT-4o-B provided the best overall quality and high interpretability, with longer processing time. GPT-4o-A was more efficient but less comprehensive. Findings support GPT-4o as a human-in-the-loop tool to improve emergency reporting, not replace physician oversight.

articles.title: An immediate reperfusion sign might increase the likelihood of favourable outcomes in patients with intracranial atherosclerotic disease-related stroke who received stent-retriever-based thrombectomy.
articles.abstract: OBJECTS: To investigate the relationship between the presence of an "immediate reperfusion sign (IRS)" during retrievable stent-based thrombectomy and clinical outcomes in patients with large vessel-occluded acute ischaemic stroke related to intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) treated with stent retrievers. METHODS: Consecutive ICAD-LVO stroke patients who were treated with stent retrievers and whose imaging records were available for the assessment of the IRS were included. The sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values of the IRS for predicting favourable outcomes were calculated. Univariate analysis and partial correlation analysis were also performed. RESULTS: Eighty-two ICAD-LVO patients were identified from 421 endovascularly treated AIS patients from 2015 to 2024. Fifty-four of them were ultimately included in the analysis, and an IRS was observed in 41 of these patients (75.9%). Favourable outcomes were significantly more frequent in the IRS (+) group (51.2% versus 7.7%, p=0.005). The sensitivity of the IRS for predicting favourable outcomes was 95.5% (21/22), the specificity was 37.5% (12/32), the positive predictive value was 51.2% (21/41), and the negative predictive value (NPV) was 92.3% (12/13). Additionally, the presence of an IRS, as well as age, baseline NIHSS score and successful final reperfusion, was significantly different between the favourable and unfavourable groups. Partial correlation analysis revealed a moderate correlation (r=0.412; p=0.002) between the comprehensive reperfusion score (in which the presence of an IRS and successful final reperfusion was counted as 1 point) and favourable outcomes. CONCLUSION: In our respective cohort of patients, the presence of an IRS during stent-retriever-based thrombectomy appeared to indicate a higher rate of first-pass-effect and a 3-month favourable outcome in acute LVO stroke patients with ICAD.

articles.title: Double origin configurations of the posterior cerebral and posterior communicating arteries associated with anterior cerebral artery fenestration.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To report a rare combination of cerebral arterial variants involving both anterior and posterior circulations and to characterize their morphology and potential clinical implications. METHODS: A 57-year-old male underwent time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography (TOF-MRA) using a 1.5 Tesla system. Multiplanar and three-dimensional reconstructions were analyzed. RESULTS: In the anterior circulation, a 6.47 mm fenestration was identified at the A1-A2 junction of the left anterior cerebral artery (ACA). The posterior circulation revealed a duplicate origin of the left posterior cerebral artery (PCA) with a length of 1.54 mm and a duplicate origin of the left posterior communicating artery (PComA) with a length of 3.56 mm. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates a rare coexistence of ACA fenestration with complex variants of the posterior circulation. These findings likely represent developmental variations, such as incomplete fusion or persistence of primitive vascular channels, rather than definitive arterial duplication. Recognition of such configurations using high-quality multiplanar and three-dimensional imaging is essential for accurate diagnosis and safe neurovascular intervention.

articles.title: European Society of Neuroradiology (ESNR).
Preoperative risk stratification for anastomotic leakage after gastrectomy: a model based on dual‑energy CT extracellular volume fraction and sarcopenia.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a purely preoperative risk stratification model for anastomotic leakage (AL) after radical gastrectomy using clinical, dual-energy CT (DECT), and body composition variables available before surgery. METHODS: This retrospective study included 439 patients with gastric cancer who underwent radical gastrectomy. Preoperative clinical, DECT, and body composition data were collected. A domain-based predictor selection strategy was used, followed by Firth penalized logistic regression to account for the low event rate. Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples, with an additional full-pipeline bootstrap sensitivity analysis. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis (DCA), and risk stratification. RESULTS: AL occurred in 27 patients (6.15%). The final model included cardia tumor location (OR = 4.44), higher ECV (OR = 1.09 per 1%), and sarcopenia (OR = 3.66). The model showed good discrimination, with an apparent AUC of 0.853 and a bootstrap-corrected AUC of 0.843. Full-pipeline bootstrap sensitivity analysis yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.833. Calibration was acceptable, with a Brier score of 0.050, and DCA suggested potential net benefit. Observed AL rates increased stepwise across low-risk (< 3%), intermediate-risk (3%-10%), and high-risk (≥ 10%) groups: 1.23%, 5.13%, and 22.78%, respectively. The high-risk group comprised 18.0% of the cohort but accounted for 66.7% of all AL events. CONCLUSION: A concise model integrating tumor location, DECT-derived ECV, and sarcopenia showed favorable performance for preoperative AL risk stratification after gastrectomy. This internally validated model may help preoperative AL risk stratification, but multicenter external validation and impact analysis are required before implementation.

articles.title: Contrast-enhanced CT-based multimodal modeling for overall survival prediction after resection of retroperitoneal liposarcoma: a bicentric retrospective study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Postoperative risk estimation in retroperitoneal liposarcoma (RPLS) remains challenging because conventional clinicopathologic models capture only part of its biological heterogeneity. We aimed to develop and externally evaluate a postoperative prognostic model integrating preoperative CT features with postoperative clinicopathologic information to estimate overall survival (OS) after RPLS resection. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This bicentric retrospective study included 367 patients who underwent complete RPLS resection between 2009 and 2021. Institution 1 provided the training cohort (n = 128) and internal validation cohort (n = 55); Institution 2 provided the external test cohort (n = 184). A radiomics signature was constructed from three-dimensional tumor features. A deep-learning signature was derived from the largest axial tumor section using an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-101 trained with Cox partial-likelihood loss. Clinical variables underwent univariable and multivariable Cox regression analysis. The retained clinicopathologic variables and imaging signatures were integrated into a combined model termed RDCS. RESULTS: During follow-up, 71, 30, and 107 patients died in the training, internal validation, and external test cohorts, respectively. The corresponding RDCS C-indices were 0.775, 0.704, and 0.725, each higher than those of the individual radiomics, deep-learning, and clinical models.
