This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the pathophysiological basis, non-invasive assessment, prognostic value, and clinical implementation of vascular phenotyping across the CKM spectrum, with particular emphasis on arterial stiffness and endothelial function. The principal approaches discussed include carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV), brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity, flow-mediated dilation (FMD), peripheral arterial tonometry, microvascular techniques, and structural markers such as coronary artery calcium (CAC) and carotid plaque, considered in the context of contemporary CKM staging and PREVENT-based risk assessment. Among functional vascular measures, cfPWV remains the best-validated non-invasive marker of aortic stiffness and is independently associated with cardiovascular and renal outcomes, whereas FMD provides complementary information on conduit-artery endothelial function but is limited by technical requirements and inconsistent incremental predictive value. Microvascular and glycocalyx-based techniques remain less standardized, while structural phenotyping, particularly CAC and carotid plaque assessment, has stronger evidence for risk reclassification in selected populations. Vascular phenotyping should therefore be regarded as a selective, risk-adapted strategy rather than a universal screening approach. Its greatest potential may lie in integrating vascular measures with CKM stage, PREVENT estimates, kidney and cardiac biomarkers, and structural imaging to identify disproportionate or subclinical vascular injury, particularly during progression from CKM stage 2 to stage 3. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether such multimodal phenotyping improves therapeutic decision-making and cardiovascular and kidney outcomes.

articles.title: GlioVision: A multimodal MRI framework for non-invasive prediction of glioma molecular biomarkers.
articles.abstract: Gliomas are primary brain tumors for which molecular biomarker assessment plays an important role in clinical evaluation and treatment planning. Traditional assessment relies on analysis of surgical tumor specimens, which carries procedural risks and sampling bias due to tumor heterogeneity. Existing deep learning methods can be computationally demanding and are often trained on narrowly represented datasets, which may limit their clinical deployment. In this study, we propose GlioVision, a multi-modal deep learning framework for non-invasive prediction of glioma molecular biomarkers using multi-parametric MRI, including T1, T1-Gd, T2, and FLAIR sequences. The framework employs a 3D DenseNet-based architecture with channel and spatial feature recalibration, combined with an adaptive processing module that handles variability across multi-institutional datasets. In addition, a confidence-based filtering mechanism (CFPM) is introduced to identify low-confidence predictions and quantify prediction uncertainty. The model is trained and evaluated on a multi-cohort dataset compiled from publicly available sources, comprising 2270 subjects with heterogeneous imaging protocols. Subject-level splitting is used to prevent data leakage, and performance is reported using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity across all biomarkers. Independent public cohorts were used for testing. GlioVision achieves AUC values of 0.94 for IDH, 0.87 for 1p/19q, 0.86 for MGMT, and 0.92 for tumor grade, indicating consistent performance across biomarkers. The effect of confidence-based filtering is also analyzed to examine the trade-off between prediction coverage and accuracy. Finally, we investigate a simple model obfuscation approach based on controlled image perturbations and evaluate its impact on prediction performance. This study presents a multi-institutional evaluation of a deep learning pipeline for predicting glioma biomarkers from MRI. It may support further research in radiogenomic analysis and non-invasive tumor characterization.

articles.title: Coronary artery anomalies in computed tomography of coronary arteries for symptomatic patients: Types, prevalence and association with atheromatous disease.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Anomalous coronary arteries are rare but potentially dangerous. Early diagnosis and recognition can prevent serious outcomes. Our study aimed to determine the prevalence of coronary artery anomalies amongst symptomatic individuals who presented for computer tomography of coronary arteries (CTCA) and their trends with age and concurrent atherosclerotic disease. METHODS: Retrospective study of all CTCAs for symptomatic patients was conducted over a 5-year period in a large healthcare network, including a dedicated heart hospital, to identify the types and prevalence of anomalous coronary arteries. Patients' age, symptomology and associated atherosclerotic burden represented by CAD-RADS and calcium scores were compared between the identified individuals with coronary artery anomalies. RESULTS: A total of 13,596 patients were recruited. 296 (2.18%) patients had significant coronary anomalies. Mean age was 53.85 years. 211/296 (71.28%) patients had anomalous coronary artery origins. 180/296 (60.81%) patients had anomalous coronary artery courses in which 85/180 (47.22%) were potentially malignant (inter-arterial course). There were 25/296 (8.45%) patients with coronary artery fistulae and 12/296 (4.05%) patients with more complex coronary vascular malformations. There was statistical significance between potentially malignant coronary artery course and younger age and trend towards lower CAD-RADS score and Agatston calcium score. CONCLUSION: Broad variability of incidence of coronary anomalies on imaging has been reported in the literature. To our knowledge, this study is amongst the first to demonstrate a statistically significant association between potentially malignant coronary artery course and younger age on CTCA, with a trend towards lower CAD-RADS score and Agatston calcium score also observed.

articles.title: From AI to AID: Algorithmic imaging detection (AID) as a more precise label for AI in radiology.
articles.abstract: The term artificial intelligence (AI) encompasses a heterogeneous range of computational methodologies that differ substantially in function, degree of autonomy, and evidentiary support. In patient-facing communication, this heterogeneity and associated uncertainty may introduce clinically relevant interpretive and liability concerns. The designation "AI" alone provides limited information regarding a system's specific function, the extent of clinician oversight and verification, or the rigor and scope of its validation. Moreover, emerging evidence indicates that diagnostic terminology can causally influence patients' perceived risk, expectations regarding care, and treatment preferences. We therefore propose targeted modifications to patient-facing materials, informed-consent discussions, and clinical report annotations to improve terminological precision and transparency. For non-imaging applications, analogous function-specific descriptors could be adopted. Importantly, terminology should complement, rather than substitute for, the substantive disclosures that patients consider most relevant, including system function, clinician involvement, validation, performance characteristics, and limitations.

articles.title: The Role of Reprojected Planar Data Derived from Fast Whole-Body Bone SPECT/CT.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The purpose of this prospective study was to investigate the preferred reconstruction SPECT parameters for generating reprojected planar images in bone studies, and to evaluate, by visual reader assessment, the feasibility of using these reprojected images as a substitute for traditional planar whole-body (WB) bone scan images. This was a single-centre feasibility study; diagnostic accuracy was not assessed. Methods: Patients referred for planar bone scintigraphy (PBS) and WB-SPECT/CT were prospectively enrolled. Reprojected planar bone scintigraphy (R-PBS) data were generated using forward projection of the three-bed SPECT/CT data. Three nuclear medicine (NM) specialists, blinded to the imaging reconstruction, evaluated both sets of images in a randomised order. The preferred reconstruction parameters for R-PBS were determined by visual assessment using a 4-point ordinal visual scoring scale. A side-by-side comparison of PBS vs. R-PBS was conducted, including assessments of image quality, artefact generation, image preference, and any clinical significance that may affect report interpretation. The agreement between the physicians' evaluations was measured using the Kappa coefficient test. Results: Of the four reconstruction parameter combinations, 6 iterations, 8 subsets, and a 5 mm Gaussian post-filter yielded the highest visual quality scores. PBS images scored higher on image quality, though this difference was not statistically significant (p > 0.05). The inter-rater agreement for image quality scores was moderate for both PBS and R-PBS images. The results indicate that among the 33 reader-level assessments derived from 11 patient pairs and reviewed by the 3 readers, PBS images were preferred 13 times (~40%), R-PBS 10 times (30%), and no preference was indicated for the remaining 10 (30%). Conclusions: In this small feasibility cohort, R-PBS images derived from fast WB-SPECT/CT data were of visual quality comparable to PBS and may have potential as an alternative to PBS. If confirmed in larger studies with formal diagnostic accuracy assessment, R-PBS could remove the need for a separate PBS acquisition and reduce overall patient imaging time.

articles.title: Epigenetic Lymphocyte Subset Associations Across Allergic Phenotypes in a Predominantly Pediatric Cohort.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: DNA methylation-based lymphocyte enumeration may provide an alternative to conventional immunophenotyping, but its associations with allergic phenotypes require careful interpretation. We examined these associations in a predominantly pediatric cohort. Methods: This retrospective study included 206 participants aged 1-57 years (189 aged <18 years; 57.8% male; median age 5 years, IQR 3-8), evaluated between 24 November 2025 and 28 February 2026. Absolute subset counts were derived from the epigenetic i.Mune TBNK assay and CBC lymphocyte counts. Group comparisons used Mann-Whitney U tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across 56 comparisons. Firth models adjusted for three subset counts, CD4/CD8 ratio, log(IgE+1), age, and sex; percentage-based, comorbidity-adjusted, and age-restricted sensitivity analyses were added. IgE-containing models included 201 complete cases. Results: Allergic rhinitis was associated with lower CD4+ counts in the primary model (OR per 100 cells/µL 0.923; p = 0.0009), with the association retained after comorbidity adjustment and age restriction but not in the percentage model. Atopic dermatitis was associated with log(IgE+1) (OR 1.475; p = 0.0009). Food allergy was associated with higher CD19+ counts in the primary model (OR per 100 cells/µL 1.060; p = 0.0341), but this association was not retained in sensitivity analyses. No absolute NK-count difference was found for food allergy. Single-marker discrimination was modest (CD4+ AUC for rhinitis 0.711). Conclusions: These exploratory associations are sensitive to the measurement scale and model specification. They do not establish phenotype-specific epigenetic mechanisms, standalone diagnostic utility, or functional immune monitoring.

articles.title: Incidental Popliteal Bursa Localization on I-131 Whole-Body Scintigraphy.
articles.abstract: I-131 scintigraphy can be performed after I-131 radioactive iodine (RAI) treatment in appropriate patients for dynamic risk stratification. Sodium iodide symporter (NIS) expression is a mechanism responsible for uptake of I-131 in thyroid tissue and thyroid cancer. There are other mechanisms that iodine engages in the body, leading to possible false-positive findings. A popliteal bursa, or Baker's cyst, is a bursa that lies in the popliteal region. As a bursa, it is a potential space and is lined by synovial membrane. It is not normally visualized on imaging. However, passive diffusion of radioactive iodine or pathological changes occur with local irritation. Presented herein is a 75-year-old woman with a history of poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma. Her postoperative American Thyroid Association risk stratification was high. A diagnostic iodine whole body scintigraphy for dynamic risk stratification following RAI treatment performed. Planar imaging on posterior-view showed mildly intense iodine uptake in the left knee, differentials included atypical location of osseous metastasis, and false-positive pathologies. Regional SPECT/CT localized the false-positive iodine uptake in the Baker's cyst. The teaching point for this case is to be vigilant of uncommon false-positive pathologies on iodine scintigraphy. Diagnostic confidence is improved by adding SPECT/CT imaging.

articles.title: Quality, Readability, Understandability, and Actionability of AI Chatbots' Responses to Dental Patient Questions: A Comparative Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used to obtain oral health information, yet prior dental studies have already evaluated overlapping domains such as accuracy, quality, readability, understandability, and actionability. This study applied and extended a multidimensional evaluation approach to compare AI-generated answers to dental patient questions, with emphasis on Turkish-language readability, standard PEMAT-P applicability, effect-size and uncertainty reporting, and inter-rater reliability. Methods: Thirty-three AI-assisted, expert-curated questions were submitted to ChatGPT 5.2, Gemini, DeepSeek V3, and Grok 3, yielding 132 responses. Three dental evaluators independently assessed clinical accuracy, Global Quality Score (GQS), understandability (PEMAT-U), and actionability (PEMAT-A). PEMAT-P scores were calculated using the standard item structure and item-specific applicability rules, with items coded as not applicable (N/A) excluded from the denominator. Readability was calculated using a deterministic, rule-based implementation of the Ateşman formula. Model comparisons used the Friedman test, Bonferroni-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, effect sizes, bootstrap confidence intervals, and two-way random-effects intraclass correlation coefficients. An exploratory Pareto analysis assessed multidimensional dominance without imposing arbitrary weights. Results: Significant model differences were observed for all five dimensions (all p ≤ 0.002). Gemini had the highest mean GQS, clinical accuracy, PEMAT-U, and PEMAT-A scores, but its Ateşman readability score was significantly lower than those of ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Grok. No significant readability differences were observed among the latter three models. Average-measure reliability was poor for GQS and clinical accuracy and moderate for PEMAT-U and PEMAT-A. No model dominated another across all five dimensions. Conclusions: The chatbots demonstrated model-specific strengths rather than uniform superiority. Their performance should be interpreted multidimensionally, together with effect magnitude, uncertainty, and inter-rater reliability, rather than through a single overall ranking.

articles.title: Label-Scarce Ultrasound Biopsy Needle Identification Using Dynamics-Guided Prior Modeling.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ultrasound-guided biopsy is essential for accurate needle placement in minimally invasive procedures. However, the limited availability of labeled medical data significantly constrains the development of needle segmentation models, and existing semi-supervised approaches rely solely on data-driven consistency constraints without incorporating domain-specific dynamic properties of the imaging process. We propose a semi-supervised unrolling optimization framework that combines dynamics-based data consistency with self-training. Methods: (1) A null-space projection-based Analytic Model (A) layer is unrolled into the network to suppress background interference and enforce dynamics-based constraints derived from temporal ultrasound sequences, in which the background subspace is estimated via singular value decomposition (SVD) of consecutive frames and the needle signal is recovered by projecting the observed image onto the orthogonal complement of this subspace. (2) A self-training strategy leverages unlabeled ultrasound data by generating soft pseudo-labels from a pretrained teacher network to iteratively supervise the student model, which shares the same unrolling architecture and is jointly trained with a supervised loss on labeled data and a pseudo loss on unlabeled data. Results: Evaluation on an ultrasound needle segmentation dataset demonstrated that the proposed method achieved a Dice score of 0.7429±0.0489 and an IoU of 0.5967±0.0917, outperforming the supervised UnrollNet baseline (Dice: 0.7298±0.0518), Co-Training (U-Net) (Dice: 0.6104±0.0949), and Meta Pseudo Labels (Dice: 0.6426±0.1140). The proposed method also yielded a mean trajectory angle error of 0.66∘±0.63∘ and a tip position error of 0.95mm±0.74mm. Conclusions: These results indicate the potential of the proposed framework for ultrasound-guided needle tracking.

articles.title: Immunohistochemical Expression of M30, BCL-2, BAX, and Ki-67 in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: Association with Clinicopathological Features.
articles.abstract: Background: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is an aggressive malignancy with limited survival despite advances in diagnosis and treatment. Dysregulation of apoptosis and tumor cell proliferation is a fundamental feature of cancer biology. M30, BCL-2, and BAX reflect different aspects of apoptotic activity and regulation, whereas Ki-67 is a widely used marker of cellular proliferation. However, the clinicopathological significance of these markers in PDAC remains incompletely characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the immunohistochemical expression of M30, BCL-2, BAX, and Ki-67 in PDAC and to investigate their associations with established clinicopathological features. Methods: This retrospective study included 50 patients with surgically resected PDAC treated at Afyon Kocatepe University Medical Faculty Hospital between January 2003 and May 2015. Archived tumor specimens were evaluated by immunohistochemistry for M30, BCL-2, BAX, and Ki-67. M30 and Ki-67 expression were quantified according to the percentage of positive tumor cells, while BCL-2 and BAX expression were assessed using semiquantitative staining scores based on staining intensity and the proportion of positive tumor cells. Immunohistochemical findings were compared with sex, tumor differentiation, tumor size, lymphovascular invasion, perineural invasion, surgical margin status, tumor stage, lymph node metastasis, and clinical stage. Results: The study cohort comprised 30 male and 20 female patients, with a mean age of 62.12 ± 10.93 years. M30 expression was detected in 39 (78%) cases, whereas Ki-67 expression ranged from 10% to 85% of tumor cells. BCL-2 and BAX expression showed variable staining patterns. None of the four markers demonstrated a statistically significant association with tumor differentiation, tumor size, lymphovascular invasion, perineural invasion, surgical margin status, tumor stage, lymph node metastasis, or clinical stage. Conclusions: In this cohort of surgically resected PDAC, immunohistochemical expression of M30, BCL-2, BAX, and Ki-67 was not significantly associated with conventional clinicopathological indicators of tumor aggressiveness. These findings indicate that immunohistochemical assessment of individual apoptosis- and proliferation-related markers may not adequately reflect tumor aggressiveness or clinicopathological heterogeneity in PDAC. Further studies incorporating larger cohorts, standardized immunohistochemical assessment, and clinical outcome data are warranted to clarify their potential biological and prognostic significance.

articles.title: Modeling Factors Associated with Smoking Dependence Severity Using Binary Classification-Based Machine Learning: Prediction with Hematological and Demographic Patient Data.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence (FTND) is a subjective, self-report-based instrument used to grade the level of nicotine dependence. Complete blood count (CBC) parameters reflect markers of smoking-related systemic inflammation. In the present study, we aimed to develop a leakage-free and interpretable machine learning approach for classifying FTND level using demographic data, CBC parameters, and duration of smoking exposure. Methods: In this retrospectively designed study, the records of 660 patients with complete data who had presented to the Smoking Cessation Outpatient Clinic of Malatya Training and Research Hospital were included. Because one of the six FTND items directly scores the number of cigarettes smoked per day, the number of packs and the features related to it constitute data leakage and were therefore excluded from the data pool. Smoking duration (years), which is not an FTND item, was retained as the sole predictor of smoking exposure. Feature engineering generated 49 candidate features. Six base learners (logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting, SVM, LightGBM, XGBoost) and a stacking ensemble were evaluated with an 80-20% training/test split and 10-fold stratified cross-validation. To prevent optimism bias, feature selection and scaling were performed only within the training folds, and class imbalance was addressed through class weighting. The models were interpreted with SHAP and LIME, and the contribution of each feature family was quantified by ablation analysis. Results: In leakage-free 10-fold cross-validation (the primary performance estimate), discrimination was modest, with the highest AUC (0.652) obtained by both SVM (RBF) and logistic regression; on the single hold-out test set, the stacking ensemble reached an AUC of 0.749 (95% CI 0.667-0.831). The full model did not significantly outperform smoking duration alone (DeLong p = 0.22), and extensive feature engineering did not provide a measurable gain (ΔAUC = -0.015). In the SHAP analysis, smoking duration and the age-based interaction terms made the largest predictive contributions. Conclusions: Routine CBC parameters do not by themselves constitute an independent diagnostic tool for determining dependence severity; they carry only weak, complementary information and should not be regarded as a screening biomarker. This exploratory study classifies FTND-based nicotine dependence severity at the individual patient level by combining CBC parameters with machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence; the model is not ready for clinical use.

articles.title: Association of Mandibular Morphological and Trabecular Bone Characteristics with Long-Term Outcomes Following First Permanent Molar Extraction: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Purpose: This study aimed to evaluate mandibular morphological, trabecular, dental, and periapical factors associated with favorable long-term outcomes following early mandibular first permanent molar (FPM) extraction. Methods: This retrospective study included 60 patients with pre-extraction and ≥5-year follow-up panoramic radiographs. Patients were classified into favorable (FO; n = 30) and unfavorable (UFO; n = 30) outcome groups according to residual space and second permanent molar (SPM) axial position. Gonial angle (GA), antegonial notch depth (AND), notch angle (ANA), cortical thickness (ACT), and corpus and angulus fractal dimensions (FD) were assessed. Initial SPM and second premolar (SP)angulations, primary second molar (PSM)-SP status, and FPM periapical index (PAI) scores were also evaluated. Analyses included Bonferroni correction, exploratory multivariable logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results: AND was greater in the FO group (Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.015) and remained associated with FO after adjustment (OR = 2.22 per millimeter; 95% CI: 1.19-4.15; p = 0.012). An extracted PSM with an unerupted SP was associated with higher odds of FO than a retained PSM (adjusted OR = 9.51; 95% CI: 1.45-62.50; p = 0.019). AND demonstrated moderate discrimination (AUC = 0.728; 95% CI: 0.600-0.856); a ≥2.0-mm threshold yielded 86.7% sensitivity and 53.3% specificity. Other morphological and fractal parameters did not differ significantly between groups; angulations and PAI were not significantly associated with outcome. Conclusions: AND and PSM-SP status were associated with FO. These exploratory findings require validation in larger, independent cohorts before clinical application, particularly given the wide confidence intervals for categorical estimates and the limited specificity of the proposed AND threshold.

articles.title: AI-Assisted Triage for Diabetic Retinopathy Integrated into Routine Diabetes Care: A Real-World Diagnostic Accuracy Study of the DAIRET® Algorithm.
articles.abstract: Background: Screening for diabetic retinopathy (DR) is resource-intensive. We evaluated the real-world diagnostic accuracy of the DAIRET® Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithm, integrated into the electronic medical record, as a triage tool in routine diabetes care. Methods: Retrospective, STARD-AI-compliant study of consecutive adults with diabetes screened with non-mydriatic fundus photography between April and December 2025. The DAIRET® output ("suspected"/"not suspected") was compared with grading by an ophthalmologist masked to the AI result. Sensitivity, specificity and predictive values with exact 95% confidence intervals were calculated for any DR and referable (moderate or worse) DR. Results: Among 1051 patients, 185 (17.6%) had DR: 160 mild and 25 moderate non-proliferative DR; none had severe DR. DAIRET® classified 271 patients (25.8%) as suspected. For any DR, sensitivity was 59.5% (52.0-66.6) and specificity 81.4% (78.7-83.9). For referable DR, sensitivity was 100.0% (86.3-100.0), specificity 76.0% (73.3-78.6) and negative predictive value 100.0% (99.5-100.0). Specificity was lower in patients aged <65 years and with type 1 diabetes. Conclusions: No referable case was missed, although sensitivity was based on 25 cases (lower limit 86.3%) and 15 AI-negative patients lacked complete verification. The 74% classified as "not suspected" is a potential, not measured, reduction in referrals. Performance for severe or proliferative DR could not be assessed, and multi-center confirmation is needed.

articles.title: Repeatability of Swan600 and Its Agreement with Lenstar LS900 for Ocular Biometry in Children.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To evaluate the repeatability of the Swan SW600 optical biometer and its agreement with the Lenstar LS900 in measuring ocular biometric parameters in children and adolescents. Methods: This prospective study included 778 children and adolescents aged 3-18 years. Parameters included axial length (AL), corneal radii in the flattest and steepest meridians (R1 and R2), central corneal thickness (CCT), anterior chamber depth (AD), lens thickness (LT), white-to-white distance (WTW), and axial length-to-corneal radius ratio (AL/CR). Repeatability of Swan SW600 was assessed using within-subject standard deviation (Sw), coefficient of repeatability (CoR), coefficient of variation (CoV), and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Agreement between devices was evaluated using paired t tests, ICC, and Bland-Altman analysis. Results: Swan SW600 repeatability was excellent for AL, R1, R2, CCT, AD, and AL/CR (ICC = 0.9918-0.9999) and lower for LT (ICC = 0.9060) and WTW (ICC = 0.8452). Agreement with Lenstar LS900 was strongest for AL (mean difference -0.050 ± 0.041 mm; 95% LoA -0.131 to 0.031 mm; ICC = 1.000), R1 (ICC = 0.986), R2 (ICC = 0.980), and AL/CR (ICC = 0.993). CCT and AD showed good agreement (ICC = 0.877 and 0.895), whereas LT showed lower agreement (ICC = 0.689). WTW showed poor agreement (ICC = 0.288). Age-stratified analyses showed consistently high agreement for AL, R1, R2, and AL/CR across all age groups, including children aged 3-6 years, whereas agreement for CCT, AD, LT, and WTW was more variable. Conclusions: The Swan SW600 demonstrates high repeatability and close agreement with the Lenstar LS900 for AL, corneal radii, and AL/CR in children and adolescents, including preschool-aged children; however, the weaker agreement observed for LT and particularly WTW suggests that these parameters should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Agreement Between Venous and Capillary Haemoglobin Concentrations in a High-Burden Urban Indian Setting: A Cross-Sectional Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background: Anaemia is a major public health issue in India, where point-of-care testing is central to national control strategies. This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of the HemoCue® Hb 201+ for haemoglobin (Hb) estimation from capillary blood compared to the gold-standard venous blood analysis. Methods: In a cross-sectional study of 748 participants in a low-resource urban Delhi setting, Hb levels from single-drop capillary samples (HemoCue® Hb 201+) were compared to those from venous samples (automated autoanalyzer). Agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, Passing-Bablok regression, and standard diagnostic accuracy metrics. Results: The mean (SD) haemoglobin concentration was lower in capillary samples (11.83 [1.95] g/dL) than in venous samples (12.56 [1.89] g/dL). Capillary Hb was, on average, 0.73 g/dL lower than venous Hb (95% limits of agreement: -3.11 to 1.65 g/dL). Consequently, the HemoCue® Hb 201+ significantly overestimated anaemia prevalence (54.4% vs. 35.0%). The capillary method demonstrated high sensitivity (92.4%) for detecting anaemia but only moderate specificity (66.1%), indicating a tendency for false positives. Conclusions: Although the HemoCue® Hb 201+ is a sensitive tool for anaemia screening in field settings, the moderate specificity and the significant negative bias can lead to overestimation of prevalence and potential misclassification of individuals. However, the limitation of single-drop capillary sampling warrant cautious interpretation of results, particularly for clinical decision-making and precise prevalence estimation.

articles.title: Association Between Urine pH and Kidney Outcomes in Patients with Biopsy-Proven Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Lower urine pH has been associated with reduced kidney function and increased risk of kidney disease, but its prognostic and pathological significance in biopsy-proven kidney disease remains unclear. Medullary cast formation has been shown to predict adverse renal outcomes beyond cortical interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IFTA), although its clinical determinants are not fully understood. We examined the associations of urine pH with kidney outcomes and medullary cast formation in patients undergoing native kidney biopsy. Methods: Among 1167 adults who underwent native kidney biopsy between 2011 and 2024, 503 patients with evaluable medullary tissue were included. Urine pH was analyzed in relation to clinical and histological variables and kidney outcomes. The primary outcome was a ≥40% decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) or initiation of renal replacement therapy. Results: Mean baseline eGFR was 60.7 ± 26.2 mL/min/1.73 m2 and urine pH was 6.15 ± 0.84. During a median follow-up of 2.11 years, 113 patients (22.5%) reached the outcome. Lower urine pH was associated with higher risk of kidney outcomes. In multivariable Cox models, urine pH remained independently associated with outcomes (hazard ratio per 1-unit increase, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.52-0.92). Addition of urine pH modestly improved discrimination (C-index 0.642 to 0.654; likelihood ratio test, p = 0.009). Lower urine pH was associated with greater medullary cast formation in unadjusted analysis. Conclusions: Lower urine pH was independently associated with adverse kidney outcomes and with greater medullary cast formation, suggesting that urine pH may reflect intratubular pathological changes associated with CKD progression.

articles.title: CT Ventricular Volume Reference Percentile Curves Using Automated nnU-Net Segmentation: A Study with LLM-Facilitated Cohort Selection.
articles.abstract: Background: Age- and sex-specific CT reference percentile curves of ventricular volume may support objective assessment of ventricular enlargement. We aimed to generate such curves by combining a locally deployed large language model (LLM) for cohort curation with nnU-Net 12-subcompartment segmentation. Methods: This retrospective study did not require formal ethics approval under the Swiss Human Research Act. We screened 42,211 head CT reports from January 2019 to April 2024. A phrase prefilter identified 9622 candidates for German-tuned 70-billion-parameter LLM review of stroke, leukoencephalopathy, parenchymal defects, enlarged ventricles, and space-occupying lesions; 6516 remained. A second LLM workflow screened 210,761 clinical data warehouse summaries to exclude dementia, organic brain disease, or cognitive decline. After image-availability and series-mismatch exclusions, the final cohort comprised 2608 CTs from 2608 patients (1374 males, 1234 females; age 14-98 years). Ventricular masks were obtained using a validated nnU-Net tool integrated in TotalSegmentator. Results: LLM labelling accuracy in 471 blinded reports ranged from 0.966 to 0.992. CDW screening audit showed 91% agreement, sensitivity 0.96, and negative predictive value 0.96. Median total ventricular volume rose from 10.94 mL in young females and 13.42 mL in young males to 21.97 mL and 31.97 mL, respectively, in the 60-69 age group. Except for the fourth ventricle, compartments showed positive age correlations (r = 0.44-0.69); the fourth ventricle showed no relevant association (r = 0.01 males; r = 0.05 females). After adjustment for age, male sex remained associated with greater total ventricular volume (6.54 mL; 95% CI, 5.61-7.46; p<0.001). Conclusions: This study provides age- and sex-specific CT ventricular nomograms in a selected reference cohort. The LLM-assisted curation and nnU-Net segmentation workflow provides a feasible approach for large-scale cohort analysis.

articles.title: Beyond Breslow Thickness: Reproducibility and Histopathologic Concordance of Ultra-High-Frequency Ultrasound in Primary Cutaneous Melanoma.
articles.abstract: Background: Ultra-high-frequency ultrasound (UHFUS) provides high-resolution assessment of superficial skin lesions, but evidence in melanoma has largely focused on preoperative thickness estimation. We evaluated the reproducibility of a structured UHFUS assessment and its histopathologic concordance in primary cutaneous melanoma. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 320 treatment-naïve, histologically confirmed primary cutaneous melanomas examined with UHFUS (48-70 MHz) before excision. Two experienced radiologists independently assessed tumor thickness, horizontal diameter, surface discontinuity, deepest involved compartment, boundary definition, morphology, echostructure, and separate perilesional hypoechoic foci. Histopathology served as the reference standard. Reproducibility was assessed using ICC and κ statistics; UHFUS-Breslow agreement was evaluated using Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and Bland-Altman analysis. Results: Interobserver reproducibility was excellent for tumor thickness (ICC 0.96; 95% CI, 0.95-0.97) and horizontal diameter (ICC 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.95). UHFUS thickness showed excellent concordance with Breslow thickness (CCC 0.95; 95% CI, 0.94-0.96 for both readers), with small positive biases (+0.12 and +0.10 mm). Exact agreement across predefined thickness strata was 90.0%. Surface discontinuity showed high sensitivity and specificity for histopathologic ulceration, whereas perilesional hypoechoic foci were highly specific but moderately sensitive for microsatellitosis. Increased tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and an associated nevus component independently predicted greater UHFUS overestimation. Conclusions: Structured UHFUS provides reproducible quantitative and qualitative preoperative assessment of primary melanoma beyond thickness alone and may serve as a complementary imaging tool within specialized multidisciplinary pathways, while histopathology remains the reference standard for definitive diagnosis and staging.

articles.title: Clinical Implications of the Age Threshold in the 2022 ACR/EULAR Classification Criteria for Takayasu Arteritis: A Real-World Study of Patients Aged over 61 Years.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The age item of the 2022 American College of Rheumatology (ACR) and the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) criteria for Takayasu arteritis (TAK) (the 2022 ACR/EULAR criteria) limits the reclassification of TAK among patients aged over 61 who were classified as TAK according to the 1990 ACR criteria. Therefore, we evaluated the clinical significance of the age item of the 2022 ACR/EULAR criteria. Methods: We included 22 previously TAK-diagnosed patients aged over 61 (TAK patient aged >61 years) and 41 TAK-reclassified patients aged 50-60 (controls) in this study and retrospectively reviewed their medical records. We compared the satisfied items of the 2022 ACR/EULAR criteria between the two groups and further investigated whether these 22 TAK patients aged >61 years fulfilled the criteria for other relevant diseases. Results: In terms of absolute requirements, TAK patients aged >61 years were significantly older than TAK-reclassified patients aged 50-60. However, there were no further significant differences in the additional clinical and imaging criteria between the two groups. TAK patients aged >61 years exhibited a significantly higher frequency of ascending aorta involvement than TAK-reclassified patients aged 50-60 (18.2% vs. 0%, p = 0.012). Among the 22 TAK patients aged >61 years, ten were categorized as clinically isolated aortitis, and three of the ten patients with CIA could additionally be categorized as restrictively defined-isolated aortitis. Conclusions: Our findings support the need for external validation of the current age threshold in larger cohorts from different ethnic and geographical populations.

articles.title: Multi-Platform Transcriptomic Classification of LUAD Driver Mutation Subtypes via Heterogeneous Ensemble Learning.
articles.abstract: Background: Accurate identification of EGFR-mutant, KRAS-mutant, and triple-negative (TN) LUAD driver mutation subtypes is essential for guiding targeted therapy, yet standard molecular testing is invasive and not always feasible. Gene expression-based machine learning offers an alternative that avoids additional invasive sampling; however, existing models are largely restricted to binary classification and lack cross-platform generalizability. Methods: We developed a multi-cohort, ComBat-harmonized pipeline integrating SHAP-driven feature selection and a Bayesian-optimized heterogeneous ensemble of five learners, extended with NSGA-II Pareto-optimal weight optimization under leak-free cross-validation. External validation used an independent RNA-seq cohort with reference-batch harmonization and threshold calibration. Results: ParetoVoting achieved the best internal performance (F1-macro = 0.736, AUROC = 0.877), statistically indistinguishable from SoftVoting (F1-macro = 0.735; Cliff's δ=-0.12), which was carried forward for external validation. On TCGA-LUAD (n=508), SoftVoting attained F1-macro = 0.700 and AUROC = 0.850, though this reflects an out-of-range KRAS threshold (representative value ∼0.66-0.68). Ablation analysis showed components contributed unequally within internal cross-validation, with ComBat's critical role instead emerging during cross-platform external generalization. SHAP analysis identified biologically coherent signatures consistent with known LUAD oncogenic signaling. Conclusions: This framework provides a reproducible, cross-platform approach to three-class driver mutation subtyping from transcriptomic data, offering benchmarks for this underexplored task and potential clinical utility where tissue-based profiling is infeasible.

articles.title: Blood and Urine Transcriptomes Reveal Complementary Host Responses and a Creatinine-Associated Urinary Transcriptional Axis in Sepsis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sepsis is characterized by systemic immune dysregulation and organ dysfunction, but transcriptomic profiles from different biofluids may provide partially overlapping and distinct molecular readouts of the host response. We characterized transcriptomic profiles of whole blood and urinary cellular fractions in sepsis, with particular emphasis on a urinary transcriptional gradient associated with continuous serum creatinine and on whether this association was mirrored in matched blood. Methods: Targeted RNA sequencing was performed on whole blood from 35 patients with sepsis and 10 healthy controls and on urinary cellular fractions from 21 patients with sepsis and 7 controls using the Ion AmpliSeq Transcriptome Human Gene Expression workflow. Differential expression was assessed with DESeq2, with sequencing-adjusted sensitivity models where appropriate. Sensitivity analyses addressed the highest creatinine value, sex and age, and matched blood-urine creatinine-associated effects. Results: Whole-blood analysis identified 2659 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including a robust core of 1796 genes characterized by neutrophil-myeloid activation and adaptive-immune suppression. The exploratory urine case-control comparison identified 1552 DEGs but was substantially confounded by sequencing chip. Continuous serum creatinine analysis identified 4064 chip-adjusted urinary DEGs, including a robust core of 3774 genes enriched for inflammatory, interferon, hypoxic, autophagic, lysosomal, vesicular, metabolic, and mitochondrial programs. Exclusion of the highest creatinine sample retained 3192/4064 strict DEGs with the same direction and 2926/3774 robust-core genes. In the same 21 patients, adjusted creatinine-associated effects were weakly concordant between blood and urine at the gene level (Pearson r = 0.192; Spearman ρ = 0.199), with five overlapping strict DEGs and no robust-core overlap. Hallmark concordance was greater but moderate (Pearson r = 0.293; Spearman ρ = 0.464), with 14 shared robust pathways. Conclusions: Transcriptomic profiles of whole blood and urinary cellular fractions showed distinct but partially overlapping host-response patterns in sepsis. The serum creatinine-associated urinary transcriptional axis was robust across sensitivity analyses and was only weakly mirrored at the gene level in matched blood, despite partial pathway-level convergence. These findings should be interpreted as serum creatinine-associated transcriptional patterns rather than as evidence of kidney-specific injury or validated diagnostic or prognostic signatures. Independent longitudinal cohorts and orthogonal molecular validation are required.

articles.title: Macular Retinal Layer Thickness in Mild-to-Moderate Parkinson's Disease.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Characterization of individual retinal layer thicknesses in mild-to-moderate Parkinson's disease (PD) remains limited. This study compares retinal layer thicknesses between patients with mild-to-moderate PD and controls. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, patients with PD of Hoehn and Yahr (HY) stage 1 to stage 3 and age- and sex-matched cognitively normal controls without PD underwent spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging. Seven retinal layers were segmented: nerve fiber layer, ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GC-IPL), inner nuclear layer (INL), outer plexiform layer, outer nuclear layer (ONL), photoreceptor layer (PRL), and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). Mean thickness for each layer and the total retina were measured within the 3 mm and 6 mm Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study rings. Results: Sixty-seven eyes from 41 patients with PD and 72 eyes from 41 controls were included. In the 6 mm ring, PD eyes had a nominally thicker GC-IPL (p = 0.01), INL (p = 0.01), RPE (p = 0.03), and total retina (p = 0.03) compared to control eyes. In the 6 mm ring, PRL was nominally thinner in HY stage 3 compared to HY stages 2-2.5 (p = 0.02). In the 6 mm ring, the ONL was nominally thinner in the eyes of PD patients in HY stage 3 compared to the eyes of PD patients in HY stages 1-1.5 (p = 0.02) and 2-2.5 (p = 0.04). However, none of these differences remained significant after False Discovery Rate adjustment (all adjusted p > 0.05). Conclusions: In this exploratory cross-sectional study, no significant differences in macular retinal layer thicknesses were found between patients with mild-to-moderate PD and controls without PD after adjusting for multiple comparisons. The nominal thickness differences observed here require larger, longitudinal cohorts to determine if true structural differences exist in mild-to-moderate PD.

articles.title: Fusion of Deep Learning Radiomics and Clinical Features for Individualized Prediction of Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Response in Osteosarcoma.
articles.abstract: Background: Stage IIB conventional osteosarcoma exhibits highly heterogeneous responses to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, necessitating reliable, noninvasive pre-treatment evaluation systems. Methods: This retrospective study of 198 patients utilized pre-treatment T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and baseline clinical data. Twelve classical convolutional neural network architectures were benchmarked to identify the optimal imaging backbone. This selected radiomics score was then integrated with core clinical variables using logistic regression to construct a multimodal model. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping++ (Grad-CAM++) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithms provided image- and feature-level interpretability. Results: DenseNet121 achieved the highest mean cross-validated area under the curve (AUC; 0.775) and was selected, with AUCs of 0.797 (95% CI: 0.716-0.877) and 0.701 (95% CI: 0.513-0.877) in the training and test cohorts. Adding the clinical variables improved discrimination, yielding a test-cohort AUC of 0.827 (95% CI: 0.661-0.992) with significant reclassification gain over the radiomics-only model (NRI = 1.28, IDI = 0.177; DeLong p = 0.011). Grad-CAM++ activation concentrated on the solid medullary and extraosseous soft-tissue components, and SHAP ranked the radiomics score as the strongest contributor. Conclusions: Integrating deep learning radiomics with key clinical features provides a noninvasive tool for the individualized prediction of neoadjuvant chemosensitivity in osteosarcoma.

articles.title: Reliability of the L3 Transverse Process as a Landmark for Lumbar Spine Enumeration Across Different Vertebral Segmentation Patterns: A Retrospective CT Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Vertebral numbering on limited lumbosacral imaging is difficult when the thoracic or lumbar count varies. The L3 transverse process has been proposed as a landmark because it is often the longest, but this has not been tested across segmentation patterns. This study assessed whether L3 as the level bearing the longest transverse process is independent of thoracic and lumbar vertebral count on whole-spine CT. Methods: Of 499 trauma CT examinations with confirmed numbering, all 49 non-standard thoracolumbar formulas were included, together with 17 C7T12L5 spines that remained after exclusion of transitional and numerical anomalies at every level (n = 66). Bilateral lumbar transverse-process lengths were measured on multiplanar reconstructions. The longest level was identified by morphological and presacral numbering. Associations with thoracic patterns (C7T11, n = 10; C7T12, n = 43; C7T13, n = 13) were tested with the Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test and Monte Carlo simulation. Nine primary analyses were adjusted with the Holm procedure. Inter-observer agreement was assessed with an intraclass correlation coefficient. Results: In this enriched cohort, L3 was the longest level in 45/66 cases (68.2%) based on the single longest transverse process and 49/66 (74.2%) based on bilateral mean length. These percentages are not population prevalences. Within the C7T12 group, the corresponding proportions were 76.7% and 83.7%, respectively. By bilateral mean length, L3 was longest in 30.0% of C7T11, 83.7% of C7T12 and 76.9% of C7T13 cases (exact p = 0.003, Holm-adjusted p = 0.014). The single-process association did not remain significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.058). The 22nd presacral vertebra showed a comparable dependence on thoracic pattern (Holm-adjusted p = 0.041 and 0.001 for the single-process and bilateral-mean analyses, respectively). Inter-observer ICC was 0.88 for individual transverse-process lengths and 0.93 for bilateral means. Conclusions: Neither L3 nor the 22nd presacral vertebra is a segmentation-independent marker of lumbar identity. Full-spine counting remains necessary when precise numbering is required.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Two Real-Time PCR Techniques for the Detection of Congenital Syphilis in Umbilical Cord Blood.
articles.abstract: Background: Syphilis remains a relevant public health problem and continues to be associated with adverse perinatal outcomes. In newborns, conventional serological tests are often difficult to interpret due to maternal antibody transfer and the immaturity of the neonatal immune response. These limitations have led to increasing interest in molecular approaches as complementary diagnostic tools. Methods: This pilot study compared two real-time PCR methodologies for detecting Treponema pallidum DNA in umbilical cord blood: a SYBR Green-based qPCR targeting the polA gene and a TaqMan probe-based qPCR targeting the TpN47 gene. Thirty samples from neonates born to mothers with suspected gestational syphilis were analyzed under standardized conditions. Analytical performance and reproducibility were evaluated before application to clinical samples. Results: Both assays showed stable amplification and acceptable reproducibility. During standardization, the TaqMan assay reached a lower detection limit. However, when applied to clinical samples, the SYBR Green approach identified more positive cases (10/30 vs. 4/30), highlighting differences between analytical performance and behavior in clinical samples. Conclusions: Both methods were suitable for molecular detection of T. pallidum. However, their performance differed in neonatal samples, indicating that analytical sensitivity alone may not predict clinical detection capacity. Molecular testing in cord blood may provide complementary information when serological results are inconclusive.

articles.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been significantly improved through deep learning techniques; however, the lack of interpretability remains a major challenge for clinical adoption. Methods: This study proposes an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-driven framework for multiclass brain tumor classification using a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) and four transfer learning models, namely ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0. The models were trained and evaluated on a publicly available brain MRI dataset consisting of glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumor classes. Their classification performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and confusion matrix analysis. To enhance transparency and interpretability, Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP were used to visualize and quantify the regions contributing to the classification decisions. Results: Experimental results state that the transfer learning models consistently outperformed the CNN by learning more discriminative feature representations while producing more localized and interpretable explanations. The agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP confirms that the proposed models predominantly relied on tumor regions rather than irrelevant background information, thereby improving the interpretability and reliability of the diagnostic predictions. Conclusions: The proposed framework provides an effective and explainable computer-aided diagnosis system that supports trustworthy deep learning-based brain tumor classification and has the potential for decision-making.

articles.title: Assessing the Positive Predictive Value of International Classification of Diseases Code K55.0 for Identifying Acute Mesenteric Ischaemia.
articles.abstract: Background: Acute mesenteric ischaemia (AMI) includes acute superior mesenteric artery (SMA) thrombosis and embolism, venous AMI, and non-occlusive mesenteric ischaemia (NOMI). Patients with AMI are identified using the International Classification of Diseases (tenth revision (ICD-10)) code K55.0 (acute vascular disorders of the intestine). Reporting of outcomes depends on reliable case identification. Methods: A retrospective review of all patients assigned with ICD-10 code K55.0 at a tertiary university hospital between 1st January 2023 and 31st December 2025 was performed. Medical records and imaging findings were scrutinized to validate the diagnosis. Results: Among 218 patients assigned ICD-10 code K55.0, 117 (53.7%) had confirmed AMI and 198 (90.8%) had acute gastrointestinal ischaemia. Patients with NOMI (n = 30, 53.3%) had a higher bowel resection rate than patients with embolic SMA occlusion (n = 21, 23.8%; p = 0.039) or venous AMI (n = 15, 6.7%; p = 0.012). The in-hospital mortality rate was lower in patients with venous AMI (6.7%) than in patients with NOMI (66.7%; p < 0.003) or thromboembolic SMA occlusion (42.9%; p = 0.015). Conclusions: The positive predictive value for AMI using ICD-10 code K55.0 was 53.7%, underscoring the need for validated case identification. The heterogeneity of diagnoses captured by this code supports consideration of a more granular ICD coding system. A conceptual proposal is presented for further discussion and validation.

articles.title: DSR-VGG: A Lightweight Depthwise Separable Residual VGG Architecture for Nasopharyngeal Histopathological Image Classification.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Deep convolutional neural networks achieve strong histopathological image-classification performance but often require substantial computational resources. This study proposes DSR-VGG, a lightweight Depthwise Separable Residual VGG architecture for nasopharyngeal histopathological image classification. Methods: DSR-VGG comprises six Depthwise Separable Blocks with residual projection shortcuts, global average pooling, dropout regularization, and a classification layer. An inverse-frequency weighted random sampling strategy was used to address severe class imbalance. The primary evaluation used 88,002 nasopharyngeal histopathology patches from four classes: Normal, lymphoid hyperplasia, nasopharyngeal inflammation, and nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Training was repeated using three random seeds, with supplementary public datasets used to assess cross-dataset architectural robustness. Results: Across three runs, DSR-VGG achieved 99.764 ± 0.049% accuracy, 99.070 ± 0.365% balanced accuracy, and 99.219 ± 0.215% macro-F1. The model contained only 0.528 million parameters, required approximately 0.31 GFLOPs, and achieved 2.38 ms single-image inference latency under the stated GPU benchmarking conditions. Although several baseline architectures achieved marginally higher accuracy, DSR-VGG maintained competitive predictive performance with substantially lower computational complexity. Conclusions: DSR-VGG provides a favorable accuracy-complexity trade-off for histopathological patch classification. However, patient-/WSI-disjoint evaluation, independent multi-center validation, and whole-slide assessment remain necessary before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Clinical and Imaging Patterns of Neurological Involvement in Intravascular Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Objective: Neurological involvement in intravascular large B-cell lymphoma (IVLBCL) is heterogeneous, prompting us to characterize its diverse manifestations through an integrated clinical and neuroimaging framework. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 55 patients with pathologically confirmed IVLBCL diagnosed at Peking Union Medical College Hospital between January 2015 and June 2023. Pretreatment neurological involvement was identified in 29 patients based on attributable clinical and/or imaging findings after exclusion of more plausible alternative causes. Patterns were assigned primarily by clinical manifestations, supported by available imaging. Results: Six potentially overlapping clinicoradiologic patterns were identified. The stroke-like pattern (n= 5) comprised acute focal deficits with corresponding infarct-like or ischemic lesions. The encephalopathy pattern (n= 11) included cognitive decline, behavioral changes, impaired consciousness, and/or seizures, with or without infarct-like lesions or white matter hyperintensities. Three patients developed encephalopathic features following stroke-like presentations, including one with concomitant myelopathy. The mass-like pattern (n= 1) presented with headache and vomiting associated with enhancing lesions and surrounding edema. Myelopathy (n= 3) was characterized by lower-limb weakness with spinal cord-localizing signs, whereas radiculoneuropathy (n= 5) manifested as bilateral lumbosacral nerve-root involvement with weakness, sensory abnormalities, and reduced reflexes. Corresponding MRI abnormalities were absent in two patients with encephalopathy and one with myelopathy. The asymptomatic pattern (n= 8) comprised patients with imaging abnormalities but no neurological symptoms or signs. A total of 19 of 22 patients evaluable for treatment response achieved complete remission. Conclusions: Neurological involvement in IVLBCL comprises overlapping and evolving clinicoradiologic presentations, with variable correspondence between symptoms and imaging findings. This descriptive framework may help clinicians recognize its diverse manifestations and consider IVLBCL when the clinical course or imaging findings remain insufficiently explained.

articles.title: Prediction of Spinal Pain Intensity from Perception-Dependent Stimulation Thresholds and Patient Characteristics: A Regression and Machine Learning Approach.
articles.abstract: Background and Objective: Spinal pain is highly prevalent, yet clinically accessible tools for pain quantification remain limited. This study evaluated whether machine learning (ML) algorithms using StimaWELL 120MTRS-derived scores alongside demographic variables can predict self-reported spinal pain intensity and compared their performance against linear mixed model (LMM)-based associations. Methods: Seventy-eight adults with spinal pain (44 female, 34 male; mean age 43.08 ± 11.50 years) were assessed under two electrode configurations: opposing electrode (OE) and adjacent electrode (AE). Self-reported pain was measured using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS). Repeated measures correlation, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), LMM, and eight ML algorithms were applied to evaluate predictive capacity. Results: Repeated measures correlations between StimaWELL scores and NPRS were negligible and non-significant (OE: r = -0.003, p = 0.970; AE: r = 0.015, p = 0.876), with ICC values indicating poor agreement (OE: 0.364; AE: 0.452). LMM revealed no statistically significant fixed effects for either configuration. Despite this, ML algorithms achieved moderate predictive performance, with Extra Trees and CatBoost yielding the highest tolerance-based accuracy (up to 73-74% for AE-based models). The AE StimaWELL score was the dominant predictor across feature importance analyses, followed by body weight and height. Conclusions: ML algorithms extracted the predictive signal from StimaWELL 120MTRS data where LMM found none, highlighting nonlinear relationships between device-derived scores and pain intensity. AE configuration demonstrated superior predictive performance. These findings suggest that StimaWELL 120MTRS may provide complementary quantitative information in spinal pain assessment, pending external validation in larger, diverse populations.

articles.title: Clinicopathological Significance of CD44 and CD117 Expression/Co-Expression in Invasive Ductal Breast Cancer.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Breast cancer (BC) is the most common cancer in women worldwide and has a high mortality rate; thus, it is essential to determine the relevance of not only standard clinicopathological parameters, but also non-standard parameters, such as cancer stem cell molecular markers CD44 and CD117. These factors could possibly be used to predict cancer aggressiveness and metastasis. The present study aimed to evaluate the significance of CD44 and CD117 expression/co-expression in relation to clinicopathological parameters, molecular cancer subtypes, and axillary lymph node (ALN) status in invasive ductal cancer (IDC) of the breast. Methods: The investigation included 136 patients with IDC in whom radical mastectomy had been performed. The level of CD44 and CD117 expression in cancer tissue (high or low) was determined via immunohistochemical analysis. Results: High CD117 expression and CD44/CD117 co-expression were closely linked to a higher Ki-67 index (p < 0.001; p = 0.003, respectively) and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) (p < 0.001; p < 0.001, respectively). Multivariate linear regression analysis revealed that CD44/CD117 co-expression was independently associated with a higher number (p < 0.001), as well as a higher percentage (p = 0.005) of metastatic ALNs. Conclusions: This study showed that CD44/CD117 co-expression is an independent predictor of a higher number and percentage of metastatic ALNs in IDC and may have potential prognostic value.

articles.title: Potential Influence of NUCB2 Genetic Variants on the Clinicopathological Features of Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most commonly diagnosed cancer type worldwide in males and the ninth among females, and it is a primary cause of cancer-associated death. The adipokine nesfatin-1, initially discovered in hypothalamic neurons, is produced by the precursor NUCB2 gene. The relationship between NUCB2 polymorphisms, behavioral risk factors that facilitate cancer, and HCC is still unknown. Methods: Four NUCB2 genetic polymorphisms were investigated in 822 normal controls and 411 patients with HCC using qPCR. The GTEx portal was used to assess the association between NUCB2 genetic variants and expression. NUCB2 levels in patients with HCC were evaluated using TCGA data. Results: Relative to the wild-type GG genotype, the AA genotype at the NUCB2 SNP rs214101 was associated with an augmented risk of distant metastasis and vascular invasion. The GA and AA genotypes at rs214101 were also associated with an increased likelihood of vascular invasion among smoking HCC patients compared to those carrying the GG genotype. Notably, GTEx data uncovered that the AA homozygous genotype was correlated with remarkably higher NUCB2 levels than those observed in individuals with the rs214101 GG genotype in lymphocytes and whole blood samples. TCGA data revealed that HCC patients exhibited higher NUCB2 expression in tumorous compared to non-tumorous liver tissue. Conclusions:NUCB2 SNP rs214101 may be associated with HCC progression and metastasis.

articles.title: Upper Extremity Fractures in Older Medicolegal Patients: Radiologic Characteristics and Factors Associated with Permanent Functional Impairment.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Upper extremity fractures in older adults may cause lasting disability, but radiologic characteristics associated with permanent functional impairment in medicolegal populations remain unclear. We described these injuries and examined associated factors. Methods: Of the 94 initially identified patients, seven with unavailable follow-up examination records were excluded. This single-center retrospective cohort included 87 medicolegal patients aged ≥65 years with 104 radiographically confirmed upper extremity fractures evaluated between 2015 and 2024. The outcome was permanent functional impairment documented in a definitive medicolegal report after clinically appropriate follow-up. An exploratory, clinically selected logistic regression model included age, multiple fractures, displacement, and intra-articular extension. Results: Median age was 70 years, 70.1% were men, and interpersonal violence was the most frequent mechanism (51.7%). Permanent functional impairment was identified in 35 patients (40.2%; 95% CI, 30.6-50.7). Multiple upper extremity fractures (aOR, 3.79; 95% CI, 1.01-14.25), at least one displaced fracture (aOR, 4.52; 95% CI, 1.30-15.73), and at least one intra-articular fracture (aOR, 3.94; 95% CI, 1.13-13.77) were associated with impairment in the adjusted model; no statistically significant association was detected for age. Conclusions: Fracture burden and morphology were associated with permanent functional impairment; an age association was not detected in this relatively small, age-concentrated cohort. Standardized reporting of fracture number, displacement, and intra-articular extension may support long-term follow-up and medicolegal evaluation.

articles.title: Three-Part MRI Morphology of the Human Masseter Muscle: A Part-Dominance Classification.
articles.abstract: Background: A simple MRI-based framework for describing part-specific dominance patterns in the human masseter muscle is lacking. This study aimed to characterize its MRI-visible parts and develop a preliminary part-dominance classification. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study analysed 58 clinical MRI examinations, comprising 116 masseter muscles with complete bilateral visualization. The three MRI-visible parts were identified on T2-weighted 3D coronal source images. Thickness and length were measured using a predefined study procedure, and each muscle was assigned a part-dominance type according to which part was thickest. Results: Three distinct parts were identified in all 116 muscles. The inferior part was thickest in 81 muscles (69.8%), the coronoid part in 31 (26.7%), and the middle part in 4 (3.4%). The inferior part was also the longest segment. Conclusions: In this dataset, the human masseter muscle showed a three-part MRI morphology. The findings provide a basis for a preliminary part-dominance classification for anatomical and radiological description. Functional, biomechanical, and clinical correlations require prospective validation.

articles.title: Dynamic Xenon-Enhanced Spectral CT Imaging to Evaluate Regional Lung Function in an In Vivo Rabbit Model.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pulmonary diseases exhibit spatially heterogeneous functional and structural abnormalities that are inadequately represented by conventional lung function testing. This pilot study investigates dynamic xenon-enhanced dual-energy CT (Xe-DECT) for a multiparametric assessment of lung ventilation and tissue. Methods: Four mechanically ventilated rabbits were scanned during washout of 70% xenon in oxygen using multibreath imaging with a clinical DECT both before (baseline) and after methacholine administration (post-MCh). Tracheal Xe concentration (CXe) and flow were monitored using mass spectrometry and pneumotachometry to estimate specific ventilation (sV˙ms) and end-expiratory lung volume (EELVms). DECT-derived xenon concentration and tissue density images (mg/mL) were obtained by material decomposition, yielding sV˙DECT and EELVDECT, respectively. Agreement with mass spectrometry and differences between baseline and post-MCh were assessed. Results: The baseline sV˙DECT and EELVDECT agreed with the mass spectrometry, with mean differences of 0.6 min-1 [-0.2 min-1, 1.4 min-1] and 0.6 mL [-6.7 mL, 7.9 mL], respectively. Following MCh administration, the mean differences increased to -2.9 min-1 [-4.1 min-1, -1.6 min-1] for sV˙ and 1.3 mL [-15.3 mL, 12.8 mL] for EELV. Post-MCh, sV˙DECT decreased from 8.6 ± 1.6 min-1 to 3.7 ± 0.9 min-1 (p = 0.034) and EELVDECT from 29.3 ± 1.0 mL to 27.0 ± 1.3 mL (p = 0.036), whereas sV˙ms (p = 0.308) and EELVms (p = 0.653) showed no substantial changes. Regional analysis revealed that sV˙DECT in well-ventilated regions matched tracheal sV˙ms. Conclusions: Dynamic Xe-DECT imaging enabled spatial and quantitative assessments of specific ventilation and tissue densities in an in vivo rabbit model. This technique allowed detection of focal alterations that remained undetected by tracheal measurements.

articles.title: AI-Based Automated Segmentation of the Mandibular Cortex and Mental Foramen for Radiomorphometric Measurement on Panoramic Radiographs: A Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the feasibility of a YOLOv5-based model for automated segmentation of these structures and automated measurement of mandibular cortical width (MCW) and panoramic mandibular index PMI. Methods: Five hundred panoramic radiographs were retrospectively collected. The mandibular cortex and the right and left mental foramina were annotated with polygon labels as three separate classes and verified by an experienced radiologist; intra- and inter-observer reliability was evaluated on a random 10% subset. A YOLOv5s-seg model was trained for 500 epochs and evaluated on an independent, patient-level test set. Model performance was quantified with precision, recall, F1 score, Dice coefficient, mean intersection over union (mIoU), and mean average precision (mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95). Results: The model achieved a precision of 0.94, a recall of 0.82, and an F1 score of 0.88 (mAP@0.5 = 0.86; mAP@0.5:0.95 = 0.52). The Dice coefficient was 0.93 for the mandibular cortex and 0.80 and 0.75 for the right and left mental foramina, respectively. In the side-level paired agreement analysis (62 measurable sides from 44 test-set patients), the ICC was 0.89 (95% CI: 0.84-0.93) for MCW, with a mean bias of +0.08 mm and 0.87 for PMI, with a mean bias of +0.01. Conclusions: YOLOv5 showed high agreement with expert observers for mandibular cortex segmentation and moderate agreement for the mental foramen, supporting the technical feasibility of automated MCW and PMI measurement. Because missed mental foramen detections reduce the number of measurable sites, automated measurement should be combined with a verification step.

articles.title: Association of Complete Blood Count Parameters and Systemic Inflammatory Indices with Early Surfactant Administration in Preterm Infants.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The decision to administer surfactant therapy to preterm newborns is typically based on clinical respiratory findings, oxygen requirements, and the level of respiratory support. The aim of this study was to assess the association of admission complete blood count parameters and derived systemic inflammatory indices with surfactant administration within the first 24 h of life in preterm infants born at ≤32 weeks of gestation, and to evaluate their discriminative performance. Methods: This single-center, retrospective observational cohort study included 100 preterm infants with a gestational age of ≤32 weeks who were admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit between 1 January 2025 and 31 March 2026. The results of the initial complete blood count and blood gas analysis, obtained as part of routine clinical care at admission, were recorded. Systemic inflammatory indices, including the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), red cell distribution width-to-platelet ratio (RPR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and mean platelet volume-to-platelet ratio (MPV/PLT), were calculated from the complete blood count results. The primary outcome was surfactant administration within the first 24 h of life. Associated factors were evaluated using logistic regression analysis, and the discriminative performance of continuous variables was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results: Surfactant was administered to 45 infants (45%) within the first 24 h of life. Infants who received surfactant had lower gestational ages, birth weights, 1- and 5 min Apgar scores, partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PCO2), hemoglobin levels, and hematocrit values. No significant differences were observed between groups in NLR, PLR, MLR, RPR, SII, or MPV/PLT. In multivariable analysis, lower gestational age (OR = 0.65; 95% CI: 0.50-0.84; p = 0.001), small-for-gestational-age (SGA) status (OR = 4.61; 95% CI: 1.25-16.91; p = 0.021), and lower 1 min Apgar score (OR = 0.67; 95% CI: 0.46-0.96; p = 0.031) were independently associated with early surfactant administration. Hemoglobin was not independently associated with early surfactant administration after adjustment. In the ROC analysis, the AUC values were 0.804 for birth weight, 0.776 for gestational age, 0.694 for hemoglobin, 0.677 for hematocrit, and 0.640 for PCO2. Conclusions: Lower gestational age, SGA status, and lower 1 min Apgar score were independently associated with early surfactant administration. No significant associations were observed between the evaluated complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices and early surfactant administration. Although hemoglobin and hematocrit levels differed between groups, hemoglobin was not independently associated with the outcome after adjustment. ROC analysis provided descriptive estimates of the discriminative performance of gestational age, birth weight, hemoglobin, hematocrit, and PCO2.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Delayed Graft Function in a Universal Hypothermic Machine Perfusion Program: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hypothermic machine perfusion (HMP) has established itself as an evidence-based and effective preservation strategy to improve graft function and survival after kidney transplantation. It demonstrated a reduction in the incidence of delayed graft function (DGF) compared to static cold storage. However, the risk factors for DGF that persist when HMP is used universally are poorly defined. The aim of this study was to explore donor and recipient factors associated with DGF in a universal HMP kidney transplantation program. Methods: A single-center retrospective cohort included 134 consecutive deceased-donor kidney transplants (KTs). The primary endpoint was the incidence of DGF. Secondary endpoints included functional results, complications and survival during follow-up. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were performed to identify factors associated with DGF. Graft and patient survival were estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method. Graft function was assessed by serum creatinine (Cr) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Results: The overall incidence of DGF was 9.7% (n = 13). When stratified by donor type, the incidence of DGF was 13.3% (n = 10) for donors after brain death (DBD) and 5.1% (n = 3) for donors after circulatory death (DCD). DGF was associated with impaired graft function during follow-up, a longer in-hospital stay and a higher incidence of major complications. Donor diabetes mellitus (DM) (adjusted OR 4.09, 95% CI 1.14-14.62; p = 0.030) and lower recipient pre-KT hemoglobin (Hb) (adjusted OR 0.62 per 1 g/dL, 95% CI 0.41-0.93; p = 0.021) were associated with DGF; Firth penalized estimates were consistent, but the association with donor DM was attenuated after adjustment for donor age and CIT (OR 3.38, 95% CI 0.91-12.00). Overall graft and patient survival were 99.3% and 100%, respectively, at 12 months, and 99.3% and 96.9%, respectively, at 36 months. Conclusions: Lower recipient pre-KT Hb was consistently associated with DGF in this exploratory cohort, whereas the association with donor DM was attenuated after adjustment for donor age and CIT. Within this universal HMP program, DGF incidence did not differ significantly between DBD and DCD grafts; however, in the absence of an SCS comparator, this observation cannot be attributed to HMP. Given the limited number of events (n = 13), the lack of detailed donor DM information and the absence of PRA data, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Association Between the Modified Renal Angina Index and Major Adverse Kidney Events at 90 Days in Critically Ill Adults: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Adult modified Renal Angina Index (mRAI) formulations predict acute kidney injury, but their association with major adverse kidney events at 90 days (MAKE90) remains unclear. We examined the association in critically ill adults without established chronic kidney disease (CKD). Methods: This retrospective cohort included 250 adults admitted to a tertiary intensive care unit (ICU) between December 2023 and April 2025. mRAI was calculated from data available at ICU admission. MAKE90 was defined as death, renal replacement therapy, or persistent renal dysfunction within 90 days. We used logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic analysis, and nested-model comparisons. Results: Admission mRAI was higher in patients with MAKE90 than in those without MAKE90 (median 10 [IQR 5-20] vs. 3 [IQR 1-6]; p < 0.001). After adjustment for SOFA score and sepsis, mRAI remained associated with MAKE90 (adjusted OR per point from the linear model, 1.073; 95% CI, 1.032-1.116). Spline analysis demonstrated a significant nonlinear association (p = 0.004), indicating that the per-point OR should be interpreted as a summary estimate rather than a constant effect across the score range. The AUC of mRAI was 0.752 (95% CI, 0.691-0.814), higher than that of admission AKI stage (0.653) and not significantly different from APACHE II (0.702) or SOFA (0.718). Adding mRAI to SOFA and sepsis raised the AUC from 0.735 to 0.782. Conclusions: In critically ill adults without established CKD, higher admission mRAI remained associated with MAKE90 after adjustment for SOFA score and sepsis and showed moderate discrimination. External validation in larger, independent cohorts is needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Detector-Stage Failures Account for Most of the Increase in the External Deficit of a Box-Prompted Glioma Segmentation Pipeline on BraTS-Africa: A Three-Arm Decomposition Across Two External Cohorts.
