articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: When a box-prompted segmentation pipeline loses accuracy on new data, the detector proposing the box or a later stage may be responsible; this study measured which. Methods: A real-time detection transformer (RT-DETR) feeding the Segment Anything Model 2.1 was compared with a detector-free model (MedSAM3 with a low-rank adapter) on whole-tumor Dice in 158 patients with glioma: held-out Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) 2020 cases (n = 24), the RHUH-GBM glioblastoma cohort (n = 39), and BraTS-Africa (n = 95, glioma presumed). Giving the segmenter the ground-truth box splits the Dice gap between the systems into a detector-stage term and a residual. Results: The detector-stage term was +0.006 Dice on held-out cases, +0.018 on RHUH-GBM, and +0.091 on BraTS-Africa. Its increase over the held-out value was +0.0854 [95% CI +0.0450, +0.1303] on BraTS-Africa (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001) and, after correction of a preprocessing fault, +0.0120 [-0.0062, +0.0295] on RHUH-GBM, which was not resolved. On BraTS-Africa, it came mainly from slices without a detector box. No residual change was resolved. Conclusions: On BraTS-Africa, the detector stage accounted for most of the increase in the pipeline's gap; on RHUH-GBM, no increase was resolved. The decomposition should be measured per cohort.

articles.title: Two-Stage Probabilistic Classification of Sperm Identity and Morphology.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: From a histological and embryological perspective, sperm identification and morphological classification are distinct assessment tasks. This study compares image-level error distributions and review-referral outcomes between separately trained conditional components and direct three-class learning. Methods: Following duplicate-image and label audits, 2947 images from the Sperm Morphology Image Dataset (SMIDS) were analyzed without changing the source labels. Logistic regression models using frozen EfficientNet-B0 features were evaluated using five outer and three inner cross-validation folds that preserved 2942 similarity groups. Final class probabilities, component probabilities, and outcomes at matched review volumes were compared. Results: Overall accuracy was 83.98% for the two-stage model and 84.80% for the direct model. Misclassification of non-sperm images as sperm decreased from 94 (direct) to 77 (two stage), whereas misclassification of true sperm images as non-sperm increased from 82 to 141. When each model referred 973 images for review, accuracy among the remaining 1974 images was 93.67% and 94.48%, respectively. Conclusions: The two models differed in the trade-off between erroneously including non-sperm material and excluding assessable sperm images. Overall and selective accuracy were higher for the direct model. The study provides a framework for jointly evaluating these two error directions on the same test images and at matched review volumes in preliminary histomorphological assessment.

articles.title: Precision Cervical Reconstruction: A State-Dependent Operative Framework for Cervical Insufficiency.
articles.abstract: Cervical insufficiency is conventionally classified by indication and named operative technique, yet neither fully describes the cervix as a dynamically remodeling, mechanically loaded, and structurally heterogeneous organ or specifies the reconstruction delivered. This Perspective proposes precision cervical reconstruction, a conceptual state-informed framework linking five domains: dynamic cervical phenotype, state-based operative assessment, mechanical objective, intended configuration, and achieved reconstruction. Safety and biological eligibility constrain the entire pathway. In the ultrasound-indicated context, morphology and trajectory complement cervical length, whereas elastography and other biomechanical measurements remain research-oriented. In emergency states, bulging extent, membrane reducibility, and cervical rim adequacy separately describe procedural complexity and feasibility. The framework distinguishes clinical observation, plausible mechanical interpretation, and testable hypothesis; it does not replace established indications or constitute a validated treatment-selection algorithm. Suture height, axial separation, sequence, material, tissue engagement, and membrane relationship are treated as reportable variables, and double-level cerclage is considered one conditional configuration rather than a universally superior strategy. Current comparative evidence does not establish consistent benefit from an additional suture or identify a validated state in which vertically distributed support improves outcomes. The immediate contribution is a standardized reasoning and reporting structure that separates indication from state, intended configuration from achieved reconstruction, and mechanistic hypotheses from clinical effectiveness. Prospective studies should establish measurement reliability, procedural fidelity, safety, and associations with maternal and neonatal outcomes before testing state-guided care.

articles.title: Serum Free Fatty Acid-Based Diagnostic Index for Cervical Cancer Including High-Risk HPV-Negative Cases: An Independent Validation Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cervical cancer (CC) is usually caused by high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV); however, some hrHPV-negative cases are undetectable by current screening programs. We evaluated a previously established diagnostic model based on serum free fatty acids (FFAs) in an independent cohort including hrHPV-negative CC. Methods: We analyzed serum FFAs from 101 patients with CC (16 hrHPV-negative), 60 healthy donors, and 16 patients with benign gynecological diseases, none of whom were included in the previous study, and gene expression levels of fatty acid metabolism-related enzymes in 64 surgical CC and five normal cervix samples. Results: Levels of nine FFAs differed between CC and the non-cancer groups but not between hrHPV-negative and hrHPV-positive CC. Gene expression levels of acetyl-CoA carboxylase 1, fatty acid synthase, stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1, and monoacylglycerol lipase were increased in CC compared with normal tissues, with no significant differences between hrHPV-negative and hrHPV-positive CC. The previous model (diagnostic index = -5.631 + 0.030 × (stearic acid) + 9.188 × (dihomo-γ-linolenic acid)) distinguished CC from the non-cancer groups (area under the curve, 0.969). At the pre-specified cut-off value, sensitivity was 97.0% (hrHPV-negative CC, 93.8%) and specificity in healthy donors was 58.3%; at the cut-off value derived in this cohort, these were 82.2% (93.8%) and 98.3%, respectively. In hrHPV-negative CC, the positivity rate exceeded those of squamous cell carcinoma antigen, carcinoembryonic antigen, and CA125. Conclusions: The serum-FFA-based diagnostic model detected CC, including hrHPV-negative cases, in an independent cohort. With calibration of the cut-off value, this approach may complement existing HPV-based testing.

articles.title: Histopathological Spectrum and Yield of Advanced Neoplasia in Opportunistic Colonoscopy Without Organised Screening: A Single-Centre Cross-Sectional Study from Western Romania.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Organised colorectal cancer screening is still being introduced in Romania, and the yield of opportunistic colonoscopy outside it is poorly documented. Our primary aim was to describe the histopathological spectrum and the yield of advanced neoplasia in an opportunistic colonoscopy service; a secondary, exploratory aim was to describe self-reported lifestyle items in a questionnaire subgroup. Methods: This study represents a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of consecutive colonoscopies (June 2023-June 2024) at a county hospital outside organised screening, restricted to patients from whom material reached histopathology; the comparison group therefore comprises patients whose sampled lesions were benign, not patients without neoplasia. Advanced neoplasia was defined histologically as adenocarcinoma or adenoma with high-grade dysplasia, without the 10 mm size criterion. A convenience subgroup self-completed a locally developed, unvalidated questionnaire before the procedure; its items were tested against advanced neoplasia and adenocarcinoma with false discovery rate correction. Results: Among 274 patients, 45 (16.4%) had adenocarcinoma, 139 (50.7%) adenoma and 72 (26.3%) advanced neoplasia; per examination (n = 978), detection was 4.6% for adenocarcinoma and 7.4% for advanced neoplasia. Forty-four of 45 carcinomas were graded as moderately differentiated, and no serrated lesion was separately reported. Age was associated with advanced neoplasia (OR 1.34 per decade, 95% CI 1.01-1.79). Questionnaire data were available for only 79 patients (28.8%), among whom adenocarcinoma was more frequent than among non-respondents (26.6% vs. 12.3%). In this subgroup, obesity was inversely (OR 0.07, 95% CI 0.02-0.28) and reported weight loss positively (OR 6.77, 2.26-20.30) associated with advanced neoplasia, and two coffee items were inversely associated; processed meat, dairy, aspirin and supplement use were not associated after correction. Conclusions: Opportunistic colonoscopy at this centre recovered a high proportion of carcinoma, consistent with symptom-driven presentation, and the reporting of serrated lesions and tumour grade requires standardisation. The questionnaire findings rest on a small, selected subgroup and are hypothesis-generating only. The inverse obesity association is most plausibly explained by selection of the comparison group and of respondents, and none of the associations identifies a risk factor.

articles.title: Association Between Local Ascending Aortic Elastic Properties and Left Ventricular Global Longitudinal Strain in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis: A Cross-Sectional Case-Control Echocardiographic Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Multiple sclerosis (MS) has been associated with subclinical cardiovascular involvement, including impaired myocardial deformation and increased arterial stiffness. However, the local elastic properties of the ascending aorta and their relationship with subclinical left ventricular (LV) longitudinal dysfunction remain insufficiently characterized in MS. Methods: In this prospective cross-sectional study, 67 adults with MS and 67 age-matched controls without cardiovascular disease underwent standardized transthoracic echocardiography. Aortic strain, distensibility and stiffness index (β) were derived from M-mode ascending aortic diameters and simultaneous brachial blood pressure, and LV global longitudinal strain (GLS) was measured by two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography. Multivariable linear regression was utilized to assess associations. Results: LV ejection fraction was similar between groups, while LV GLS was less negative in MS (-17.49 ± 1.81% vs. -19.85 ± 1.80%, p < 0.001). Patients with MS had lower aortic strain (7.54 ± 3.66% vs. 12.91 ± 3.84%) and distensibility (3.81 [2.23-6.06] vs. 5.95 [4.90-9.26] × 10-3 mmHg-1) and a higher stiffness index (4.77 [3.10-7.10] vs. 3.44 [2.31-4.05]) (all p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, and body mass index, MS remained independently associated with aortic strain, distensibility, and stiffness index. Within the MS group, aortic strain was independently associated with LV GLS after adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, Expanded Disability Status Scale score and LDL cholesterol (B = -0.276, standardized β = -0.558, p < 0.001). LV GLS was independently associated with log-transformed distensibility (B = -1.021, p = 0.011) and stiffness index (B = 1.095, p = 0.014). Conclusions: Patients with MS show concurrent, inter-related impairment of local ascending aortic elasticity and LV longitudinal deformation despite preserved ejection fraction. Further studies are needed to establish the temporal sequence and prognostic relevance of these findings.

articles.title: Shared Enrichment of the MUC5B Variant rs35705950 in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis and Fibrotic Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis: Evidence from a Russian Cohort.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The MUC5B rs35705950 polymorphism is the strongest common genetic risk factor for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), whereas its role in fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis (fHP) remains incompletely characterized, particularly in Eastern European cohorts. This study aimed to evaluate the distribution of MUC5B rs35705950 genotypes and alleles in Russian patients with IPF and fHP and to assess their association with disease susceptibility using a large external Russian reference dataset. Methods: The study included 114 patients with interstitial lung disease: 50 with IPF and 64 with fHP. Genotyping was performed using a custom PCR-restriction fragment length polymorphism assay. Genotype and allele frequencies were compared with an external reference dataset from the National Genetic Initiative of Russia (n = 89,261). Association analyses were performed under dominant T-carrier and allelic models. Results: The rs35705950 T allele was significantly enriched in both IPF and fHP compared with the external reference dataset. T-carrier genotypes were detected in 52.0% of patients with IPF and 42.2% of patients with fHP, compared with 18.9% in the reference dataset. T-allele frequencies were 28.0%, 26.6%, and 10.0%, respectively. In the dominant model, T-carrier status was associated with increased odds of IPF (OR = 4.65; 95% CI, 2.56-8.46; p < 0.001) and fHP (OR = 3.13; 95% CI, 1.83-5.29; p < 0.001). The direct comparison between IPF and fHP was inconclusive because of limited statistical power. Conclusions: In this Russian clinical cohort, the rs35705950 T allele was more frequent in patients with IPF and fHP than in the external Russian reference dataset. These findings provide regional replication of previously reported associations. The study did not assess causal mechanisms or diagnostic performance.

articles.title: Generative Forecasting of Longitudinal 3D-OCT Under Anti-VEGF Therapy for Diabetic Macular Edema.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Forecasting the individual anatomical response to anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy from optical coherence tomography (OCT) could support the management of diabetic retinal disease. Direct volumetric generation is difficult because treatment-associated change is local while most of the retina is stationary, so generative models regress to the mean and blur retinal layers. Methods: We propose a two-stage framework that decouples baseline anatomy from longitudinal change in 3D-OCT. A Retinal Response Tokenizer compresses the latent residual between baseline and follow-up volumes into discrete action tokens via Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ), and a conditional decoder renders the follow-up volume from baseline features and these tokens. An Action Transformer predicts the tokens from the baseline scan, the follow-up interval, and baseline covariates. Results: On the OLIVES trial cohort (diabetic retinopathy and macular edema; 738 test pairs from five held-out eyes), our method achieved the highest structural similarity in every test eye (SSIM 0.657 vs. 0.543-0.623) and tracked the central subfield thickness (CST) change measured by a frozen regressor (Δ-r=0.88). In a five-fold cross-validation over 52 eyes, it improved PSNR over an identity copy by 1.27 dB (95% CI 0.93-1.57) and reduced the CST change error by 10.5 μm (95% CI 3.1-19.4). Conclusions: Prospective validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Prospective External Validation of the HFA-ICOS Baseline Cardiovascular Risk Classification in Women with Breast Cancer Receiving Anthracycline-Containing Therapy in a Central Asian Cohort.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The HFA-ICOS baseline cardiovascular risk classification was developed to standardize pretreatment risk stratification before potentially cardiotoxic cancer therapy, but its external performance across diverse populations remains incompletely characterized. We prospectively evaluated its performance in women with breast cancer receiving anthracycline-containing therapy in Central Asia. Methods: This prospective single-center external validation study used data from the PREDICATE cohort (ISRCTN12628444). Participants were classified at baseline as being at low, moderate, high, or very high cardiovascular risk according to the HFA-ICOS classification before treatment and outcome ascertainment; the high- and very-high-risk categories were pooled for analysis because of small numbers. Participants underwent serial cardiovascular surveillance, including echocardiographic assessment of left ventricular ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain, together with serial cardiac biomarker measurements. The primary outcome was cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD), defined according to the 2022 ESC cardio-oncology criteria. Results: The analysis included 108 participants. CTRCD occurred in 43 of 108 participants (39.8%). The observed proportion of participants who developed CTRCD increased from 30.0% in the low-risk group to 47.5% in the moderate-risk group and 75.0% in the high/very-high-risk group (p = 0.026). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significant separation of CTRCD-free survival across HFA-ICOS risk categories (log-rank χ2 = 10.12; p = 0.006). Compared with the low-risk group, the hazard of CTRCD was higher in the moderate-risk group (hazard ratio [HR], 2.16; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.13-4.13) and high/very-high-risk group (HR, 3.59; 95% CI, 1.42-9.11). Discrimination was modest (area under the curve, 0.630; 95% CI, 0.530-0.724). Conclusions: The HFA-ICOS classification demonstrated a clear ordinal gradient in CTRCD risk and significant time-to-event separation but showed limited discrimination at the individual-patient level. It may guide initial risk stratification but should be complemented by longitudinal cardiovascular surveillance rather than used as a stand-alone predictor.

articles.title: Development and External Validation of Machine Learning Models for Ionized Calcium Estimation in Hypoalbuminemia.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning models for predicting ionized calcium levels in patients with hypoalbuminemia, compare their performance with classical correction formulas and unadjusted total calcium levels, and assess their transportability through external validation. Methods: In a retrospective development cohort of 14,745 adults with hypoalbuminemia, XGBoost and ordinary least squares (OLS) models used total calcium, albumin, total protein, and eGFR and were evaluated with nested cross-validation. Frozen models were then applied without recalibration to an independent external cohort of 2751 patients using the same analyzer platforms. Results: Development XGBoost performance was R2 = 0.500 and AUC-ROC = 0.798 (95% CI 0.788-0.807), with 98.5% sensitivity and 26.0% specificity. External R2 was 0.397 for XGBoost and 0.363 for OLS. External AUC-ROC was 0.818 (95% CI 0.791-0.845) for XGBoost, 0.823 (0.797-0.850) for OLS, and 0.819 (0.791-0.845) for total calcium. Threshold-matched and exploratory decision-curve analyses showed no clear incremental XGBoost advantage over total calcium. Conclusions: Machine learning models provided useful continuous ionized-calcium estimates and high sensitivity for hypocalcemia detection, although specificity was low. In independent external validation, hypocalcemia discrimination was comparable to unadjusted total calcium. The models should be considered complementary rather than substitutes for measured ionized calcium, and further multicenter and prospective evaluation is warranted.

articles.title: AdaSwitch3D: Reliability-Aware Human-in-the-Loop Artificial Intelligence for Breast Tumor Segmentation in Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced MRI Across Unseen Centers.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Deep learning models for breast tumor segmentation in dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) often lose accuracy at centers that did not contribute training data. We investigated whether case-wise routing between two low-resource adapted models, combined with an uncertainty-based review-prioritization signal, behaves consistently under severe cross-center domain shift. Methods: Using the four public collections of the MAMA-MIA dataset (DUKE, ISPY1, ISPY2, NACT; 1231 cases), we performed four-fold leave-one-center-out experiments in which each held-out center contributed only five labeled cases and a pool of unlabeled scans. We compared source-only transfer, five-shot fine-tuning, and teacher-student self-training with AdaSwitch3D, which routes each case between the two adapted branches using 17 label-free features and produces a heuristic review-prioritization signal. The complete pipeline-data splits, five-shot selection, training, adaptation, router construction, and referral calibration-was repeated with five random seeds, and each seed was evaluated once on 80 untouched test cases (400 seed-specific test observations). Results: Across five independent repetitions, mean Dice was 0.325 ± 0.051 for source-only transfer, 0.353 ± 0.052 for five-shot fine-tuning, 0.372 ± 0.047 for teacher-student adaptation, and 0.377 ± 0.057 for AdaSwitch3D; a validation-selected per-center strategy reached 0.376 ± 0.044. AdaSwitch3D exceeded five-shot fine-tuning in all five seeds and teacher-student adaptation in four, but the difference between AdaSwitch3D and teacher-student adaptation was small (mean +0.005) and varied by seed, while inference required both branches (approximately twice the single-model time). Observed test referral rates ranged from 23.8% to 56.3% against a 20% validation target, and low-Dice (<0.20) failure capture ranged from 21.7% to 71.8%. In the prespecified case-level analysis of seed 42, AdaSwitch3D improved on source-only transfer and five-shot fine-tuning (Holm-adjusted p=0.021 for each), whereas the comparison with teacher-student adaptation did not provide evidence of a difference (Holm-adjusted p=0.508). Conclusions: Absolute segmentation accuracy remained low, the incremental benefit of case-wise routing over teacher-student adaptation was small and seed-dependent, and referral behavior was unstable across repetitions. The principal finding is therefore that cross-center adaptation, case-wise model selection, and heuristic referral remain sensitive under limited target supervision. AdaSwitch3D should be interpreted as an exploratory case study of these challenges rather than as a clinically validated segmentation or referral system.

articles.title: Extravascular Cyanoacrylate "Embolization" for the Treatment of Vesico-Vaginal Fistula: A Minimally Invasive Alternative.
articles.abstract: Vesico-vaginal fistula (VVF) is a debilitating complication commonly occurring after gynecologic surgery and frequently associated with significant morbidity and impaired quality of life. Although surgical repair remains the standard treatment, management strategies remain heterogeneous, while conservative approaches often require prolonged urinary diversion with variable success rates. We report a case of persistent post-surgical VVF successfully treated with image-guided embolization using N-butyl cyanoacrylate methylsulfone (NBCA; Glubran 2, GEM; Viareggio, Italy) through a transvesical catheter-based approach after failure of conservative management. This case illustrates the potential role of interventional radiology in the management of selected VVFs, suggesting that image-guided fistula embolization may represent a minimally invasive treatment option when conservative management fails and surgical reintervention is undesirable or can be deferred.

articles.title: Ligamentary Leiomyoma Presenting as a Mons Pubis Mass: A Rare Clinical Manifestation.
articles.abstract: We present the case of a 47-year-old woman (gravida II, para II; both deliveries by cesarean section) with a rare case of a ligamentary leiomyoma appearing as a mass lateral of the mons pubis. The lesion had first been noticed approximately seven months prior to the first examination at our institution and had shown continuous growth since its initial detection. Apart from occasional mild discomfort, no additional symptoms such as skin changes, discharge, or systemic complaints were reported. Based on the clinical and sonographic findings, no suspicion of malignancy was raised during the preoperative assessment, and elective surgical excision was scheduled for both diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. The described lesion presented intraoperatively as a ligamentary leiomyoma and subsequent histopathological examinations confirmed the diagnosis.

articles.title: Determinants and Prognostic Value of Persistent Congestion Assessed by Venous Excess Ultrasound Score in Acute Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Background: Reliable quantification of systemic venous congestion in acute heart failure (HF) has become feasible with the advent of the venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) score, informing therapeutic management. Nevertheless, the determinants of the VExUS score trajectory during hospitalization and the prognostic implications of persistent subclinical congestion at discharge remain poorly defined. Methods: Consecutive patients admitted for acute HF were prospectively enrolled (n = 418, 73.3 ± 11.8 years old, 59.1% male). VExUS scores were assessed at admission and prior to discharge to categorize the patients into three groups: non-congested (persistent score of 0; n = 81), improved (score reduction of ≥1 point; n = 214), and non-improved (persistent congestion without score reduction; n = 123). Baseline clinical data were collected and all the patients had a transthoracic echocardiogram on admission. All patients were followed up post-discharge and the primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization. Results: Patients with non-improved VExUS exhibited a higher burden of right-sided remodeling and dysfunction including larger right chambers, lower right ventricle (RV) systolic function indices, higher RV systolic pressures and a higher prevalence of severe tricuspid regurgitation (all p < 0.001). Severe tricuspid regurgitation was the sole independent predictor of VExUS non-improvement (OR 2.86, 95% CI 1.51-5.45, p = 0.001). Non-improved VExUS (HR 1.77; 95% CI 1.17-2.67; p = 0.007), severe tricuspid regurgitation (HR 1.88; 95% CI 1.16-3.02; p = 0.010) and intravenous furosemide dose (HR 1.00; 95% CI 1.00-1.01; p = 0.011) were independent predictors of the composite primary endpoint. Inclusion of non-improved VExUS provided incremental prognostic value over models including clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic parameters (Δχ2= 9.22; p = 0.007). Conclusions: VExUS non-improvement throughout hospitalization marks patients with worse primary endpoint Severe tricuspid regurgitation emerges as an independent determinant of VExUS non-improvement which is independently associated with poor long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Survival Outcomes in Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis in the Tafamidis Era: Real-World Evidence from Greece.
articles.abstract: Background: Diagnoses of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) have increased in recent years, with a growing proportion of patients being identified at earlier disease stages. However, temporal trends in ATTR-CM diagnosis and survival during the tafamidis era in the Greek population remain largely unknown. Methods: This retrospective study included 75 patients with ATTR-CM treated with tafamidis. Baseline demographic, clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic characteristics were assessed, and survival outcomes were subsequently evaluated. Results: Among 75 tafamidis-treated patients, 14 deaths (19%) occurred during a median follow-up of 20 months [IQR 10.0-30.5] with an estimated 30-month survival of 75%. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly poorer survival among patients aged ≥80 years (log-rank p = 0.013), those with NYHA class III-IV (log-rank p = 0.018), and across progressively more advanced NAC stages I-III (global log-rank p < 0.001). In contrast, survival did not differ significantly according to LVEF <50% versus ≥50% (log-rank p = 0.863) or maximal wall thickness ≥15 mm versus <15 mm (log-rank p = 0.801). After Holm correction across five comparisons, only NAC stage remained statistically significant (adjusted p < 0.001). Conclusions: In this real-world Greek cohort of patients with ATTR-CM treated with tafamidis, the estimated 30-month all-cause mortality was 25% and more advanced NAC stage was associated with poorer survival.

articles.title: Optimizing Portal Venous Phase Acquisition Quality of Contrast-Enhanced CT in Oncology.
articles.abstract: Background: Portal venous phase (PVP) contrast-enhanced CT is a cornerstone for response assessment in early-phase oncology trials, yet contrast-enhancement phase timing remains insufficiently monitored across sites. We assessed PVP timing using a validated artificial intelligence (AI) quality control tool (CECT-QC). Methods: In this retrospective multicenter study, 402 CT examinations from 402 patients enrolled in phase I oncology trials across three European institutions were analyzed using CECT-QC, which quantifies aortic and portal venous enhancement to classify contrast-enhancement phase. The primary analysis included 335 standard CT examinations. Optimal PVP classification was compared (i) across institutions, (ii) before vs. after French regulatory changes impacting contrast delivery, and (iii) across scanner technologies (photon-counting CT [PCCT] vs. standard CT). Results: Among the 335 standard CT examinations included in the primary analysis, 53.1% (178/335) were classified by CECT-QC as optimal PVP. Optimal PVP rates were 39.0% (32/82) at Institution A, 56.9% (87/153) at Institution B, and 59.0% (59/100) at Institution C, with a significant adjusted institutional association (p = 0.039). No significant temporal association was observed before versus after the legislative change (p = 0.716). At Institution A, standard CT was associated with higher odds of optimal PVP classification than PCCT (OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.07-4.68; p = 0.031), while PCCT showed higher aortic and portal venous attenuation (both p < 0.001). Conclusions: Approximately half of standard CT examinations in phase I oncology trials were classified as optimal PVP. Classification varied significantly across institutions and by scanner technology, whereas no significant temporal association was observed before versus after the legislative change. These findings support continued quality-control monitoring, protocol harmonization, and adaptation of classification tools to emerging CT platforms.

articles.title: Deep Learning for Root Canal Filling Quality on Panoramic Radiographs with Detection and Grading Measured Separately.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The European Society of Endodontology names two filling requirements with a reproducible link to outcome: apical extent and material density. Panoramic radiography shows every treated tooth in one exposure, but systems built on it pool detection with grading into one average precision that hides which of the two has failed. This study graded both axes on panoramic radiographs with detection and discrimination measured separately. Methods: In this retrospective study, two specialist endodontists read 830 panoramic radiographs independently, and a third adjudicated every disagreement. The 1668 root fillings of 806 radiographs were encoded into a binary and an axis-resolved label space, and 160 radiographs were locked away before training. The remaining 646 were evaluated under five-fold cross-validation, with four architectural interventions tested alongside input resolution. Localisation was measured by class-agnostic recall, grading by matched-box accuracy and per-axis F1, and label spaces were compared by paired bootstrap. Results: Refining the label space left detection recall at 92.6% against 93.1%, but cost 11.41 points of matched-box accuracy, 8.20 to 14.46, and 12.16 on the locked test. Asked the same binary question, it fell 1.12 points behind in cross-validation and 3.13 points behind on the locked test, where the binary decision reached 76.25% sensitivity given detection and 68.75% specificity at the best of ten readings, or 71.52% and 68.21% at the development-selected one. At 1024 pixels, no architectural change improved density F1 beyond the 8.2 to 10.8 points this design can detect, and enlarging training from 207 to 517 radiographs gained 11.42, 5.92 to 16.56. Conclusions: Separating detection from grading locates the cost of a finer label space in discrimination, bounds four architectural interventions below the resolution of this design, and supports a binary but not an axis-resolved quality decision as a potential teaching and audit aid, pending external validation beyond this single centre, not a screening test.

articles.title: Subclinical Cardiovascular Adaptation in Uncomplicated Monochorionic Twin Pregnancies: Echocardiographic and Cardiac Biomarker Findings.
articles.abstract: Background: Although cardiac involvement is well characterized in complicated monochorionic (MC) pregnancies, whether subtle cardiovascular changes occur in uncomplicated pregnancies remains unclear. We characterized fetal and neonatal cardiovascular adaptation using echocardiography and cardiac biomarkers. Methods: In this prospective longitudinal cohort, 76 dichorionic (DC) and 68 uncomplicated monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) twins underwent fetal echocardiography at 28 weeks and neonatal echocardiography within 72 h after birth. Cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP) were assessed at delivery. Analyses used generalized estimating equations to account for within-pregnancy clustering and Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons. Associations between cardiac biomarkers and fetal echocardiographic parameters and interactions with chorionicity and gestational age at birth were also evaluated. Results: MCDA fetuses showed trends toward a higher cardiothoracic ratio, lower right ventricular fractional shortening and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion, and a higher prevalence of tricuspid regurgitation (TR) compared with DC fetuses. In the early neonatal period, nominal differences in interventricular septal thickness and tissue Doppler indices did not persist after FDR correction. Cord-blood hs-cTnI (21.83 vs. 12.29 pg/mL; p = 0.015, FDR-adjusted p = 0.027) and NT-proBNP (1327.6 vs. 887.6 pg/mL; p = 0.018, FDR-adjusted p = 0.027) concentrations were higher in MCDA twins. After gestational age adjustment, the association with hs-cTnI remained relatively stable, whereas that with NT-proBNP was attenuated; neither remained significant after FDR correction (p = 0.116 for both). The TR-hs-cTnI association differed by chorionicity (p for interaction < 0.001, FDR-adjusted p < 0.004) and persisted after adjustment for gestational age at birth. Conclusions: Conventional echocardiographic measures of cardiac structure and function appear to be largely preserved in uncomplicated MCDA twins during fetal life and the early neonatal period. Higher cord-blood hs-cTnI and NT-proBNP may suggest subclinical myocardial stress associated with monochorionicity, although gestational age-adjusted findings warrant caution.

articles.title: Stage Migration, Treatment Patterns, and Machine Learning-Based Prediction of 12-Month Mortality in Lung Adenocarcinoma Across the COVID-19 Era: A SEER Population-Based Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The COVID-19 pandemic coincided with widespread disruption of cancer care. We examined changes in lung adenocarcinoma presentation and outcomes across the COVID-19 era and whether diagnosis-time information identifies patients at risk of early death. Methods: Adults with microscopically confirmed lung adenocarcinoma diagnosed during 2018-2023 were identified from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results 17 Registries database and grouped into three diagnostic periods. Logistic regression, time-varying Cox, and Fine-Gray models evaluated stage, metastasis, surgery, delay, and mortality. Four machine-learning algorithms using only diagnosis-time variables were developed (2018-2021; n = 87,281) and temporally validated (2022; n = 22,012). Results: Among 133,306 patients, COVID-19 versus pre-COVID-19 differences were significant but small in absolute terms: stage IV disease 47.9% versus 47.4% (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.03; 95% CI, 1.00-1.06), organ-specific metastasis 45.8% versus 44.4% (OR, 1.06; 1.04-1.09), and treatment delay exceeding 90 days 11.1% versus 10.2% (OR, 1.11; 1.06-1.17). Post-COVID-19 (2022-2023) diagnosis showed less advanced disease but substantially longer delay (14.5% versus 10.2%; OR, 1.45; 1.39-1.52). Gradient boosting achieved a 2022 ROC AUC of 0.840 (0.834-0.845); it flagged 46.8% of patients and correctly flagged 81.6% of those who died, against 44.0% and 75.4% for stage IV classification. Conclusions: COVID-era changes in stage and metastatic presentation were small in absolute terms, whereas the increase in treatment delay was larger and persisted. A diagnosis-time model modestly improved identification of early death beyond stage alone, flagging 28 more patients per 1000, of whom 21 died within the year. These findings support further evaluation; external validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Reliability-Audited Explainable AI for Multi-Class Skin-Lesion 2 Triage Under Cross-Device Domain Shift.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Reliable skin-lesion AI requires evaluation beyond the development distribution. This study assessed whether a source-developed multi-class system preserves discrimination and reliability when transferred to an unseen smartphone-acquired domain. Methods: A source-only multimodal four-class classifier was developed using HAM10000 and Derm7pt and evaluated on PAD-UFES-20 without target-domain adaptation. Reliability was assessed using class-specific calibration, uncertainty-based error detection, class-conditional conformal prediction, selective classification, demographic subgroup auditing, controlled ablation, and an independent DDI out-of-distribution (OOD) and explainability (XAI) audit. Results: Across five prespecified seeds, macro-F1 decreased from 74.27 ± 1.36% on the source domain to 54.92 ± 2.60% on PAD-UFES-20. Calibration, conformal efficiency, and selective coverage also deteriorated externally, although macro-AUROC remained comparatively preserved. The independent DDI audit showed limited OOD separation, while explanation stability was interpreted only as descriptive evidence. Ablation analysis indicated that clinical metadata contributed importantly to external performance. Conclusions: Internally reproducible discrimination did not guarantee reliable external behavior. These findings support explicit external reliability auditing and specialist-supervised selective decision support before cross-device deployment.

articles.title: Lower Serum SCCA2 Detectability in Chronic Spontaneous Compared with Chronic Inducible Urticaria: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Squamous cell carcinoma antigen 2 (SCCA2; SERPINB4) is an IL-4/IL-13-inducible epithelial serpin that can inhibit human mast-cell chymase, providing a potential link to mast-cell-mediated inflammation. To our knowledge, SCCA2 has not previously been studied in chronic urticaria; we hypothesized that circulating SCCA2 would differ among chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), chronic inducible urticaria (CIndU), and healthy controls. Methods: This prospective, single-center observational study included 36 patients with CSU, 35 with provocation-confirmed CIndU, and 45 healthy controls; atopic or allergic diseases were excluded in all groups. Baseline blood sampling was performed before treatment initiation. Serum SCCA2 was measured by ELISA. Because quantification below the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ, 0.16 ng/mL) was not validated, primary interpretation used assay-defined categories based on the limit of detection (LOD, 0.09 ng/mL) and LLOQ; continuous analyses were exploratory. Results: SCCA2 detectability was 22.2% in CSU, 62.9% in CIndU, and 68.9% in controls. Detectability was lower in CSU than in CIndU and controls (Holm-adjusted p = 0.0015 and p < 0.001), whereas CIndU and controls did not differ (p = 0.637). Among patients, below-LOD SCCA2 was associated with CSU (OR 5.92, 95% CI 2.09-16.81) and remained associated after adjustment for total IgE, eosinophil count, and CRP (aOR 4.73, 95% CI 1.59-14.08; p = 0.005). Conclusions: Serum SCCA2 showed a CSU-associated low-detectability pattern, whereas CIndU and controls did not differ significantly. Because most estimates were below the LLOQ, findings represent differences in assay-defined detectability rather than validated concentrations. Independent validation is required.

articles.title: Association Between Admission Calculated Serum Osmolality and New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Non-ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
articles.abstract: Background: New-onset atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common complication of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and is associated with adverse outcomes. We evaluated whether admission calculated serum osmolality is associated with new-onset AF in NSTEMI. Methods: This retrospective study included 656 eligible NSTEMI patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) between March 2021 and April 2022. Only patients in sinus rhythm at admission whose blood sample preceded any AF episode were analyzed. Osmolality was calculated as 2 × sodium + glucose/18 + blood urea nitrogen/2.8. Prespecified logistic models were assessed for discrimination, bootstrap internal validation, calibration, and incremental value. Results: New-onset AF developed in 136 patients (20.7%). Osmolality was higher in patients with AF (297.4 ± 8.9 vs. 291.6 ± 15.7 mOsm/kg, p < 0.001). In the complete-case model (n = 570; 130 events), osmolality was associated with AF (adjusted OR 1.565 per 10 mOsm/kg, 95% CI 1.102-2.223; p = 0.012). Adding osmolality increased the AUC from 0.927 to 0.933 (DeLong p = 0.081; likelihood-ratio p = 0.012; optimism-corrected AUC 0.924). The association was attenuated without renal-function adjustment (p = 0.060). Conclusions: Admission calculated serum osmolality was associated with new-onset AF in NSTEMI patients undergoing PCI, but its incremental predictive value was modest. External validation is required.

articles.title: Size Matters: A Large-Scale, Real-World Dataset of Smartphone-Based Obstructive Sleep Apnea Screening in the General Population.
articles.abstract: Background: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a highly prevalent sleep-related breathing disorder that remains substantially underdiagnosed and is causally linked to cardiovascular and metabolic morbidity. Clinical diagnosis relies on the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) derived from polysomnography (PSG) or home sleep apnea testing. Low-threshold, clinically validated screening tools that can be used repeatedly outside a clinical setting may help to reduce underdiagnosis and to capture longitudinal information. Methods: We describe a real-world dataset generated by a medical device-grade, smartphone-only OSA screening application (Snorefox M) that calculates the AHI from nocturnal breathing sounds. All users who provided informed consent for the research use of their anonymized data between March 2023 and December 2025 were included. The diagnostic performance of the application had previously been validated against parallel PSG. Additional post hoc analysis of classification performance at additional AHI thresholds, together with the linear correlation between the app-derived and PSG-derived AHI are described. Results: The dataset comprises 239,132 measurements from 31,647 consenting adults. A total of 14,351 users contributed at least two valid nights, yielding 221,820 nights of longitudinal screening data. Across all attempted measurements, 96.5% yielded a valid analysis result. The mean per-measurement AHI was 14.3 (median 11.8, SD 11.0). Voluntary, self-reported demographic information was available for a subgroup of 8092 users (mean age 54.4 years, mean ESS score 7.2). Against PSG, the application detected moderate-to-severe OSA (AHI ≥ 15) with a sensitivity of 0.91 and a specificity of 0.83, and severe OSA (AHI ≥ 30) with a sensitivity of 0.93 and a specificity of 0.97. The app-derived AHI correlated strongly with the PSG-derived AHI (Pearson r = 0.80, p < 0.001). The app-derived AHI discriminated against the PSG reference with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.951 for severe OSA (AHI ≥ 30), 0.925 for moderate-to-severe OSA (AHI ≥ 15) and 0.877 for the AHI ≥ 10 threshold. Conclusions: This is, to our knowledge, the largest longitudinal dataset of unsupervised, real-world OSA screening from a general adult population using a clinically validated, low-threshold smartphone tool. Smartphone-based screening can complement established diagnostic pathways, support pre-clinical triage and generate longitudinal data not accessible through single-night testing, while self-selection and the unsupervised nature of data capture constrain representativeness. By introducing this resource, this work provides the basis for the in-depth analyses of demographics, symptom-result concordance and night-to-night variability.

articles.title: Quantitative Glandular Tissue Component Assessment on Breast Ultrasound Using an Anatomically Constrained Deep Learning Framework.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Glandular tissue component (GTC) has been incorporated into BI-RADS v2025 as part of breast tissue composition assessment, but visual grading remains subjective and does not provide continuous quantification. We developed and evaluated an ROI-guided, anatomically constrained deep learning framework for quantitative GTC assessment on breast ultrasound. Reader performance was compared between unaided and AI-assisted sessions. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 421 ultrasound images from 114 women for model development and 150 women for clinical evaluation. The framework segmented fibroglandular tissue (FGT) and glandular tissue to calculate continuous GTC percentage and assign the corresponding image-derived P1-P4 category. Four model configurations were compared during model development using patient-level five-fold cross-validation. Standalone AI performance was evaluated against expert consensus. Two senior and two junior radiologists assessed the clinical cohort without and with AI assistance, separated by a 4-week washout period. Results: During model development, the anatomical constraint markedly improved anatomical consistency while quantitative error and segmentation performance remained comparable. In the clinical cohort, continuous GTC percentage showed an MAE of 3.88 percentage points and strong correlation with the reference percentage (Spearman ρ = 0.957, p < 0.001). Exact P1-P4 agreement was 78.0%, adjacent agreement was 99.3%, and weighted κ was 0.888. However, 26 of 36 reference P4 cases (72.2%) were underestimated. Exact agreement was significantly higher for all four readers in the second, AI-assisted session than in the first, unaided session (all p < 0.001). Conclusions: The framework enabled anatomically consistent continuous GTC quantification and categorical assessment on individual breast ultrasound images.

articles.title: Multimodal Cataract Severity Classification from AS-OCT Examination Reports: Analyzing the Complementarity of B-Scan Images and A-Scan Profiles.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Deep learning on anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) has been applied mainly to nuclear cataract. This study evaluated whether the A-scan profile in Anterion reports adds information to the B-scan image for classifying nuclear (N), cortical (C), and posterior subcapsular (P) cataract severity. Methods: B-scan images and A-scan profiles were extracted from 1416 reports of 691 patients. LOCS III grades were converted into three levels (None/Mild, Moderate, Advanced); inter-observer agreement was excellent (weighted κ 0.84-0.97). Image and profile encoders were combined using five fusion strategies and evaluated with patient-level 5-fold cross-validation. Results: Adding the A-scan profile improved F1 for N (+0.030) and P (+0.094) but not for C (-0.002). All fusion strategies outperformed single-modality models and performed comparably (average F1 0.514-0.531). For P, the gain was largest at the Moderate grade (F1 0.183 to 0.336), and masking the profile segment containing the posterior capsule caused the largest drop. B-scan line profiles could not replace the device-provided profile, and most misclassifications occurred between adjacent grades. Conclusions: The A-scan profile provided a useful incremental contribution, particularly for N and P, in this single-center dataset. The approach may be useful in retrospective and multi-center settings, but this remains to be demonstrated.

articles.title: Near-Infrared Spectroscopy-Guided Selective Distal Perfusion in Femoral Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We evaluated the feasibility of a near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS)-guided selective strategy based on a single absolute regional tissue oxygen saturation (rSO2) threshold and described clinically overt limb ischemia. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 110 adults receiving femoral venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation between April 2020 and December 2024. All underwent bilateral lower-extremity NIRS monitoring. In 83 patients, distal perfusion catheter (DPC) placement was triggered by rSO2 < 40% in the cannulated limb or clinically evident limb ischemia; 27 received routine prophylactic DPC placement at cannulation. Primary endpoints were DPC avoidance and clinically overt limb ischemia. Results: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) accounted for 64.5% of patients. Under the selective strategy, 45/83 patients (54.2%; exact 95% CI, 42.9-65.2%) avoided DPC placement, with no clinically overt limb ischemia (0/45; exact 95% CI, 0-7.9%). Limb ischemia occurred in 2/83 versus 2/27 patients (2.4% versus 7.4%; risk difference, -5.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -21.1 to +3.0; p = 0.252). Because threshold crossing triggered DPC placement, the reported threshold characteristics reflect the operation of the management protocol rather than independent diagnostic accuracy. Conclusions: A single-threshold NIRS-guided selective strategy was feasible in this ECPR-dominant population, allowing just over half of patients to avoid prophylactic DPC placement. No clinically overt limb ischemia was observed in this subgroup, but the upper 95% confidence limit of 7.9% precludes a definitive safety conclusion. Prospective studies are needed to assess limb ischemia risk and refine selection criteria.

articles.title: Is Eligibility Enough? Pretreatment Prediction of Failure to Reach a Second Cycle of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA Radioligand Therapy.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Current guidelines define no absolute contraindication to prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radioligand therapy (RLT), yet some patients receive only a single cycle. We aimed to characterize this single-cycle attrition (SCA) and derive an exploratory pretreatment risk score predicting it. Methods: Seventy consecutive patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer treated with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT at one center (2022-2025) were reviewed; 58 were assessable. SCA was defined as permanent non-initiation of a second cycle. The analyses employed false-discovery-rate-adjusted nonparametric comparisons, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), Kaplan-Meier and univariable Cox methods, with optimism-corrected bootstrap internal validation. Results: SCA occurred in 12 of 58 patients (20.7%), owing to death or rapid clinical deterioration (n = 8) or grade 3-4 hematotoxicity (n = 4); all 12 died (median overall survival 3 months). Higher C-reactive protein (CRP), lower lymphocytes and hemoglobin, and higher alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and prostate-specific antigen (PSA) separated the groups (all q < 0.05). The five-item Single-Cycle Attrition Risk (SCAR-5) score (one point each: CRP ≥ 16.5 mg/L, lymphocytes ≤ 1.39 × 109/L, hemoglobin ≤ 9.6 g/dL, ALP ≥ 191 U/L, PSA ≥ 34.2 ng/mL) discriminated SCA with an optimism-corrected area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.88 (apparent AUC 0.95, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.89-0.99). No SCA occurred below score 3 (0/39; upper 95% confidence limit 9.0%); a score ≥ 3 identified all events (sensitivity 100%, 95% CI 74-100; specificity 85%, 95% CI 71-94) and was associated with shorter survival (univariable Cox hazard ratio 3.94, 95% CI 2.01-7.74). Conclusions: One in five patients who initiated RLT did not proceed beyond the first cycle. SCAR-5, an exploratory score derived from routine pretreatment laboratory values, stratified risk of early treatment attrition; external prospective validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Uterine Fibroids in Pregnancy: Maternal, Obstetric, and Neonatal Outcomes in a Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Uterine fibroids are the most common benign tumors in women of reproductive age, and their coexistence with pregnancy is becoming increasingly frequent as maternal age at first pregnancy rises. Objective: The objective of this study was to evaluate the impact of uterine fibroids on obstetric and neonatal outcomes and, secondarily, the effect of pregnancy on fibroid growth. Study Design: This retrospective observational study included 1512 pregnant women, 136 of whom had uterine fibroids, who were followed at a university hospital. Ultrasound examinations were performed before pregnancy (T0) and during the first (T1), second (T2), and third (T3) trimesters. Fibroid number, size, location, and ultrasound characteristics according to FIGO classification were recorded. Obstetric complications, mode of delivery, and neonatal outcomes were analyzed according to fibroid type and size. Fibroid growth throughout pregnancy was also evaluated. Results: Among 1512 pregnant women followed between 1 January 2024 and 30 November 2025, 136 patients (9.0%) had uterine fibroids. A positive family history of fibroids was identified in 36% of cases. Gestational complications were infrequent overall, although gestational hypothyroidism was significantly more common among women with fibroids, whereas preeclampsia and postpartum hemorrhage were significantly less frequent in univariable analysis. Vaginal delivery was less frequent in the fibroid group, while operative vaginal delivery and cesarean section were significantly more common. Fetal growth restriction (FGR) and umbilical venous pH also differed significantly between groups. In multivariable analysis adjusted for maternal age, BMI, parity, ART, smoking, chronic hypertension, and diabetes, the association with cesarean section was attenuated (aOR 1.47, 95% CI 0.93-2.32), whereas lower PPH rates persisted (aOR 0.34, 95% CI 0.14-0.84) and a slight inverse association with umbilical venous pH remained detectable (β -0.01, p = 0.01). Exploratory stratification according to FIGO classification (3-4 vs. 5-7) showed significant differences in PPH, cesarean section, FGR, and LGA. Repeated-measure analysis demonstrated progressive fibroid growth in maximum diameter during pregnancy compared with preconceptional measurements (T0) (p < 0.001), with substantial enlargement already observed by the second trimester and fibroids ≤5 cm exhibiting greater relative growth at T2 compared with T0 than larger lesions (+18% vs. +7%; p = 0.03). Conclusions: Uterine fibroids were not consistently associated with adverse obstetric or neonatal outcomes, although careful obstetric surveillance remains warranted. Pregnancy was associated with progressive fibroid growth, particularly in smaller lesions and during early gestation.

articles.title: Multimodal Detection of a Minute Uterine Cornual Lesion in Cervical Clear Cell Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Cervical clear cell carcinoma (CCC) is a rare human papillomavirus (HPV)-independent adenocarcinoma. A 73-year-old woman presented with postmenopausal bleeding. Ultrasonography demonstrated a cervical mass and a 5.0 × 5.0 mm right cornual nodule. On 3.0-T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), the cornual lesion measured 5.2 × 5.3 mm and, like the cervical tumor, showed high signal intensity on diffusion-weighted imaging (b = 1000 s/mm2). 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) demonstrated intense uptake in the cervical mass (30.6 × 29.2 × 41.2 mm; SUVmax 10.4) and in the spatially separate right cornual nodule (5.2 × 5.1 mm; SUVmax 14.6), without FDG-avid nodal or distant metastatic disease. The concordant identification of the cornual lesion by ultrasonography, MRI, and PET/CT prompted multidisciplinary reassessment and radical hysterectomy to obtain definitive pathological characterization of both lesions. Histopathology demonstrated clear cell carcinoma at both sites; however, because molecular, genomic, or clonality analyses were not performed, their biological relationship remains uncertain. All 30 examined lymph nodes and the surgical margins were negative. The cervical primary was staged as pT1b3 pN0 cM0 (FIGO 2018 stage IB3). The patient received four cycles of postoperative chemotherapy with paclitaxel plus cisplatin. At 14 months after surgery, gynecological examination and pelvic MRI showed no evidence of recurrence. This case highlights the complementary roles of ultrasonography, MRI, and 18F-FDG PET/CT in characterizing a minute spatially separate uterine lesion while underscoring the need for cautious interpretation when the relationship between lesions cannot be established.

articles.title: Multi-Locus Molecular Findings in Pediatric-Onset Inherited Metabolic Disorders: An Eight-Year Series of Outsourced Genomic Testing in Taiwan.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Outsourced genomic testing can identify additional findings in patients with inherited metabolic disorders (IEMs), including lysosomal storage diseases. We examined these findings in a selected Taiwanese series. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 13 patients referred during 2018-2025 with a reported or suspected metabolic diagnosis. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was initially used mainly after inconclusive testing or for incompletely explained phenotypes and was used more broadly later. The original registry also records whole-genome sequencing (WGS) for two included patients. We distinguished reported gene-level findings from diagnoses supported by pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants at each locus. Results: The 13 patients had 18 reported gene-level findings comprising 27 variants. Five met the inclusive multi-locus definition (38.5%; exact 95% confidence interval, 13.9-68.4%). The proportion was 30.8% after excluding candidate gene-disease associations and 7.7% when P/LP variants in the expected zygosity were required at both loci using the later case-summary classifications. Several classifications differed between the original registry and later summaries. These estimates are not directly comparable with the published 4.9% benchmark because ascertainment and diagnostic definitions differ. Enzyme replacement therapy was documented in three patients, including one treated before WES. Conclusions: Unexplained features may warrant evaluation for an additional diagnosis. The selected sample and differing levels of diagnostic certainty limit estimates of confirmed multi-locus disease.

articles.title: Aortic Endograft Infection After COVID-19: A Single-Centre Case Series and a Proposed Descriptive Clinical-Radiological PET/CT Staging Framework.
articles.abstract: Background: Aortic endograft infection (AEI) after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is rare but life-threatening. The Management of Aortic Graft Infection Collaboration (MAGIC) criteria define infection, but there is no standard way to report the extent of infection. We describe patients who developed AEI after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and propose a descriptive clinical-radiological PET/CT staging framework. Methods: Retrospective, single-centre case series of EVAR patients who underwent [18F] fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG PET/CT) between 2020 and 2023. Six index patients (Group A) were managed for AEI after PCR-confirmed COVID-19. Five reference patients without COVID-19, imaged during the same period for suspected infection at another site (Group B, n = 2) or malignancy (Group C, n = 3), were included to describe endograft uptake in the absence of AEI; they were not matched controls. Each patient was classified according to MAGIC, with the finding supporting each criterion recorded. Each endograft was assigned a descriptive clinical-radiological stage (0-III): Stages 0-II were defined by PET/CT uptake pattern and anatomical extent, and Stage III by an additional imaging-defined (e.g., endograft limb thrombosis) or clinical (sepsis) complication, recorded separately. Results: Mean age was 76 years (9 men). Of the six index patients, one (Case 6, organism cultured from the explanted endograft) met the MAGIC definition of diagnosed AEI and five met that of suspected AEI. All six presented with fever, and every index patient had at least one additional source of bacteraemia or cause of immunosuppression, including corticosteroids given for COVID-19 pneumonia. Five had iliopsoas abscess. Four index endografts were classified as Stage III (clinical complication, sepsis, in all four; imaging-defined complication, endograft limb thrombosis, also in one) and two as Stage II; all five reference endografts were Stage 0. The median interval from COVID-19 to AEI diagnosis was 14 months (IQR 10-16), and from EVAR to PET/CT 15 months (IQR 4-35). Three index patients died (two infection- or aorta-related), and all three Group C patients died of malignancy progression. Conclusions: This case series describes late AEI, frequently with iliopsoas involvement, in patients with prior COVID-19 and multiple other risk factors. The design does not permit any conclusion as to whether COVID-19 contributes to endograft infection. The proposed descriptive clinical-radiological PET/CT framework may help standardise the reporting of disease extent alongside MAGIC-based diagnosis but requires validation in larger, independent cohorts before any diagnostic or therapeutic use.

articles.title: Premature Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease in a Middle Eastern Cohort: A Risk-Accumulation Perspective on Shared Determinants and Temporal Exposure Patterns.
articles.abstract: Background: Premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) represents a growing clinical and public health concern, particularly in regions with a high burden of modifiable risk factors. Whether premature ASCVD reflects a distinct pathophysiological entity or an earlier manifestation of shared risk exposures remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the clinical profile of premature ASCVD and to examine its relationship with conventional cardiovascular risk factors within a Middle Eastern cohort. Methods: This pooled observational analysis included 2763 adults with established ASCVD derived from multiple cardiovascular registries and a prospective cohort. Premature ASCVD was defined using sex-specific age thresholds (<55 years in men and <65 years in women). Multivariable logistic regression analyses, including sex-stratified models, were performed to evaluate associations between premature presentation and cardiovascular risk factors, including smoking, family history, lipid parameters, and cardiometabolic comorbidities. Results: Among 2763 participants in the pooled clinical cohort, 1335 (48.3%) met the study definition of premature ASCVD. Compared with later-onset disease, premature ASCVD was strongly associated with current smoking, family history of premature cardiovascular disease, and a more atherogenic lipid profile, including higher levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. In contrast, later-onset ASCVD was characterized by a higher prevalence of hypertension and diabetes mellitus. These patterns were consistent across sex-stratified analyses. Despite high rates of secondary prevention therapy use, a substantial residual atherogenic burden was observed among patients with premature ASCVD. Conclusions: In this predominantly coronary cohort, the findings suggest that premature and later-onset ASCVD occur within a broadly overlapping risk-factor landscape, but that the relative distribution of these factors differs according to age at first clinical presentation. The greater prevalence of smoking, family history, and atherogenic lipid abnormalities among younger patients may reflect earlier or greater exposure to these factors, whereas the greater burden of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and other chronic comorbidities among older patients is consistent with their progressive accumulation with age. These cross-sectional associations should not be interpreted as demonstrating distinct causal mechanisms or age-independent risk profiles.

articles.title: Radiographic Evaluation of Scoliosis in Pediatric, Adolescent, and Young Adult Patients: Associations Between Curve Severity, Localization, and Skeletal Maturity.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The vertebral column is exposed to significant mechanical loads, exceeding 8000 N at certain levels due to bipedal posture and locomotion. These forces may contribute to structural alterations during growth. Scoliosis is among the most common structural spinal conditions in children and adolescents, with reported prevalence ranging from 0.5% to 5.2%. Our study aims to evaluate the radiographic characteristics of scoliosis in pediatric, adolescent and young adult patients and to analyze associations between curve severity and anatomical and developmental parameters. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 233 patients (152 females, 81 males) examined between August and October 2023. Cobb angle, curve localization, curve direction, Risser stage, and spina bifida occulta were assessed. Associations between variables were analyzed using chi-square and Fisher's exact tests, and multivariable linear and ordinal regression models. Results: Scoliosis (Cobb angle ≥ 10°) was identified in 62.2% of patients within this referral cohort. A statistically significant association was observed between curve localization and scoliosis severity (p = 0.007), with thoracic curves being present more frequently with higher Cobb angles. No statistically significant associations were found between scoliosis severity and sex or curve direction. Spina bifida occulta was detected in 11.7% of scoliotic patients. Skeletal maturity followed expected age-related patterns. In multivariable ordinal logistic regression across the entire cohort, primary thoracic curve localization (aOR = 4.64, p < 0.001), female sex (aOR = 3.06, p < 0.001), and older age (aOR = 1.18, p = 0.002) were independently associated with higher scoliosis severity categories, whereas Risser stage and spina bifida occulta were not. In subgroup multivariable linear regression restricted to thoracic curves, higher Risser stage (β = -3.11°/stage, p = 0.041) and older age (β = 2.12°/year, p = 0.013) were independently associated with continuous Cobb angle magnitude. Conclusions: Scoliosis severity is associated with anatomical curve localization and skeletal maturity demonstrates age-appropriate ossification patterns. These findings support the value of integrated radiographic assessment, including Cobb angle evaluation and Risser staging, in the diagnostic work-up of pediatric, adolescent, and young adult scoliosis.

articles.title: MicroRNAs as Diagnostic Biomarkers for Deep Vein Thrombosis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: In patients with suspected acute deep vein thrombosis (DVT), new blood biomarkers with high specificity for DVT could potentially lower the proportion of patients requiring imaging. The plasma microRNAs (miRs) miR-134-5p, miR-103a-3p and miR-210-3p have been proposed as diagnostic biomarkers of venous thromboembolism, but their diagnostic accuracy for acute DVT has not been investigated. We aimed to assess the diagnostic performance of miR-134-5p, miR-103a-3p and miR-210-3p for DVT in patients with suspected first-lifetime acute lower-extremity DVT. Methods: This prospective cross-sectional study consecutively included outpatients with suspected first-lifetime acute lower-extremity DVT. Plasma levels of miRs were measured using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. DVT status was determined by whole-leg duplex compression ultrasonography. Diagnostic test performance was assessed by the area under the curves (AUCs) from receiver operating characteristic curves with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (95% CI). The diagnostic accuracy of D-dimer was also assessed for comparison. Results: Among the 360 patients included in this study, 28% had a first-lifetime acute lower-extremity DVT. The AUCs for miR-134-5p, miR-103a-3p, and miR-210-3p ranged from 0.53 to 0.57, with 95% CIs overlapping 0.50. D-dimer had a sensitivity of 97% and specificity of 41% using the cut-off value of 0.5 µg/mL. Conclusion: Plasma miR-134-5p, miR-103a-3p and miR-210-3p showed poor diagnostic test performance for DVT. Our findings suggest that these miRs would not be helpful in discriminating between patients in whom DVT can be safely excluded and those who require imaging.

articles.title: Ocular Surface Findings in Patients with Surgery-Indicated Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Inflammation plays a central role in the pathophysiology of both chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) and dry eye disease (DED), suggesting a possible link between these two conditions. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between surgery-indicated chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) and ocular surface parameters related to dry eye disease and to evaluate their association with radiological disease severity. Methods: This retrospective study included 32 patients with surgery-indicated CRSwNP who underwent functional endoscopic sinus surgery (January 2021-January 2025) and 31 controls, all of whom had complete ophthalmological examinations. Ocular surface parameters, including Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) scores, tear break-up time (BUT), Schirmer test values, and Oxford staining scores, were compared between the groups. Disease severity was assessed using the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test-22 (SNOT-22) and the Lund-Mackay score (LMS). Generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used for eye-level analyses. Associations between ipsilateral LMS and ocular surface parameters, as well as the effects of the degree and location of sinus involvement, were also assessed. Results: Higher OSDI scores (p = 0.001), lower BUT and Schirmer test values, and higher Oxford staining scores were observed in the CRSwNP group (all p < 0.05). Ipsilateral LMS was not significantly associated with ipsilateral BUT, Schirmer test values, or Oxford staining scores. No association was observed between OSDI scores and either LMS or SNOT-22 scores. No sinus region, including the osteomeatal complex, showed a significant association after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusions: Surgery-indicated CRSwNP is associated with objective ocular surface dysfunction, including impaired tear film stability and reduced aqueous tear secretion. However, ocular surface findings and dry eye symptoms were not related to radiological disease burden. These findings suggest that ocular surface evaluation may be considered in patients with surgery-indicated CRSwNP, but prospective studies are needed to confirm this.

articles.title: From Host Response to Microbiological Risk: Association of the RIN-IM Score with Culture-Positive Sepsis and Antimicrobial Resistance in Critically Ill Adults.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Early identification of microbiologically confirmed sepsis and antimicrobial-resistant infection remains challenging in critically ill patients. The renal-inflammatory-nutritional-metabolic (RIN-IM) score integrates serum creatinine, the systemic immune-inflammation index, pan-immune inflammation value, serum albumin, and triglyceride-glucose index. This study investigated the association of the RIN-IM score with culture-positive sepsis and antimicrobial resistance phenotypes in critically ill adults. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 318 adults with sepsis admitted to the intensive care unit between 1 January 2023 and 31 March 2026. The RIN-IM score was calculated from laboratory measurements obtained within 24 h and categorized as low (0-3), intermediate (4-6), or high risk (7-10). The primary outcome was culture-positive sepsis. Secondary analyses, restricted to patients with culture-positive sepsis, examined associations between RIN-IM and multidrug-resistant (MDR), extensively drug-resistant (XDR), and pandrug-resistant phenotypes. Results: Culture-positive sepsis was identified in 154 patients (48.4%). The median RIN-IM score was higher in culture-positive than in culture-negative patients (6 [interquartile range, 4-8] vs. 4 [2-5]; p < 0.001). Culture positivity increased from 29.1% in the low-risk group to 50.4% in the intermediate-risk group and 74.6% in the high-risk group. Each one-point increase in RIN-IM was independently associated with culture-positive sepsis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.21-1.51), while high- versus low-risk classification was associated with an aOR of 4.65 (95% CI, 2.25-9.62). Among culture-positive patients, 67 (43.5%) had MDR, and 20 (13.0%) had XDR infections. Each one-point score increase was independently associated with MDR infection (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.12-1.48). The exploratory XDR analysis was based on 20 events and used Firth's bias-reduced logistic regression; a one-point score increase was associated with XDR infection (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.09-1.52), but the categorical estimates were imprecise. The score demonstrated moderate discrimination for culture-positive sepsis (AUC, 0.752; 95% CI, 0.699-0.805) and MDR infection (AUC, 0.724; 95% CI, 0.643-0.805); discrimination for XDR infection was exploratory (AUC, 0.742; 95% CI, 0.635-0.849). Twenty-eight-day mortality increased from 13.6% to 27.7% and 47.9% across the three risk categories (p < 0.001). Conclusions: Higher admission RIN-IM scores were associated with culture-positive sepsis. Among patients with culture-positive sepsis, higher scores were also associated with MDR infection; this subgroup analysis was conditioned on microbiological confirmation and should not be interpreted as prediction of resistant infection in the overall sepsis population. The association with XDR infection was exploratory, based on only 20 events, and requires confirmation in larger independent cohorts. Because RIN-IM assessment and microbiological sampling were not fully time-synchronized, these findings should not be interpreted as real-time microbiological prediction or evidence of clinical utility. RIN-IM should not replace culture-based diagnosis, susceptibility testing, individual risk-factor assessment, local antibiograms, or clinical judgment. The observed associations do not establish a direct biological relationship between RIN-IM and microbial burden or antimicrobial resistance.

articles.title: Panel-Specific Optimization and Benchmarking of Copy-Number Callers for ERBB2 Amplification Detection Using the Nanodigmbio NanOnco Plus Panel v3.0.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: ERBB2 amplification is a clinically relevant breast-cancer biomarker, but CNV detection from targeted sequencing depends on assay design, normalization, tumor fraction, and decision rules. We evaluated panel-specific ERBB2 analysis configurations against a binary FISH reference, with emphasis on the distinction between development-set performance and internal validation. Methods: We retrospectively evaluated 126 FFPE breast-tumor specimens (59 FISH-positive and 67 FISH-negative; 123 recorded patient identifiers) sequenced using NanOnco Plus Panel v3.0 on DNBSEQ-G400. Seven tumor-only, panel-compatible CNV caller configurations were compared; no matched normal tissue was available, although panel-matched normal reference pools were used where required by a caller. PureCN was run as a standalone tumor-only workflow, and CNVkit was run independently. Original fixed-rule results were calculated on the development cohort. An additional common 5-fold, 20-repeat patient-grouped cross-validation procedure selected decision rules using training data only, maximizing sensitivity subject to training specificity ≥90%. Upstream caller outputs were held fixed. Technical no-calls were retained. Results: On the development cohort, the fixed CNVkit median-bin log2 rule yielded 76.3% sensitivity (Wilson 95% CI, 64.0-85.3%) and 91.0% specificity (81.8-95.8%), with F1 81.8% and κ = 0.679. Native standalone PureCN yielded 16.9% sensitivity and 95.5% specificity at absCN ≥ 14; PURPLE had three numerical no-calls. Under the common patient-grouped decision-calibration procedure, CNVkit yielded 67.8% sensitivity and 91.0% specificity, whereas native PureCN yielded 19.3% sensitivity and 91.2% specificity. Exploratory computational purity subgroups and descriptive profiles across 554 genes illustrated heterogeneity of the measured DNA copy-number signal; independent pathology cellularity was unavailable, while quantitative FISH fields were recovered only for 45 of 126 specimens and were not used to define the full-cohort benchmark. Conclusions: The results support assay-specific development of ERBB2 decision rules but do not establish an intrinsic ranking of CNV software or clinical validation of other panel genes. The original full-cohort metrics are development-set estimates, and the additional cross-validation is conditional on previously generated caller outputs. External validation with independently assessed tumor content and complete clinical HER2 adjudication remains necessary.

articles.title: PD-L1 Expression and Clinicopathologic Associations in Mediastinal Aggressive Large B-Cell Lymphomas: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) contributes to immune escape and is a therapeutically relevant target in aggressive B-cell lymphomas.
