However, its distribution and clinicopathologic significance across primary mediastinal aggressive large B-cell lymphomas remain incompletely defined. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 53 cases diagnosed between 2010 and 2025, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma (PMBCL), mediastinal gray zone lymphoma (MGZL), and T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma (THRLBCL). PD-L1 immunohistochemistry (clone 22C3) was performed on formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue. Tumor cells and intratumoral inflammatory cells were assessed together. Membranous staining was scored as 0, 1+, 2+, or 3+, and the proportion of cells in each category was recorded. Results: PD-L1 staining was present in 40/53 cases (75.5%; 95% CI, 61.7-86.2%). Mean PD-L1-positive percentages were similar in DLBCL, PMBCL, and MGZL (38.81%, 31.67%, and 43.89%, respectively; p = 0.726), and no tested cutoff separated the diagnostic groups. In contrast, MGZL showed a higher mean 3+ component (31.11%) and more cases with 3+ staining in at least 50% of evaluated cells (4/9, 44.4%; 95% CI, 13.7-78.8%) than DLBCL (1/21, 4.8%; 95% CI, 0.1-23.8%) or PMBCL (1/21, 4.8%; 95% CI, 0.1-23.8%); the overall comparison remained significant after Bonferroni correction (unadjusted p = 0.012; adjusted p = 0.049). PD-L1 extent was not associated with age, tumor size, LDH, beta-2 microglobulin, Ann Arbor stage, SUVmax, treatment response, or overall survival. Conclusions: PD-L1 expression is common in mediastinal aggressive large B-cell lymphomas. MGZL showed an exploratory strong-staining pattern that requires independent validation. No prognostic association was detected in this cohort.

articles.title: Serum Tumstatin and Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Levels in Patients with Rosacea: A Cross-Sectional Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Angiogenesis is a core feature of rosacea and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is upregulated in lesional skin, yet serum tumstatin, an endogenous angiogenesis inhibitor, has not been measured in rosacea. Methods: In this cross-sectional case-control study, serum VEGF and tumstatin were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in 44 patients with rosacea and 44 age- and sex-comparable controls, with each analyte measured on a single plate. Results above the upper limit of quantification were treated as censored. Groups were compared with the Mann-Whitney U test and Tobit regression adjusted for age, sex and body mass index. Results: Both biomarkers were lower in rosacea: median VEGF 3.39 versus 5.50 ng/mL (p < 0.001; adjusted geometric mean ratio 0.71, 95% CI 0.58-0.86) and tumstatin 13.27 versus >20 ng/mL (p < 0.001; ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.56-0.87). The analytes were very strongly correlated (ρ = 0.95), also within the measuring range (ρ = 0.91). Neither correlated with the Rosacea Area and Severity Index, disease duration or subtype, and discrimination was modest (area under the curve 0.72 and 0.70). Conclusions: In this preliminary single-centre study, serum VEGF and tumstatin were lower in patients with rosacea. Because the two analytes covaried to a degree that suggests a shared analytical factor, the samples were measured in singlicate, the kits were not validated in-house, many results exceeded the calibrated range, and VEGF concentrations (control median 5.50 ng/mL) exceeded published serum values from other immunoassays (≈0.04-0.23 ng/mL) more than tenfold, an analytical explanation cannot be excluded; the findings require confirmation with validated assays before any biological interpretation.

articles.title: Intraoperative OCT-Based Stromal Topography in Phototherapeutic Keratectomy.
articles.abstract: Objectives: This study aims to investigate whether anterior corneal curvature can be reliably measured by combined Placido-optical coherence tomography (OCT) during phototherapeutic keratectomy (PTK) despite intraoperative stromal swelling, and to quantify the immediate smoothing effect of PTK on anterior stromal higher-order aberrations (HOAs). Methods: In this prospective study, 20 eyes with epithelial basement membrane dystrophy (EBMD) undergoing PTK were examined using the MS-39© (CSO©) at four timepoints: preoperatively (t1), after epithelial debridement (t2), after PTK ablation (t3), and at 3-month follow-up (t4). Anterior curvature, corneal and stromal thickness, and epithelial thickness were analyzed across 17 corneal sectors within an 8 mm zone using two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) (timepoint × sector). Anterior Zernike HOAs were computed globally, and the smoothing effect of PTK ablation was assessed by paired comparison of t2 and t3, both obtained on de-epithelialized stroma. Results: Mean central sagittal anterior curvature remained stable across intraoperative timepoints (t1: 44.27 ± 2.32 D; t2: 44.83 ± 2.75 D; t3: 45.01 ± 2.48 D; p = 0.490), despite substantial stromal swelling: Central corneal thickness increased by 114.4 ± 53.0 μm from t2 to t3 (p < 0.001), exceeding preoperative values. At 3-month follow-up, a significant flattening of -1.13 ± 1.38 D was observed (t3→t4; p = 0.002). Stromal HOA analysis revealed a significant smoothing effect of PTK ablation: total HOA root mean square (RMS) decreased from 2.28 ± 2.14 to 0.99 ± 0.46 μm (t2→t3; p = 0.001), with coma RMS showing the most consistent reduction (Δ = -0.38 ± 0.33 μm, p < 0.001; 19/20 eyes). Epithelial thickness distribution narrowed at t4 (interquartile range (IQR) -52.2%), consistent with epithelial remodeling after stromal surface regularization. Conclusions: Anterior corneal curvature remains stable during PTK despite intraoperative stromal swelling, supporting the feasibility of OCT-based intraoperative topographic assessment. In contrast, pachymetric readings are rendered unreliable by stromal hydration. Anterior stromal HOA, particularly coma RMS, may serve as a quantitative intraoperative marker of the smoothing effect achieved by PTK.

articles.title: Pre-Transplant Laboratory Parameters and Early Outcomes in HBV-Related Deceased Donor Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Background: Early postoperative outcomes after deceased donor liver transplantation (DDLT) are influenced by recipient, donor, and perioperative factors. Routinely available pre-transplant laboratory tests may provide complementary information for risk assessment. This study aimed to explore associations between routine pre-transplant laboratory parameters and early postoperative outcomes after DDLT. Methods: This retrospective single-center descriptive pilot study included 32 adult recipients who underwent DDLT for hepatitis B virus-related liver disease between 2004 and 2019. Pre-transplant biochemical and hematologic parameters were evaluated in relation to in-hospital mortality, biliary complications, infectious complications, bleeding, and hospital stay. Descriptive group comparisons and exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed. Results: In-hospital mortality occurred in 6/32 recipients (18.8%), biliary complications in 5/32 (15.6%), infectious complications in 9/32 (28.1%), and postoperative bleeding in 2/32 (6.2%). Routine laboratory parameters did not significantly discriminate mortality. Among 28 recipients with available potassium measurements, four developed biliary complications. Potassium showed exploratory discrimination for biliary complications (AUC = 0.818, p = 0.048), based on only four biliary events. Bilirubin and GGT did not significantly discriminate mortality. Conclusions: Routine pre-transplant laboratory parameters showed no consistent association with in-hospital mortality after DDLT. The potassium association is hypothesis-generating and requires validation in larger cohorts before clinical application.

articles.title: Localiser-Based Software-Assisted Patient Positioning in Chest CT: A Propensity Score-Matched Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Vertical off-centring in chest CT impairs bowtie-filter beam-hardening correction, degrading noise uniformity and image quality. iCentering derives the patient's geometric centre from a single posteroanterior localiser and automatically adjusts table height. This study aimed to evaluate whether iCentering reduces off-centring distance (OCD) and improves image quality versus manual positioning in chest CT, and to investigate correlations between OCD and noise characteristics. Methods: In this retrospective, single-centre study, 192 propensity score-matched pairs from 423 adults undergoing non-contrast chest CT were analysed. OCD, objective image quality (standard deviation (SD), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), figure of merit (FOM)), noise distribution ratio (NDRA-P), and radiation dose indices were measured. Paired comparisons employed t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and effect sizes reported. Directionally stratified Spearman correlation and multivariable regression examined OCD-noise associations. Results: Intra- and inter-observer reliability was good to excellent (ICC 0.87-0.99 for OCD; 0.75-0.97 for most regions of interest). iCentering moved median OCD closer to zero at all levels (Level 1: -7.25 vs. -29.40 mm; Level 2: -1.45 vs. -22.00 mm; Level 3: 7.45 vs. -11.90 mm; all p < 0.001; r range: 0.76-0.77). Regarding image quality, SD decreased and SNR, CNR, and FOM increased at all levels (all p < 0.001), while NDRA-P approached 1.00 (p < 0.05). Radiation dose indices were unchanged (p > 0.05). OCD correlated with SD (|ρ| = 0.478-0.812, p < 0.001); regression confirmed independent associations in both strata (OCD < 0: β range: -0.068 to -0.079, R2 = 0.52-0.65; OCD > 0: β range: 0.056-0.078, R2 = 0.28-0.54), whereas the association between OCD and NDRA-P was weak. Conclusions: iCentering improves centring accuracy and objective image quality in chest CT, without increasing radiation exposure. Reduced OCD is independently associated with lower image noise, underscoring the value of precise centring.

articles.title: Peripheral Nerve Conduction and Anthropometric Characteristics in Elite American Football Players: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: American football exposes athletes to repeated collisions and intense physical loading. This exploratory study compared anthropometric characteristics and peripheral nerve conduction parameters between elite American football players and healthy sedentary men. Methods: Thirty-six elite male players and 39 sedentary male controls underwent anthropometric assessment and motor and sensory nerve conduction studies (NCSs) of the upper and lower extremities. Groups were compared with Welch's t-test, and effect sizes (Hedges' g) were reported with 95% confidence intervals. The false discovery rate (FDR) was controlled across all 110 NCS parameters, which were also analysed in linear models adjusted for age, for age, height and body mass index, and for age and local limb circumference. Results: Players had larger shoulder, upper-arm and forearm circumferences, whereas height and limb segment lengths were similar. After age adjustment and FDR control, players had longer accessory nerve motor latencies on both sides (right: 3.70 ± 0.86 vs. 2.74 ± 0.85 ms; left: 3.63 ± 0.94 vs. 2.69 ± 0.75 ms; both q < 0.001), a shorter left musculocutaneous motor latency and a faster left sural sensory conduction velocity. Median, ulnar, sural and tibial response amplitudes were lower in players, but these differences were attenuated after adjustment for age. Conclusions: Elite American football players differ from sedentary controls in a small number of nerve conduction parameters, most consistently in accessory nerve motor latency. Because the controls were sedentary and the design was cross-sectional, these differences cannot be attributed specifically to American football rather than to intensive athletic training in general. They should be regarded as hypothesis-generating findings that require independent replication.

articles.title: Growth and Pubertal Status in Children with Type 1 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Comparison with Non-Diabetic Controls.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) has historically been associated with impaired linear growth and delayed pubertal development due to chronic insulin deficiency. Advances in intensive insulin therapy and glucose monitoring may have substantially reduced these effects. This study evaluated growth and pubertal development in children with T1DM treated with multiple daily injections (MDIs) or continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) compared with non-diabetic controls and investigated whether metabolic control was associated with anthropometric outcomes. Methods: This retrospective observational study included 177 children aged 3-18 years: 102 with T1DM (60 treated with MDI and 42 with CSII) and 75 non-diabetic hospital-based controls. Height SDS, BMI SDS, Tanner stage, biochemical parameters, and diabetes-related variables were analyzed. Comparisons, correlations and multiple linear regression analyses were performed to evaluate associations between metabolic control and anthropometric parameters. Results: No significant differences were observed between children with T1DM and healthy controls regarding height SDS, BMI SDS, or pubertal development. Likewise, no anthropometric differences were identified between the MDI and CSII groups. Fasting plasma glucose was significantly lower in the CSII group (p < 0.001), whereas HbA1c was comparable between treatment modalities. Neither HbA1c nor other routinely assessed metabolic parameters showed significant associations with height SDS or BMI SDS in correlation or multivariable regression analyses. Conclusions: Children and adolescents with T1DM showed no significant differences in height SDS, BMI SDS, or Tanner stage compared with controls, and similar anthropometric findings were observed in patients receiving MDI and CSII. These results suggest that major disturbances in attained height and pubertal status were not evident in this contemporary cohort of children with T1DM. However, given the retrospective cross-sectional design, longitudinal studies are needed to determine how contemporary diabetes management and long-term metabolic control influence growth trajectories and pubertal progression.

articles.title: Machine Learning Prediction of 90-Day Readmission and Mortality in General Internal Medicine: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Predicting post-discharge outcomes in general internal medicine (GIM) is essential for targeted intervention. This study developed machine learning (ML) models to predict 90-day hospital readmission and 90-day all-cause post-discharge mortality using routine clinical data. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 935 adult admissions to a tertiary GIM department (January 2022-December 2023), of which 881 were retained after data quality verification. Six ML algorithms-Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Neural Network, and Voting Ensemble-were evaluated across admission-only (Tier 1) and discharge-augmented (Tier 2) feature sets using Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), SelectKBest feature selection, and five-fold cross-validated hyperparameter tuning. Results: The 90-day readmission and mortality rates were 33.4% and 4.8%, respectively. Mortality models substantially outperformed readmission models (best admission-model AUC 0.821 for the Voting Ensemble vs. 0.645 for Logistic Regression in readmission; best discharge-model mortality AUC 0.828 for Logistic Regression, 95% CI: 0.694-0.930). Discharge models did not improve over admission models for either outcome. Key mortality predictors included code status, albumin level, functional dependence, and age. Conclusions: Admission-available clinical variables enabled good discrimination of 90-day mortality but only modest readmission prediction. Given the low events-per-variable ratio and single-centre design, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require external validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Reliability, Quality, and Readability of Freely Available Large Language Models for Clinical Decision Support in Perforated Peptic Ulcer: A Blinded, Multidimensional Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Perforated peptic ulcer (PPU) is a common surgical emergency in which each hour before surgery increases mortality, and the decision is often made by a single surgeon on call. Large language models (LLMs) may offer rapid decision support, but their reliability in this setting is unknown. We compared five freely accessible LLMs in a blinded, multidimensional design. Methods: Twenty-four structured questions derived from the WSES 2020 guideline, covering the preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative phases, were posed to the free versions of ChatGPT (GPT-5.3 Instant), Claude (Sonnet 4.6), DeepSeek-V3, Gemini (2.0 Flash), and Grok 3 during April and May 2026, yielding 120 responses. Two general surgeons blinded to model identity scored scientific reliability with the modified DISCERN instrument (mDISCERN, 8-40) as the primary measure and overall quality with the Global Quality Score (GQS, 1-5) as a secondary measure. Because every question was answered by all five models, the Friedman test was primary. Results: Models differed significantly in reliability (Friedman chi-square(4) = 71.35, p < 0.001, Kendall W = 0.743) and separated into two tiers: Claude (mDISCERN 37.83), Grok 3 (36.08), and DeepSeek-V3 (34.92) scored higher than ChatGPT (30.62) and Gemini (29.48). All between-tier comparisons were significant, whereas no within-tier comparison reached significance. Inter-rater agreement was moderate (mDISCERN ICC(2,k) = 0.647) and internal consistency high (Cronbach alpha 0.867 and 0.916). Reliability correlated positively with response length (rho = 0.717) and negatively with readability (rho = -0.452). Conclusions: Freely accessible LLMs vary substantially in reliability for PPU, so model choice has clinically meaningful consequences. This variation is specific to the models, versions, and access tier evaluated, and no model should be used for emergency surgical decision support without independent, setting-specific validation.

articles.title: Comparative Detection of IDH1 R132H and TERT Promoter Mutations in Plasma and Cerebrospinal Fluid of Patients with Glioma Using Targeted Droplet Digital PCR.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Molecular profiling is essential for glioma classification, but in some cases tissue sampling may be limited, whereas reported detectability of cell-free tumor DNA (cftDNA) in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) varies considerably. The aim of this study was to compare the detection rates and concentrations of cftDNA carrying IDH1 R132H and TERT promoter C228T/C250T mutations in paired plasma and CSF samples, as well as to examine associated clinical characteristics. Methods: 66 patients with WHO grade 1-4 gliomas were enrolled before surgery. Preoperative plasma and lumbar CSF were collected before tissue-damaging procedures. Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) was isolated from 5 mL of plasma and 2.5-5.0 mL of CSF and analyzed using mutation-specific droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) assays. Results: cfDNA was available from 65 CSF and 63 plasma samples. Total cfDNA concentration was lower in CSF than in plasma (medians: 434.1 vs. 1240.3 copies/mL; p < 0.001). Nevertheless, cftDNA carrying at least one of the assayed mutations was detected in 14/65 CSF samples (21.5%) and in 0/63 plasma samples (0.0%) (p < 0.001). IDH1 R132H was detected in 4.6% of CSF samples, and TERT promoter mutations were detected in 16.9%. Every CSF mutation with available paired tissue data was also identified in the corresponding tumor. Glioma grade 4 and contrast-enhancing tumors were associated with higher CSF cfDNA, cftDNA carrying at least one of the assayed mutations, and mutant allele fraction values (p < 0.05), whereas tumor size and localization were not significantly associated with these parameters (p > 0.05). Conclusions: With the presented targeted ddPCR workflow, lumbar CSF was substantially more informative than plasma for detecting the selected glioma-associated mutations. CSF cftDNA analysis may complement tissue profiling, although broader panels and larger prospective studies are needed to establish its clinical sensitivity.

articles.title: Non-Nodular CT Patterns of Solid Lung Cancer in the Early Growth Phase: A Two-Center Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Early diagnosis of solid lung cancer (SLC) is essential for better prognosis. However, non-nodular patterns, atypical CT manifestations of SLC in the early growth phase, are easily overlooked, potentially leading to delayed diagnosis. This study aimed to characterize the clinical features and CT findings of non-nodular patterns of SLC in the early growth phase. Methods: Between January 2015 and October 2025, 365 patients with 365 pathologically confirmed SLCs were retrospectively enrolled from two centers. Based on initial morphological appearances, lesions were classified into nodular and non-nodular groups (patch-like, strip-like, bead-like, pleural plaque-like, and cystic-cavity subtypes). Clinical data and CT findings were summarized and compared between the two groups. Results: Of the 365 SLCs, 107 (29.32%) initially presented as non-nodular lesions, among which patch-like lesions (56, 52.34%) were the most prevalent, followed by bead-like (20, 18.69%), strip-like (16, 14.95%), pleural plaque-like (9, 8.41%), and cystic-cavity lesions (6, 5.61%). Both nodular and non-nodular lesions were predominantly located in the upper lobes (55.04% vs. 58.88%, p = 0.611). Multivariable analysis revealed that smoking history (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-8.28; p = 0.040), subpleural distribution (aOR, 3.37; 95% CI, 1.61-7.72; p < 0.001), interstitial lung disease (ILD) (aOR, 66.45; 95% CI, 23.57-220.04; p < 0.001), and post-tuberculosis lung changes (aOR, 8.60; 95% CI, 2.37-32.64; p = 0.001) were independently associated with a non-nodular pattern (AUC: 0.869; p < 0.001). Conclusions: In smokers or patients with ILD/post-tuberculosis lung changes, subpleural non-nodular lesions in the upper lobes require close monitoring for growth.

articles.title: Yield of Low Serum Vitamin B12 Results in General Pediatric Outpatient Practice: Age-Specific Patterns and Associations with Testing Indications and Recorded Clinical Features.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Serum vitamin B12 testing is frequently ordered in pediatric outpatient practice, either routinely or incidentally as part of broad laboratory panels or in response to symptoms and nutritional concerns; however, how the yield of low serum vitamin B12 results varies across age groups and testing indications remains poorly defined. The primary focus was age-related variation in low serum vitamin B12 results, with recorded testing indications examined as a secondary question and symptom-specific analyses considered exploratory. Methods: This single-center retrospective study analyzed testing episodes from children aged 0-18 years attending general pediatric outpatient clinics in 2025. Outcomes were <200 pg/mL (primary) and <300 pg/mL (secondary). Two blinded physicians classified testing indications. Cluster-robust regression evaluated age, sex, and indication; 18 symptom indicators were evaluated in age- and sex-adjusted models with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Results: Of 34,744 episodes, 34,721 were valid; 5.8% were <200 pg/mL and 27.5% were <300 pg/mL. Low-result yield (<200 pg/mL) showed a bimodal age pattern: 7.9% at ages 0-2 years, 2.3% at 3-5 years, and 10.6% at 15-18 years. The number of tests per low result ranged from 9.4 at ages 15-18 years to 42.8 at ages 3-5 years. Routine or incidental testing comprised 63.9% of episodes; crude yield by indication ranged from 4.9% to 7.3%. Compared with 6-11 years, adjusted odds were higher at 0-2 years (aOR 2.81, 95% CI 2.44-3.24) and 15-18 years (aOR 3.92, 95% CI 3.42-4.51). No indication independently predicted the primary outcome; no symptom remained significant for that outcome after false discovery rate correction. Conclusions: The yield of low serum vitamin B12 results was strongly age-dependent and bimodal, with higher-yield periods during the first two years of life and adolescence. Broad retrospectively recorded testing indications were not independently associated with results < 200 pg/mL after adjustment for age and sex. These findings support age-informed assessment alongside clinician-directed testing.

articles.title: Treatment-Stratified Immune-Inflammatory Trajectories and Early Response in Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma Receiving Systemic Therapy.
articles.abstract: Background: Systemic therapy outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain heterogeneous, and treatment selection is still largely guided by clinical eligibility rather than dynamic biologic response. We evaluated whether accessible standard-of-care immunophenotypic and immune-inflammatory markers, tumor-marker kinetics, and immune-context variables could generate treatment-stratified early response signals. Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 153 unique patients with HCC, each contributing one systemic therapy episode. First on-treatment imaging response was classified as complete response, partial response, stable disease, or progressive disease. Routine immune-cell indices, including neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio, lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio, and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), were evaluated at baseline and early post-treatment timepoints. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) kinetics and overall survival were analyzed descriptively. Results: A total of 153 patients were included: 124 received immunotherapy-based therapy and 29 received tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. Overall objective response rate was 26.8%, disease control rate was 56.2%, and progression occurred in 43.8%. AFP trajectory separated responder from non-responder phenotypes, supporting the value of dynamic marker change. Treatment-stratified trajectories revealed distinct patterns: among immunotherapy-treated patients, Week 2 SII increase was associated with progression at first on-treatment imaging (median log2 ratio 0.17 vs. -0.24 for progression vs. non-progression; p = 0.026), whereas TKI response was associated with lymphocyte expansion and decline in neutrophil-dominant inflammatory indices. Conclusions: Routine immune-inflammatory trajectories, particularly early SII change, may provide clinically relevant treatment-stratified response signals in patients with HCC receiving systemic therapy. These findings support interpreting standard clinical markers as evolving biologic trajectories rather than isolated prognostic scores and provide a practical foundation for future biomarker-informed treatment strategies.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Based Versus Threshold-Based Bone Removal for CT Angiography of Head and Neck Arteriovenous Fistulas: A Retrospective Comparison of Image Quality, Key-Structure Display, and Post-Processing Time.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Bone overlap at the skull base limits CT angiography (CTA) in head and neck arteriovenous fistulas (hAVFs), and threshold-based bone removal fails where bone and contrast attenuation overlap. Whether deep learning-based removal improves the display of the structures that determine endovascular planning is unknown in a DSA-confirmed cohort. We therefore compared the two methods within the same CTA datasets. Methods: In this single-centre retrospective study, 35 patients with DSA-confirmed hAVF underwent head and neck CTA and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) within two weeks of each other, and each CTA dataset was post-processed with both methods on one workstation. Two blinded readers scored the fistula site, feeding artery and draining vein (0 to 2 each) and overall image quality (5-point scale). Scores were compared with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, vessel edge sharpness and post-processing time with paired t tests, and technical visualisation with McNemar's test. Results: Deep learning-based removal displayed the fistula site, feeding artery and draining vein more completely (median total anatomical score 6.00 versus 3.00; p < 0.001 for both readers) and overall image quality was higher (5.00 versus 4.00; p < 0.001). Objective vessel edge sharpness was concordant (316.47 ± 46.68 versus 273.70 ± 45.66 HU/mm; p < 0.001). Technical visualisation was numerically higher (97.1% versus 88.6%) but not significantly so (p = 0.248; three discordant pairs), which makes this endpoint inconclusive rather than negative. Post-processing time was shorter (40.56 ± 1.61 s versus 101.70 ± 4.39 s; mean paired difference 61.14 s, 95% CI 59.53 to 62.74 s; paired t test, p < 0.001). Conclusions: In DSA-confirmed hAVF, deep learning-based bone removal displayed the structures that determine endovascular planning more completely than threshold-based removal and was about one minute faster per case. It does not replace DSA for definitive assessment of fistula architecture, and the apparent advantage at the cavernous sinus is exploratory and requires external validation in larger multicentre cohorts.

articles.title: Effect of Peripheral Defocus Contact Lens Residual Decentration After Six Months of Wear on the Astigmatic Component in Myopic Children.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To ascertain if the residual decentration of contact lenses with peripheral retinal defocusing geometry could be associated with alterations in the astigmatic refractive component over a six-month period of wear in children. Methods: A total of 39 eyes from 39 participants (mean age: 11.1 ± 1.54 years, ranging from 6 to 13 years) were included. Participants underwent an eye examination and were assigned to one of three studied lenses: multifocal contact lenses with either non-adjustable (Biofinity Multifocal) or adjustable parameters (Gentle 80 Multifocal), or a contact lens designed for myopia control (MYLO). After six months of lens wear, a refractive assessment was performed and topographic images of the eye with the contact lens fitted were taken. From these images, the decentration of each contact lens was calculated using ImageJ 1.54d software. Results: There was no significant difference in the decentration amount or angle between the three contact lenses studied (one-way ANOVA, both p ≥ 0.088). After six months of contact lens wear, there were no significant differences in astigmatic components (cylinder power and axis and J0 and J45 vectors) related to lens decentration (Wilcoxon test; all p ≥ 0.209). Moreover, there was no significant relationship between lens decentration (amount or angle) and changes in astigmatic components (Spearman's correlation, all p ≥ 0.147). Conclusions: Residual contact lens decentration was observed in both adjustable and non-adjustable lenses. However, within the limitations of this study, no significant correlation was detected between lens decentration and variations in the astigmatic refractive components after six months of contact lens wear.

articles.title: PACS-Integrated Artificial Intelligence-Based Software Tool for Rapid and Fully Automatic Bone Fracture Assessment of the Tibial Plateau.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries requiring accurate reduction and stable fixation; inadequate planning can prolong recovery and increase osteoarthritis risk. Although CT-based 3D reconstructions are routine, automated 3D identification and separation of individual fracture fragments is uncommon. We evaluated a PACS-integrated AI workflow for automated 3D segmentation of intact bones, fracture detection, and fracture-fragment delineation. Methods: This single-center retrospective study analyzed preoperative TPF CT scans acquired on 64- and 128-slice scanners. Femur, patella, tibia, fibula, and fracture components were manually segmented in Visage 7 by a radiologist (9 years of experience) and an orthopedic surgeon (4 years). Segmentations were exported as NIfTI and used to train a 3D nnU-Net model with default preprocessing and parameters on 20 annotated TPF cases using a two-phase training strategy (initial training followed by retraining with refined labels). The trained model was integrated into Visage 7 and executed via an interactive PACS button for fully automated segmentation. Two independent readers rated outputs on a five-point Likert scale for intact bone segmentation, fracture detection, and fragment delineation; inter-reader association was assessed using Spearman and Kendall correlations. Results: In 108 fully rated cases, intact bone segmentation scored very high (means 4.67/4.72; median 5) and fracture detection was good (means 4.15/4.20; median 4). In contrast, individual fracture-fragment differentiation was limited (means 2.64/2.75; median 2). Inter-reader association was very high (Spearman r 0.943-0.967; Kendall's tau-b 0.875-0.971; all p < 0.001). Greater fracture complexity was associated with poorer fracture-fragment differentiation. Discussion: A PACS-integrated AI workflow can reliably segment intact bones and detect TPF within routine imaging, supporting rapid 3D visualization for surgical planning. However, robust separation of individual fracture fragments remains the primary limitation, motivating larger and more diverse training datasets and continued model refinement.

articles.title: A Candidate Verification Gate for Reducing False-Positive Staging in a Pressure Ulcer AI Pipeline.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: A four-class stage classifier can assign a pressure ulcer stage to an erroneous detection. We evaluated supervised candidate verification and its rejection costs. Methods: This retrospective challenge-set study used a frozen detector and stage classifier with an existing binary gate threshold of 0.70. Negative evaluation data comprised 1138 Normal-labeled skin images from 347 source photographs and 328 non-pressure-wound images. A stronger source-family audit reduced the original 112-image positive subset to 94 images from 93 families; these still overlapped detector development. Additional experiments compared three source-grouped binary classifiers and paired detector fine-tuning with or without mined negative images. Results: The historical gate reduced skin images with false-positive outputs from 269/1138 (23.6%) to 54/1138 (4.7%). In the corrected positive subset, 106/107 detected lesions were retained; overall lesion recall changed from 107/110 to 106/110. Both historical false-negative lesions remain in the safety review. Newly trained You Only Look Once (YOLO) 26s, ResNet18, and MobileNetV3-small models achieved internal test-positive retention of 97.4-98.5% after separate calibration. Adding mined negatives directly to detector fine-tuning also reduced false-positive outputs. The historical gate accepted 122/147 matched non-pressure-wound candidates. Conclusions: Negative supervision reduced false-positive outputs through both modular verification and detector retraining. The findings do not establish superiority of a separate gate, patient-level generalization, clinical acceptability of missed lesions, or pressure ulcer etiology discrimination.

articles.title: Toward a National Tuberculosis Lateral-Flow Urine Lipoarabinomannan (LF-LAM) External Quality Assessment Program in Thailand: Feasibility Demonstration Through Panel Development, Validation, and Proficiency Testing, March 2025-April 2026.
articles.abstract: Background: The World Health Organization and the Thailand National HIV Treatment Guidelines recommend the use of lateral flow urine lipoarabinomannan (LF-LAM) testing for tuberculosis (TB) detection in people living with HIV (PLHIV) with advanced HIV disease who have signs and symptoms of TB or are seriously ill. As Thailand decentralizes LF-LAM testing, a robust quality assurance system is needed to maintain diagnostic accuracy across healthcare levels. Methods: We developed, validated, and rolled out Thailand's first national external quality assessment (EQA) and internal quality control (IQC) framework for urinary TB LF-LAM testing. Pre-characterized urine panels were distributed to 20 provinces spanning 12 health regions nationwide across four cycles from 2025 to 2026. Longitudinal monitoring of reporting compliance, pass rates, and failure modes was performed across 30 participating sites in 2025 and 64 and 42 sites in 2026 Rounds 1 and 2, respectively. Results: IQC coverage increased from 7 to 68 facilities by the final cycle in January 2026, with satisfaction rates of 85.7-100%. EQA pass rates showed a stepwise improvement: 83.3% in Round 1/2025, 93.1% in Round 2/2025 and 97.5% and 98.4% in the 2026 rounds (p < 0.05). Initial failures were primarily due to false-positive interpretation of Grade 1 bands and deviation in the reading window. Targeted retraining and standardized reference match-cards reduced user-dependent false-positive results to 0% in the final cycle. Conclusions: A centralized national quality assurance framework may be an effective mechanism for standardizing the reliability and interpretation of point-of-care LF-LAM testing across decentralized healthcare systems. This approach strengthens diagnostic capacity at peripheral facilities and supports the safe expansion of TB services for PLHIV.

articles.title: Predicting MCI-to-Alzheimer's Conversion: A Systematic Benchmark of Classical, Machine Learning, and Deep Survival Models.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Predicting time-to-conversion from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a critical clinical challenge. Most survival analyses rely on static baseline variables, ignoring the temporal dynamics of serial neuroimaging. We benchmark seven survival model families using a novel temporal MRI descriptor pipeline on ADNI. Methods: A cohort of 661 MCI patients (250 conversion events, 37.8%, median follow-up 42.0 months) was constructed from ADNI. FreeSurfer volumetrics of six brain regions were summarised into three time-based descriptors each (atrophy rate, trajectory variability σ, and time-weighted cumulative mean μ) under strict anti-leakage constraints, yielding 18 neuroimaging features which, combined with six clinical variables (age, sex, education, MMSE, ADAS-13, and APOE-ε4), form a 24-dimensional covariate vector. Cox PH, Weibull AFT, Exponential, RSF, GBST, DeepSurv, and DeepHit were evaluated under stratified 5-fold cross-validation and assessed on an independent OASIS-3 cohort (n=78) as an exploratory analysis. Results: All seven models achieved C-index 0.853-0.863 (Δ=0.010), with Cox PH reaching 0.863±0.027 using only routine structural MRI. Time-dependent AUC ranged from 0.856 (12 months) to 0.938 (48 months). Risk stratification by quartile yielded highly separated Kaplan-Meier curves (log-rank p<0.001). On OASIS-3 (n=78, exploratory), classical models showed preliminary cross-cohort consistency (Weibull AFT 0.760±0.063, RSF 0.759±0.049), while deep learning degraded substantially (DeepSurv 0.551±0.116); these results are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as confirmatory given the small per-fold sample size (EPV ≈ 1). Conclusions: The temporal MRI descriptor pipeline achieves a C-index of 0.863 using only routine structural MRI, without PET or CSF biomarkers, demonstrating strong discriminative performance on ADNI MCI-to-AD conversion. The narrow performance band (Δ=0.010) suggests that, within this feature-engineering paradigm, no clear performance separation was observed among the evaluated model architectures; this convergence may reflect feature-level rather than architecture-level constraints, although the underlying cause cannot be established from discriminative performance alone. Classical models showed more stable cross-cohort behaviour under data-scarce conditions; prospective validation on larger cohorts with full covariate parity is required before clinical translation can be considered.

articles.title: A Facet-Associated Cyst with Aneurysmal Bone Cyst Morphology Causing T10-T11 Compressive Myelopathy Mimicking Cauda Equina Syndrome in an Octogenarian.
articles.abstract: Aneurysmal bone cysts (ABCs) are benign, locally aggressive osseous lesions that predominantly affect children and young adults; ABC morphology in a facet-associated cystic lesion in an octogenarian is highly unusual and may overlap radiologically with a degenerative facet or synovial cyst. An 81-year-old woman presented with a 2-month history of progressive bilateral lower-limb weakness, sensory disturbance, and gait deterioration, followed by acute saddle anaesthesia and bowel dysfunction, prompting concern for cauda equina syndrome. Examination showed bilateral MRC 3/5 weakness, mildly increased lower-limb tone, brisk reflexes, and bilateral Hoffmann signs. Lumbar MRI did not demonstrate cauda equina compression. Dedicated thoracic MRI revealed severe multifactorial T10-T11 canal stenosis with marked cord compression, together with a small right posterolateral extradural lesion adjacent to the facet/posterior elements. Posterior T10-T11 decompression, including laminectomy and flavectomy, with excision of the cystic lesion resulted in neurological improvement. Histopathology demonstrated blood-filled cystic spaces separated by fibrovascular septa containing osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and reactive bone, without malignant features, consistent with ABC morphology. This case emphasizes careful neurological localization when cauda equina-like symptoms coexist with upper motor neuron signs and highlights an unusual facet-associated cystic lesion with ABC morphology contributing to multifactorial thoracic spinal stenosis in an elderly patient.

articles.title: Baseline OCT Biomarkers and Early Outcomes After Idiopathic Full-Thickness Macular Hole Surgery: Associations with Primary Failure and Visual Acuity After Successful Closure.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Baseline visual acuity (VA) and minimum linear diameter (MLD) are well-established predictors after surgery for idiopathic full-thickness macular hole (FTMH). It is less clear whether other optical coherence tomography (OCT) features provide additional information. We examined the associations of selected baseline OCT biomarkers with primary anatomical failure and with early postoperative VA after successful closure. Methods: We retrospectively studied eyes that underwent surgery for idiopathic FTMH at a single Swiss center between 2019 and 2024. Primary failure was assessed exploratorily using Firth penalized logistic regression. Early postoperative VA was analyzed among eyes with successful primary closure and an eligible visit 21-60 days after surgery. Linear regression models included baseline VA and MLD, with each OCT biomarker added separately. Patient-level cluster-robust standard errors accounted for bilateral inclusion. Results: This study included 127 eyes from 124 patients. Primary closure was achieved in 116 eyes (91.3%), while 11 eyes (8.7%) had primary failure. Greater MLD was associated with higher odds of primary failure (odds ratio per 100 µm, 2.09; 95% confidence interval, 1.46-3.26). Among the 99 successfully closed eyes with eligible early follow-up, several OCT biomarkers were associated with postoperative VA in univariable analyses. However, none remained significant after adjustment for baseline VA and MLD and correction for multiple testing. Bumpy borders produced the largest, although modest, improvement in model performance. Conclusions: MLD showed the most consistent exploratory association with primary failure. Additional OCT biomarkers provided limited independent information about early postoperative VA beyond baseline VA and MLD in eyes with successful primary closure and eligible early follow-up.

articles.title: Anomalous Origin of the Right Pulmonary Artery from the Ascending Aorta in an Adult After Prior Patent Ductus Arteriosus Surgery.
articles.abstract: We present an adult patient with a history of surgical treatment of a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in whom contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography (CT) demonstrated anomalous origin of the right pulmonary artery (RPA) from the ascending aorta. Axial CT images clearly demonstrate an discontinuity between the main pulmonary artery and the right pulmonary artery (RPA), and delineate an abnormal opening on the ascending aorta; multiplanar reconstruction technology precisely locates the origin of the artery; dynamic volume imaging integrates the three-dimensional anatomical structure into a model nearly equivalent to a surgical perspective. This case illustrates that an anomalous pulmonary artery associated with a ductus may remain unrecognized at the time of ductus surgery and persist into adulthood, and that a single contrast-enhanced CT examination with multiplanar and cinematic reconstruction provides comprehensive, single-session confirmation of the diagnosis, together with the anatomic roadmap required for surgical planning. For any patient undergoing PDA closure-particularly when pulmonary hypertension or right-heart dilation seems disproportionate-deliberate verification of the origin of both pulmonary arteries may prevent a missed lesion and a second, avoidable operation.

articles.title: Regional Perivascular Space Burden in Pediatric Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension: A Case-Control MRI Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Altered perivascular fluid dynamics and glymphatic function have been implicated in the pathophysiology of idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH), but data in pediatric patients remain limited. Our aim was to evaluate MRI-visible perivascular space (PVS) burden in pediatric IIH and investigate its relationship with conventional MRI findings, transverse sinus stenosis (TSS), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) opening pressure. Methods: In this retrospective case-control MRI study, 46 pediatric patients with clinically confirmed IIH and 46 controls frequency-matched by age and sex were included. PVS burden was independently assessed by two pediatric radiologists on axial T2-weighted images using the Potter grading system. Conventional MRI findings associated with IIH and TSS were evaluated. Associations between PVS burden, TSS, and CSF opening pressure were analyzed. Interobserver agreement was assessed using Cohen's kappa statistics. Results: Basal ganglia PVS scores were significantly higher in pediatric IIH patients than in controls (p = 0.005), while no significant differences were observed in centrum semiovale or brainstem PVS scores. Centrum semiovale PVS scores differed according to TSS status; TSS-negative patients had lower scores than both TSS-positive patients and controls (Holm-adjusted p = 0.007 for both comparisons), whereas TSS-positive patients did not differ significantly from controls. No significant correlation was observed between CSF opening pressure and PVS scores in any evaluated region. Interobserver agreement for PVS grading was good for the centrum semiovale and basal ganglia and moderate for the brainstem. Conclusions: Pediatric IIH was associated with increased basal ganglia PVS burden, suggesting a regionally heterogeneous pattern. Pediatric IIH was associated with increased basal ganglia PVS burden, suggesting a regionally heterogeneous pattern. Centrum semiovale PVS burden differed according to TSS status, with lower scores in TSS-negative patients than in both TSS-positive patients and controls, whereas TSS-positive patients did not differ significantly from controls.

articles.title: Development and Temporal Validation of a Three-Metabolite Cerebrospinal Fluid Model for the Diagnosis of Leptomeningeal Metastasis from Solid Tumors.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is a severe complication of solid tumors. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology is only about 70% sensitive on a single examination, and objective markers are needed. Methods: CSF from 49 patients with LM and 16 with intracranial disease without LM was analyzed by targeted LC-MS in a training batch (n = 30) and a temporally independent validation batch (n = 35). Metabolites selected by both LASSO and random forest entered a logistic regression model, which was applied unchanged to the validation batch and evaluated by repeated and nested cross-validation on all 65 samples. Results: Hydroxyphenyllactic acid, argininosuccinic acid and norepinephrine were selected by both algorithms. The model reached an AUC of 0.954 in the training batch and 0.839 (95% CI 0.687-0.991) in the validation batch. In repeated cross-validation on all 65 samples, the AUC was 0.790 (95% CI 0.655-0.924), with sensitivity 0.714 and specificity 0.938; nested cross-validation gave 0.747. Conclusions: A three-metabolite CSF panel discriminates LM from non-LM and retains discrimination under cross-validation and in a temporally independent batch. It is a candidate adjunct to cytology and imaging whose specificity, based on 16 controls, requires confirmation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Photon Absorption Remote Sensing Virtual Histopathology: A Preliminary Exploration of Diagnostic Equivalence to Gold-Standard H&E Staining in Skin Cancer Excisional Biopsies.
articles.abstract: Background: Photon Absorption Remote Sensing (PARS) enables label-free imaging of subcellular morphology by observing absorption interactions. Coupled with deep-learning, PARS produces label-free virtual hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images in unprocessed tissues. This study evaluates the diagnostic performance of PARS-derived virtual H&E images in skin excisions, including squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), basal cell carcinoma (BCC), and normal skin. Methods: Sixteen unstained formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded excisions were PARS-imaged, then stained with chemical H&E dye. Seven fellowship-trained dermatopathologists assessed all 32 images (16 PARS and 16 H&E) in a masked randomized fashion. Example PARS and chemical-H&E whole-slide images are available at the S-BIAD2324 Archive. Results: Diagnostic sensitivity and specificity were comparable between PARS (sensitivity: 96.7% [95% CI: 89.5-100.0%]; specificity: 95.2% [95% CI: 74.7-100.0%]) and H&E (sensitivity: 95.6% [95% CI: 88.2-100.0%]; specificity: 85.7% [95% CI: 50.2-100.0%]). Primary diagnostic agreement was 95.5% (95% CI: 89.5-100.0%; Cohen's κ=0.929 [95% CI: 0.869-0.989]), with high inter-rater reliability (Fleiss' κ=0.886 [95% CI: 0.751-1.00] for PARS; κ=0.805 [95% CI: 0.652-0.958] for H&E). Inter-modality subtyping agreement was 91.8% (95% CI: 81.4-100.0%; Cohen's κ=0.731 [95% CI: 0.375-1.000]) for SCC and 100% (κ=1.000) for BCC. For margin confinement, agreement was 92.2% (95% CI: 85.0-99.4%; Cohen's κ=0.718 [95% CI: 0.452-0.984]). Dermatopathologists could not reliably distinguish image origin, and diagnostic confidence was statistically equivalent between modalities. Conclusions: Diagnostic performance of PARS virtual H&E images was consistent with established clinical benchmarks, providing encouraging preliminary evidence of diagnostic concordance with conventional H&E staining. While larger validation cohorts are required to establish true clinical equivalence, these initial findings highlight PARS label-free virtual histology as a promising approach to enhance dermatopathology diagnostics by preserving tissue for downstream analysis while supporting AI integration.

articles.title: Bloodstream Infections in Patients with Malignancy: Microbiological Epidemiology, Antimicrobial Resistance, and Factors Associated with Mortality in a Nine-Year Single-Center Retrospective Cohort.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) are a major cause of morbidity and mortality among patients with malignancy because of disease-related immune dysfunction, intensive chemotherapy, neutropenia, and frequent exposure to invasive procedures. This study aimed to characterize the microbiological profile and antimicrobial resistance patterns of BSIs in patients with malignancy and to identify clinical and laboratory factors associated with in-hospital mortality, explicitly treating ICU admission as an associated marker of critical illness rather than a predictor. Methods: This retrospective study included 191 clinically significant BSI episodes recorded between 2016 and 2025; record review confirmed that each included episode represented a different patient. Demographic characteristics, underlying diagnoses, comorbidities, chemotherapy history, catheter status, infection source, hematological and biochemical parameters, bloodstream pathogen category, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, ward and intensive care unit (ICU) lengths of stay, and in-hospital mortality were evaluated. Categorical variables were compared using the chi-square or Fisher's exact test, while continuous variables were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors independently associated with in-hospital mortality. Results: Of the 191 episodes, 96 (50.3%) occurred in female patients and 95 (49.7%) in male patients. Acute leukemia was the most common underlying diagnosis (n = 70, 36.6%). Blood cultures yielded Gram-negative organisms in 110 episodes (57.6%), Gram-positive organisms in 58 (30.4%), fungi in 19 (9.9%), and polymicrobial growth in 4 (2.1%). Among 168 episodes with interpretable bacterial antimicrobial susceptibility results, 99 (58.9%) met the study-defined composite resistance category was not equivalent to multidrug resistance. An indwelling catheter was present in 27 episodes (14.1%), ICU admission occurred in 25 (13.1%), and severe neutropenia (<500 cells/µL) was documented in 72 (37.7%). The median ward length of stay was 8.0 days (interquartile range, 5.0-14.0 days). In-hospital mortality occurred in 39 episodes (20.4%). Patients who died had significantly lower neutrophil, platelet, lymphocyte, and albumin levels and significantly higher urea and C-reactive protein levels than survivors (p < 0.01). In multivariable analysis, ICU admission (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 18.94; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.49-102.82; p < 0.001) and severe neutropenia (aOR, 6.06; 95% CI, 2.13-17.23; p < 0.001) were associated with in-hospital mortality. However, the wide confidence intervals, particularly for ICU admission, indicate substantial uncertainty in the magnitude of these associations. Conclusions: These estimates should therefore be interpreted cautiously, especially because the timing of ICU admission relative to BSI onset could not be established. Gram-negative organisms predominated among BSI episodes in patients with malignancy, and study-defined resistance phenotypes were frequent but heterogeneous. Severe neutropenia and ICU admission-analyzed specifically as a concurrent marker of critical illness rather than a predictor due to unestablished temporal sequence relative to BSI onset-were associated with in-hospital mortality. These estimates should be interpreted cautiously. Continuous surveillance of local pathogen distributions and resistance phenotypes, early identification of high risk patients, and institution-specific selection of empirical antimicrobial therapy may contribute to improved clinical outcomes.

articles.title: High-Grade Renal Trauma Due to Blunt Injury: Do All Require Surgical Intervention?
articles.abstract: Background: Renal trauma management has increasingly shifted toward non-operative treatment, particularly in hemodynamically stable patients. Advances in imaging, resuscitation, and monitoring have improved the outcomes of conservative management, even in high-grade injuries. Blunt trauma, most commonly from falls, is the leading cause, and renal injuries often occur within the context of polytrauma involving multiple organ systems. Management is primarily guided by hemodynamic stability, overall clinical condition, existing comorbidities, and the severity of injury as determined by the American Association for the Surgery of Trauma (AAST) grading system. This study aimed to describe the management strategies and clinical outcomes of patients with high-grade blunt renal trauma (AAST grades III-V), with particular emphasis on the use of conservative management in selected patients. Methods: This study is a retrospective analysis conducted in our department (Emergency Clinical County Hospital in Brasov, Romania) to identify the data of the patients admitted with high-grade blunt renal trauma from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2025. Results: A total of 58 patients with blunt renal trauma (grade III or higher) were identified. According to the AAST classification, the most common injuries were grade III (35 patients), followed by grade IV (11 patients) and grade V (12 patients). The majority of cases (68.97%) were treated conservatively, and the overall mortality rate was 8.62%. Conclusions: This study highlights the importance of individualized management in renal trauma, supporting conservative treatment in hemodynamically stable patients. Hemodynamic stability, renal injury grade, and the extent of associated injuries should guide treatment decisions. Further research is needed to refine treatment protocols and assess long-term outcomes.

articles.title: A Reproducible Benchmark for Leakage-Resistant Machine Learning on Multi-Site Brain Connectivity Graphs.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Machine-learning studies of autism spectrum disorder from resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging routinely report near-perfect accuracy, yet the models rarely transfer to an unseen scanner. We audited a pipeline of the kind this literature builds, which reported an accuracy of 0.999, and traced that number to five data-leakage pathways. Methods: Under a nested leave-one-site-out protocol on 871 participants from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange, in which the held-out site influenced nothing but model selection, the threshold, the combiner, or the site correction, we closed every pathway, priced each by reopening it, and validated on a locked external cohort. Results: With all five pathways closed, the graph attention network reached an area under the curve of 0.648 and did not outperform a support vector machine on the same connectivity (0.679; p = 0.009). Decision-level fusion added nothing detectable (0.682, p = 0.72). A network identified its training participants better than it detected autism (0.710 versus 0.610); both questionnaire benchmarks proved label-tautological, and performance held on the external cohort. Conclusions: Reported gains in this literature should be read as claims about evaluation protocols until shown otherwise on an untouched acquisition site; all predictions, models, and code are released.

articles.title: Mapping Preeclampsia Risk Thresholds to Screen-Positive Rates in Routine First-Trimester Screening: A Single-Centre Audit.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: First-trimester screening for preeclampsia (PE) with the Fetal Medicine Foundation (FMF) competing-risks algorithm assigns each pregnancy a numeric risk (1:X), which is compared against a threshold to decide aspirin eligibility. What proportion of a real-world screened population a given numeric threshold actually selects-its screen-positive rate (SPR)-depends on which markers were available and on the population's underlying risk distribution, independently of how well that threshold detects PE. We audited this relationship directly from routine data from a single centre. Methods: Retrospective cohort of 5493 singleton pregnancies with a first-trimester PE risk calculated at 11-14 weeks (2020-2026) in one Romanian fetal-medicine centre. Pregnancies were stratified into five groups according to which markers were available at screening (maternal factors ± biochemistry [PAPP-A] ± uterine artery pulsatility index [UtA-PI] ± mean arterial pressure [MAP]), and the centre-specific SPR at fixed risk thresholds and the risk threshold corresponding to fixed SPR targets of 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% were computed for each group. The operational clinical threshold (1:150 before and 1:100 after the introduction of systematic MAP measurement in October 2023) was benchmarked against this map. Outcome ascertainment was quantified to determine whether these data could support any estimate of detection performance. Results: Among pregnancies screened with the maternal factors + MAP + UtA-PI + PAPP-A combination now used in routine practice (n = 1797), the operational threshold of 1:100 corresponded to an SPR of 16.7%, closer to the 15% than the 10% mapping point (local threshold for SPR = 10%: 1:66); the same numeric threshold corresponded to an SPR of only 11.0% among pregnancies screened with maternal factors and UtA-PI alone (n = 317). The historical reduction in SPR from 25.0% (pre-October 2023, threshold 1:150) to 16.1% (post-October 2023, threshold 1:100) was attributable mainly to the threshold change itself, since a same-era comparison at an identical fixed threshold (1:100) showed little difference in SPR between examinations with and without MAP (16.2% vs. 16.0%). Documented pregnancy outcome was available for only 13.5% of pregnancies (742/5493) and was strongly enriched for complicated pregnancies (documented PE prevalence 5.53% in this subset versus 0.87% in the whole cohort and 0.87-1.2% in published Romanian single-centre series). Consequently, outcome data in this dataset were considered unsuitable for local estimation of detection performance or treatment effect, and no such estimate is offered. Conclusions: The numeric risk threshold used clinically does not correspond to a fixed screen-positive rate across marker combinations in routine practice; local mapping of this relationship is a low-cost, outcome-independent audit that any screening centre can perform on its own data before, and independently of, any attempt to validate detection performance.

articles.title: Longitudinal Delta-Radiomics Identifies Treatment-Fraction-Associated Features Linked to Outcomes After Carbon-Ion Radiotherapy for Head and Neck Cancer.
articles.abstract: Background: Longitudinal imaging during carbon-ion radiotherapy (CIRT) may capture dose-related tumor evolution before clinical assessment. We investigated whether serial CT-based Δ-radiomic features follow treatment-fraction (dose escalation)-associated trajectories with prognostic relevance in patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) treated with CIRT. Methods: We analyzed 167 HNC patients receiving 16-fraction CIRT. Features were extracted from plan-CT, confirm-CT, and weekly-CT scans after 5, 9, and 13 fractions. Δ-radiomic features were defined as time-normalized relative changes from confirm-CT. Linear mixed-effects models, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and monotonicity assessments identified features with systematic longitudinal changes. Endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and local recurrence (LR). Optimal prediction timing was determined using optimism-corrected C-indices. Bootstrap resampling and multivariable Cox models assessed cutoff stability and incremental value beyond clinical factors. Results: During a median follow-up of 15.2 months (range: 1.2-67.7), 64 PFS events, 18 deaths, and 24 local recurrences occurred. Five, eight, and six candidate Δ-radiomic features were retained for PFS, OS, and LR. Selected prediction time points spanned fractions 5, 9, and 13. In multivariable analyses, four PFS-related features met the predefined robustness criteria and improved discrimination over the clinical model (C-index, 0.646-0.661 vs. 0.580; likelihood ratio test, p = 0.002-0.004). Sequential adjustment retained two OS-related and two LR-related features. Exploratory histology-specific analyses provided some support, primarily for two PFS-related features. Conclusions: Serial CT-based delta-radiomics identified treatment-fraction-associated imaging features associated with clinical endpoint risk after CIRT for HNC, particularly PFS. These findings are exploratory and require prospective external validation before clinical application.

articles.title: Fluoroscopic Catheter-Tip Positioning During Internal Jugular TIVAD Placement in Breast Cancer: A Two-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Fluoroscopy permits direct assessment of catheter course and tip position during totally implantable venous access device (TIVAD) placement. We compared left- and right-sided internal jugular vein (IJV) port placement in breast cancer. Methods: This retrospective two-center cohort included 836 ultrasound- and fluoroscopy-guided IJV procedures performed during 2021-2024. The institutional optimal radiographic band was 20-40 mm below the carina; 10-20 and 40-45 mm were adjacent acceptable bands. Results: Left and right IJV access were used in 478 and 358 procedures. The imaging-defined reference lengths were 25.0 ± 0.5 and 22.2 ± 0.5 cm. First-pass target success was 70.3% and 77.1%, respectively. Guidewire-assisted repositioning (9.6% vs. 2.8%) and abnormal initial catheter course (7.9% vs. 2.0%) were more frequent on the left. Final tips were in the optimal band in 97.1% and 96.6%, and in the broader acceptable band in 99.4% on each side. Immediate complications comprised three pneumothoraces and six bleeding events. Among 823 patients with documented 90-day status, 45 had a first device-related event (12 mechanical, 18 thrombotic, 10 infectious, and 5 other). Conclusions: Left IJV placement involved a longer route and more intraprocedural correction, while final tip-position distributions were similar. Fluoroscopic assessment documented and guided the correction sequence.

articles.title: False Positives in Esophageal pH Monitoring: The Pitfalls of Single-Value Interpretation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Esophageal pH monitoring is a key diagnostic modality in the evaluation of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and employs either a traditional transnasal catheter or wireless probe. In clinical practice, findings from these studies are often represented by a single metric, such as acid exposure time (AET), designed to quantitatively summarize reflux burden. However, these composite scores are susceptible to error derived from sensor position, patient diet and posture, transient pH fluctuations, anatomical variations, and esophageal motility. This study sought to identify false-positive mechanisms in esophageal pH testing. Methods: We retrospectively identified institutional logs of false-positive pH findings from a single medical center from January 2019 to January 2025, and in conjunction with expert opinion, we classified false-positive patterns based on the original clinical interpretation. Results: The most common mechanism was technical error originating from factors that directly impact sensor integrity, such as a dislodged capsule or withdrawal of the transnasal catheter. Additional confounders comprised patient-specific variables, including esophageal stasis or behavioral disorders like belching or rumination syndrome. Conclusions: Ultimately, false-positive GERD findings are uncommon but can occur when AET is derived from misleading data. We also sought to develop a diagnostic framework that incorporates clinical context, adjunctive testing, and sensor verification protocols in order to mitigate confounders inherent to ambulatory pH monitoring. This study represents one of the first evaluations of false-positive patterns in esophageal pH testing, offering insight that may ultimately enhance precision and clinical decision-making in the diagnosis of GERD.

articles.title: Atypical Periocular Dermatophytosis Caused by Trichophyton mentagrophytes Species Complex Misdiagnosed as Refractory Bacterial and Viral Infection.
articles.abstract: A previously healthy 4-year-old boy presented with progressive left eyelid swelling and erythema, without reported animal exposure. Initially diagnosed as impetiginized eczema, the lesion was treated with topical antibiotic and corticosteroid therapy. Due to early clinical worsening, this was subsequently escalated with oral amoxicillin-clavulanate (50 mg/kg/day) and azithromycin (10 mg/kg/day). However, this local and systemic regimen failed and worsened the clinical presentation over a 9-day period. Inflammatory markers and blood cultures remained normal. Due to outpatient treatment failure, an initial periorbital skin and ciliary margin swab was collected on day 9 of oral antibiotics. Two days later, worsening symptoms prompted hospital admission for intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics (ceftriaxone and clindamycin) and fluconazole. Pending culture results, suspected vesicular lesions led to empirical oral acyclovir (20 mg/kg/dose, 4 times daily); this was discontinued after 3 days when the initial swab returned negative for HSV. Ultimately, after an 8-day incubation, the outpatient swab culture yielded Trichophyton mentagrophytes species complex. Following microbiological identification of the dermatophyte, antifungal treatment was optimized with systemic griseofulvin and topical terbinafine, leading to complete clinical resolution. This case highlights atypical periocular dermatophytosis masquerading as a refractory bacterial and viral infection. Since direct animal exposure was not reported and phenotypic identification alone cannot distinguish between zoophilic (T. mentagrophytes) and anthropophilic (T. interdigitale) subtypes, the exact source of infection remains undetermined. In conclusion, while 'tinea incognito' is well documented, this report illustrates an exceptionally atypical periocular manifestation that mimicked a refractory bacterial cellulitis and simulated a herpetic infection. The novelty of this case lies in its severe clinical mimicry-including the development of chalazion-like lesions-which confounded a multidisciplinary team and led to unnecessary systemic antiviral and broad-spectrum antibiotic therapies, strongly highlighting the clinical importance of considering dermatophytosis in atypical orbital presentations.

articles.title: Positivity Rates and Serum Levels of Antibodies Against Histone H3 Lysine 9 and Its Lactylated Form in Rheumatoid Arthritis and Its Mimics.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To compare the positivity rates and serum levels of antibodies against histone H3 lysine 9 (anti-H3K9) and its lactylated form (anti-H3K9la) among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), or Sjögren disease (SjD) and controls. Methods: Serum anti-H3K9 and anti-H3K9la levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay from 93 patients with RA, 40 with SLE, 40 with SjD, and 40 controls. Antibody findings were compared across study groups and according to rheumatoid factor immunoglobulin M (RF-IgM) and anti-citrullinated protein antibody (ACPA) status in RA. Results: Anti-H3K9 positivity was 28.0% in RA, 40.0% in SLE, 0% in SjD, and 2.5% in controls. Anti-H3K9la positivity was 22.6% in RA and 20.0% in SLE; no SjD patients or controls were positive. Patients with SjD had lower levels of both antibodies than controls. No statistically significant differences were detected according to RF-IgM or ACPA status, although the seronegative subgroups were small. In exploratory multivariable models, TNF inhibitor use was associated with higher levels of both antibodies. Adding either antibody to ACPA and RF-IgM increased sensitivity at the expense of specificity. Conclusions: Anti-H3K9 and anti-H3K9la antibodies were detected more frequently in RA and SLE than in controls, whereas patients with SjD had lower serum levels of both antibodies. No statistically significant differences in antibody positivity or levels were detected according to RF-IgM or ACPA status in RA, although the small seronegative subgroups limited the precision of these comparisons. Their potential value as adjunctive diagnostic biomarkers requires confirmation in larger, independent cohorts with formal diagnostic-performance analyses.

articles.title: Quantitative MRI Characterization of Fluid-Related Phenotypes in Pediatric Epilepsy: Deep Learning-Assisted Assessment of Enlarged Perivascular Space Burden, Regional Distribution, and Clinical Associations.
articles.abstract: Objective: To quantitatively characterize EPVS burden and regional distribution, together with CP and ventricular CSF structural imaging phenotypes, in pediatric epilepsy and to explore within-epilepsy clinical associations of EPVS measures differing from controls. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 123 children with epilepsy and 108 controls aged 10-17 years. Enlarged perivascular space (EPVS), choroid plexus (CP), and ventricular cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) structural imaging phenotypes were quantitatively assessed using SHIVA-PVS, FreeSurfer, and 3D Slicer with expert visual quality control. Primary between-group comparisons used general linear models adjusted for age and sex, with estimated total intracranial volume additionally included for absolute volumetric measures, and multiple comparisons were controlled using the false discovery rate (FDR). Exploratory within-epilepsy clinical-association analyses were subsequently performed for EPVS measures showing FDR-significant between-group differences. Results: Global EPVS burden was higher in the epilepsy group than in controls (q < 0.01), with the most pronounced regional differences in the basal ganglia (BG; q < 0.001). Relative distribution measures showed higher BG burden and lower centrum semiovale (CSO) burden and CSO/BG ratios in epilepsy (q < 0.01). No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in the CP or ventricular CSF phenotypes. In exploratory within-epilepsy analyses, longer disease duration and drug resistance were associated predominantly with BG-EPVS measures, whereas associations with antiseizure medication burden were limited. Bilateral epileptiform activity was also associated with higher BG-EPVS burden after FDR correction (q < 0.05). Conclusions: Primary between-group analyses identified greater EPVS burden in pediatric epilepsy, with the most pronounced regional differences involving the BG. Exploratory within-epilepsy analyses identified associations between selected EPVS measures and specific clinical characteristics. These cross-sectional structural imaging findings characterize a regional EPVS phenotype for further longitudinal and multimodal investigation but do not establish an underlying glymphatic mechanism.

articles.title: Predictive Value of Left Atrial Strain Combined with Low-Voltage Substrate for Recurrence After Radiofrequency Catheter Ablation in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To evaluate associations of left atrial strain and low-voltage area (LVA) with recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) for persistent atrial fibrillation. Methods: This retrospective cohort included 66 patients undergoing first-time RFCA. Strain was measured before ablation and at 3 months, and voltage mapping quantified LVA. Recurrence after the 3-month blanking period was assessed during approximately 3 months of intermittent follow-up. Results: Recurrence was detected in 16 patients (24.2%). Preoperative left atrial reservoir strain (LASr) and contraction strain were lower in patients with recurrence. At 3 months, LASr-3mo and contraction strain remained lower, whereas LVA percentage was higher (11.50% vs. 3.00%; p < 0.001). LASr-3mo correlated negatively with LVA (r = -0.345; p = 0.005). In multivariable analyses, LASr-3mo (OR = 0.617; p < 0.001) and Delta LASr (OR = 0.461; p < 0.001) were inversely associated with recurrence, whereas LVA was positively associated (OR = 1.069; p = 0.044). The LASr-3mo plus LVA model showed promising apparent discrimination (apparent AUC = 0.923; bootstrap-corrected AUC = 0.913). Conclusions: LASr-3mo may contribute to postoperative risk reassessment. LVA remains an exploratory observational marker because voltage mapping influenced treatment selection. The cohort-derived 4.5% LVA cut-off and model performance require prospective external validation using standardized ablation protocols.

articles.title: Performance of Direct Identification and EUCAST Rapid Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing in Bloodstream Infections Using Sepsityper® and Disk Diffusion Methods.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rapid pathogen identification and targeted antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) in bloodstream infections are critical to reducing sepsis-related mortality. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of direct MALDI-TOF MS identification using the rapid Sepsityper® kit and to determine the diagnostic accuracy and reliability of the EUCAST Rapid Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing (RAST) protocol at various incubation periods (4, 6, 8, and 16-20 h) from positive blood culture bottles. Methods: A total of 71 clinical isolates recovered from positive blood cultures in the Medical Microbiology Laboratory of Ondokuz Mayıs University Faculty of Medicine were included. Samples prepared directly using the rapid Sepsityper® kit were identified via MALDI-TOF MS, while the EUCAST RAST protocol was simultaneously performed on Mueller-Hinton agar using disk panels guided by Gram stain results. Results were analyzed for Categorical Agreement (CA), major errors, and very major errors using routine automated AST data as the reference standard. Results: The rapid Sepsityper® kit successfully identified 51 of 71 isolates (71.8%) at the species level within 30-60 min. The overall categorical agreement of EUCAST RAST with the automated system increased from 67.5% at 4 h to 76.6% at 6 h, 82.7% at 8 h, and 87.0% at 16-20 h. With prolonged incubation, the major error rate dropped significantly from 51.3% to 3.8%. However, the very major error rate remained at 8.1% in final readings, with these errors predominantly clustering in carbapenems and fluoroquinolones among Klebsiella pneumoniae strains. Conclusions: The rapid Sepsityper® kit provides species-level identification in under an hour in approximately three-quarters of cases, facilitating the early de-escalation of empirical therapy. Although EUCAST RAST categorical agreement improves progressively with time, conventional methods are still recommended for confirmation due to the risk of very major errors, particularly in detecting carbapenem resistance.

articles.title: Minute-Scale Sleep-Onset HRV as a Candidate Risk-Stratification Biomarker for Diabetic Retinopathy: An Exploratory Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the most common microvascular complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), yet DR screening coverage remains inadequate worldwide. Diabetic autonomic neuropathy typically precedes DR, and heart rate variability (HRV) provides a non-invasive autonomic measure; however, whether HRV can screen for DR remains unexplored.
