Methods: This pilot study investigated whether sleep-onset minute-scale HRV indices-SDANN1 (standard deviation of 1-min segment means of normal-to-normal intervals) and SDANN2 (2-min segments)-serve as candidate screening biomarkers. Using a public 24-h Holter ECG dataset of T2DM inpatients (N = 39; 11 DR-positive, 28 DR-negative), sleep-onset time-points from cardiopulmonary coupling analysis were used to extract 30 min of post-onset ECG. Results: SDANN1 was significantly lower in the DR group (median 23.6 vs. 44.8 ms, p = 0.028, d = 0.74), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.731 (95% CI: 0.530-0.901). At the optimal threshold of ≤ 25 ms, the odds ratio was 8.1 (95% CI: 1.7-38.4), with DR prevalence of 58% in the high-risk versus 12.5% in the low-risk group. Among 12 candidates, only the SDANN family reached significance. Conclusions: sleep-onset minute-scale HRV shows promise as a candidate risk-stratification biomarker for DR; prospective longitudinal validation in larger, sex-balanced cohorts is required before any screening application.

articles.title: Serum Osteopontin Is Associated with Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index-Defined Arterial Stiffness in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Peripheral arterial stiffness (PAS) is common in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Despite osteopontin (OPN) being linked to structural alterations in the vasculature, its specific association with the cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI) as an indicator of PAS is still unclear. Methods: A total of 120 patients diagnosed with T2DM were enrolled in this cross-sectional study. Participants were stratified into the PAS group (CAVI ≥ 9.0) and the control group (CAVI < 9.0) based on the diagnostic criterion of CAVI ≥ 9.0. Circulating OPN concentrations were determined via a commercial enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kit. Results: PAS was present in 72 (60.0%) participants. Relative to the control group, individuals with PAS were older (p < 0.001) and had higher fasting glucose (p = 0.015), glycated hemoglobin (p = 0.006), urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (p = 0.007), and OPN (p < 0.001) levels, whereas their high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) concentrations were markedly lower (p = 0.021). Spearman's rank correlation demonstrated a significant positive association between serum OPN concentrations and bilateral CAVI measurements (both p < 0.001). In multivariable Firth logistic regression, elevated serum OPN concentrations were independently predictive of PAS (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.035; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.012-1.066; p = 0.001), along with older age and lower HDL-C levels. These associations were consistent across conventional and penalized logistic regression analyses. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis revealed that OPN alone achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.748, whereas the model combining OPN, age, and HDL-C achieved an AUC of 0.831. Conclusions: Higher serum OPN levels were independently associated with PAS in patients with T2DM, particularly when combined with age and HDL-C.

articles.title: Arterial and Venous Thrombotic Events in Urological Malignancy-A Real-World Cohort Study from a Tertiary Urology Referral Center.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cancer-associated thrombosis (CAT) increases morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. To describe CAT in urological malignancies and explore associated factors, timing, Khorana score performance and systemic inflammatory indices. Methods: This retrospective study included 1044 patients. Oncological, cardiovascular and laboratory data from medical records were compared by CAT status. Firth penalized logistic regression was used for sparse-event analyses. Results: Thirty-one patients (2.97%) developed CAT, including 17 arterial thrombotic events (ATE) and 14 venous thromboembolic events (VTE). Advanced stage was associated with CAT (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] per stage 1.60, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.21-2.17; p < 0.001) in the primary and sensitivity analyses. In an exploratory analysis, cardiovascular disease was associated with ATE (odds ratio [OR] 4.58, 95% CI 1.67-15.16; Benjamini-Hochberg [BH]-adjusted q = 0.031), although the small number of ATE precluded a reliable subgroup conclusion. Median time from cancer diagnosis to CAT was 3 months. The Khorana score did not show useful VTE discrimination in the systemic chemotherapy subgroup (77 patients; four VTE; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.437, 95% CI 0.127-0.746). The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) showed no useful discrimination (AUCs 0.487-0.513) or improvement of the clinical model (all BH-adjusted q = 0.963). Conclusions: Advanced stage was the most consistent correlate of CAT. Arterial and venous events occurred in similar proportions and were concentrated early after diagnosis. Exploratory analyses suggested a possible relationship between cardiovascular disease and ATE, whereas the Khorana findings were inconclusive and the inflammatory indices lacked discriminatory value. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Machine Learning Detection of Peritoneal Entry from Vibroacoustic Signals During Veress Needle Insertion.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Establishing access is a hazardous step of laparoscopic surgery, and the widely used Veress needle offers only subjective tactile and auditory cues for peritoneal entry. Proximal vibroacoustic (VA) sensing captures needle-tissue interaction non-invasively and is known to contain a characteristic peritoneal puncture signature, which could help surgeons to precisely identify peritoneal entry. However, the VA signature has been evaluated only by retrospective, video-anchored and manual signal analysis. We investigate whether peritoneal entry can instead be detected automatically. Methods: Cavity entry is framed as a binary classification of VA signal segments, and four model families are benchmarked under a single unified protocol: a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN), a multilayer perceptron, a bidirectional long short-term memory network (LSTM), and a support vector machine (SVM) with a radial basis function kernel. All models were trained, selected, and threshold-tuned on a synthetic abdominal phantom (996 segments) and tested once on an independent porcine cadaver dataset (154 cavity, 462 non-cavity signals) so that every test result measures generalisation across a phantom-to-porcine domain shift. Results: The 1D CNN performed the best (accuracy 0.869, AUROC 0.904, macro F1 0.833, cavity recall 0.818), closely followed by the SVM (AUROC 0.900, AUPRC 0.878). Conclusions: These results establish the feasibility of automatically detecting peritoneal entry across a phantom-to-porcine domain shift and extend the descriptive cadaveric characterisation of the puncture signature toward the automated machine learning-based detection of peritoneal entry in laparoscopic access with a Veress needle.

articles.title: Sycophancy in Large Language Models in Oral and Maxillofacial Radiology: The Impact of Misleading Context on Image- and Text-Based Diagnostic Scenarios.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in clinical decision-support, yet their sycophantic behavior in response to user-provided misleading contextual cues remains underexplored in image-based disciplines such as oral and maxillofacial radiology. This study compared sycophantic behavior across five LLMs using image-based and text-based diagnostic scenarios in oral and maxillofacial radiology. Methods: ChatGPT-5.3, Google Gemini 3, Grok 4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and DeepSeek V3.2 were evaluated on 200 scenarios (100 image-based and 100 text-based) under three prompt conditions: neutral, misleading-cue, and authoritative-cue. The resulting 3000 responses were analyzed using generalized estimating equations (GEE). Results: Diagnostic accuracy ranged from 53.5% to 65.0% under the neutral condition and declined to 28.5-44.0% under the authoritative-cue condition. The authoritative-cue condition had significantly higher odds of sycophancy than the misleading-cue condition (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 2.92; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.52-3.37). Modality had no significant main effect on diagnostic accuracy or sycophancy outcomes; however, the Model × Modality interaction was significant for the overall sycophancy rate (p = 0.014). Under the authoritative-cue condition, self-reported confidence did not differ significantly between correct and incorrect responses (p = 0.678). Conclusions: LLMs are susceptible to misleading contextual cues in oral and maxillofacial radiology diagnostic scenarios, particularly when misinformation is presented as an authoritative cue. The dissociation between self-reported confidence and accuracy indicates that self-reported confidence scores alone are unreliable indicators of diagnostic performance. LLMs should therefore serve as supportive tools requiring expert verification rather than as independent decision-makers in clinical practice.

articles.title: A Duplex Isothermal RPA-Lateral Flow Platform for Concurrent Detection of Staphylococcus Aureus and mecA-Mediated Methicillin Resistance.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rapid identification of Staphylococcus aureus and differentiation of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) remains critical to infection control and antimicrobial stewardship, particularly where rapid screening is desirable. In this study, we developed and evaluated a duplex recombinase polymerase amplification coupled with lateral flow dipstick (RPA-LFD) platform enabling simultaneous detection of the species-associated spa locus and the methicillin resistance determinant mecA within a single isothermal reaction. Methods: Primer-probe architecture and reaction parameters were systematically adjusted, with 39 °C selected as the operating temperature, to enable concurrent visual detection of both targets within 15 min. Results: In a preliminary ten-fold serial dilution experiment, visible detection was observed down to 101 CFU/mL for both targets, whereas conventional PCR produced visible amplification down to 102 CFU/mL under the respective assay conditions. This difference represents an assay-specific observation and was not used to establish a statistically validated detection limit. No cross-reactivity was observed against a panel of non-target bacterial species. A preliminary evaluation of 25 nasal swab-derived DNA specimens showed complete concordance with reference PCR within this limited sample set. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate the feasibility of concurrent visual detection of species-associated and resistance targets within a single RPA-LFD configuration. Although further analytical and clinical validation is required, the platform provides a technical framework for simplified duplex isothermal detection of S. aureus and mecA.

articles.title: Exploratory Agreement of 3D Body Surface Analysis with Expert Manual Assessment of Pelvic Malalignment in Patients with Non-Acute Low Back Pain: A Prospective Pilot Study with Linked Post-Hoc Analyses.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We aimed to explore whether selected non-invasive three-dimensional (3D) body surface indicators differed between prospectively defined enrollment groups and, in linked post-hoc analyses, to identify candidate indicators associated with expert manual judgment. Methods: At screening (visit 1), 88 participants underwent manual examination and pelvic X-ray assessment. Of these, 60 entered the prospective pilot study and underwent 3D body surface analysis at visit 2. The prespecified prospective comparison used the protocol-defined malalignment group (n = 30) and comparison group (n = 30). Final manual diagnosis served as an expert-judgment reference comparator. For post-hoc exploratory ROC analyses, the same 60 participants were reclassified according to final manual diagnosis alone as manual-positive (n = 40) or manual-negative (n = 20). Results: In the prespecified prospective comparison, neither 3D surface-height asymmetry nor marker-angle outcomes differed significantly between the protocol-defined enrollment groups across postures P1-P4. Among all 88 screened participants, X-ray sensitivity and specificity relative to final manual diagnosis were 88.6% and 34.1%, respectively. In the post-hoc exploratory ROC analyses, IC surface-height difference at P3 showed an apparent AUC of 0.684 (p = 0.015), and the highest individual marker-angle AUC was 0.706 at P2 (p = 0.005). An exploratory five-variable model, developed and evaluated in the same dataset, yielded an apparent in-sample AUC of 0.756. Conclusions: The prespecified 3D comparisons did not distinguish the protocol-defined enrollment groups. Post-hoc analyses of the same 60 participants identified candidate 3D indicators associated with expert manual judgment, but these findings were exploratory and do not establish diagnostic accuracy or clinical utility. Prospective validation using prespecified indicators and thresholds, an appropriate independent or composite reference standard, and formal reliability assessment is required before a clinical role for 3D body surface analysis can be determined.

articles.title: Quadrilateral Segmental Analysis (QSA): A Calibration-Free Geometric Method for Detecting Lumbar Spondylolisthesis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: On standing lateral radiographs, millimetre measurements of vertebral slip depend on magnification and calibration; slip percentage is scale-free but is usually reported in coarse Meyerding grades. In this exploratory derivation study, we introduce quadrilateral segmental analysis (QSA), a calibration-free geometric method for detecting anterolisthesis. Methods: In 50 patients with degenerative spondylolisthesis from the PROGRES cohort, a blinded observer drew the L1-S1 superior endplate lines on standing radiographs; an automated pipeline computed the diagonal ratio K and the posterior angles of each quadrilateral formed by adjacent lines. The annotation was performed by a single observer; its reproducibility was not assessed, and its sensitivity to annotation error was simulated. The reference standard was an adjudicated two-radiologist classification (κ = 0.916). Segments outside the anterior-translation domain (negative shear; n = 90) were not graded further; the remaining 160 were analysed with patient-cluster bootstrap and leave-one-patient-out validation. Results: Anterolisthesis was present in 54 of 160 segments (33.8%). K discriminated well (area under the curve [AUC] 0.892, 95% CI 0.841-0.937): K ≤ 0.85 supported a slip (specificity 99.1%), and K > 0.95 argued against it (sensitivity 100%; smallest reference-positive slip 9%). Rounded to one decimal, K assigned 46.9% of segments to extreme tiers without observed misclassification. With the lower posterior angle N ≤ 93° in the intermediate tier, the two-step rule reached 94.4% sensitivity and 95.3% specificity, unchanged under nested leave-one-patient-out validation. Simulated endpoint errors of 0.5-1.0 mm changed the two-step classification in 5-13% of segments (ICC 0.74-0.92 for K and 0.85-0.96 for N). Conclusions: Calibration-free QSA parameters discriminated reference-positive from reference-negative segments in patients with degenerative spondylolisthesis. K (the diagonal ratio) translates the radiologist's assessment of anterolisthesis into a single number. These exploratory findings, which do not establish performance for small or borderline slips, require replication in independent cohorts and by other observers before the thresholds can be applied clinically.

articles.title: Convergent Immunopathology in Influenza-Associated Encephalopathy: CD3+ CD4+ T Cell Depletion, IL-6-Mediated Inflammation, and Complement C3 Dysregulation.
articles.abstract: Background: Influenza-associated encephalopathy (IAE) is a severe neurological complication, yet immune biomarkers for its early prediction remain limited. This study aimed to elucidate the systemic immune signature defining IAE by integrating humoral and cellular immunity analyses. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 623 pediatric influenza patients presenting with fever and convulsions (55 IAE, 568 febrile seizure (FS) group) at Wuhan Children's Hospital (2020-2025). Serum complement components (C3, C4), lymphocyte subsets (including CD3+ CD4+, CD3+ CD8+, CD19+ B cells, and NK cells), and cytokines (IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-10, TNF-α) were quantified. Multivariable logistic regression was performed, rigorously adjusted for age, sex, influenza subtype, time from fever onset to sampling, prior use of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) or glucocorticoids, and pre-diagnostic convulsive episodes. Sensitivity analysis via 5th-percentile Winsorization addressed floor effects in C3 measurements. Results: IAE was associated with distinct alterations in both humoral and cellular immunity. Patients with IAE had significantly lower serum C3 levels and higher IL-6 concentrations compared to controls. Multivariable regression revealed that IL-6 (adjusted OR = 1.002, 95% CI: 1.000-1.003, p = 0.037) and CD3+ CD4+ T cells (adjusted OR = 0.983, 95% CI: 0.979-0.988, p < 0.001) were independent predictors in the fully adjusted model. Lower serum C3 levels were associated with IAE across sequentially adjusted models (fully adjusted OR = 0.05, 95% CI: <0.001-0.138, p = 0.002). Sensitivity analysis using 5th-percentile Winsorization of C3 yielded a consistent direction of association (adjusted OR = 0.019, 95% CI: 0.002-0.226), supporting the robustness of the primary finding. Conclusions: These findings identify a convergent immunopathology involving CD3+ CD4+ T cell depletion, IL-6-dominated inflammation, and lower C3 levels in pediatric IAE. Monitoring this immune triad may facilitate early risk stratification. The causal relationships and therapeutic implications of these observations require validation in prospective and mechanistic studies.

articles.title: Advancing Lumbar Disc Herniation Classification from MRI Using an Efficient and Reproducible Classical Machine Learning Framework.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: A common diagnosis for lumbar disc herniation is an image taken with Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). Due to the need for expertise during manual interpretation of MRI scans by specialists, the process is very time consuming. The use of a machine learning (ML)-based pathway to classify lumbar MRI images as either "normal" or "herniated" represents an efficient way to analyse MRI scans seeking similar pathologies. Methods: The proposed methodology transforms original lumbar MRIs (from colour to greyscale), resizes them, filters, and normalises them (using bilateral algorithms) before conducting extraction of features using PCA-based decomposition. A total of ten classical ML classifiers were evaluated using five-fold outer and three-fold inner nested cross-validation, with the number of PCA components selected exclusively within the inner folds. Results: Extra Trees achieved the highest F1-score of 85.86% (95% CI: 84.16-87.44%) and the highest ROC-AUC of 90.96% (95% CI: 89.27-92.54%), with an accuracy of 84.29%, precision of 82.03%, recall of 90.07%, and specificity of 77.79%. Random Forest achieved the highest accuracy of 84.36% (95% CI: 82.40-86.26%), although its overall performance was comparable to that of Extra Trees. Conclusions: The findings support the potential of traditional machine learning classifiers for binary classification within the evaluated image-level dataset, while maintaining a relatively simple design and computational efficiency. No direct empirical comparison with deep learning models was conducted in this study.

articles.title: Automated Segmentation of Mass Lesions in Mammography: Mask R-CNN Versus Classical Methods, Fuzzy Clustering and MedSAM.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The automatic and accurate segmentation of mass lesions in mammograms is a critical step in the computer-aided diagnosis workflow. This study evaluates the mask region-based convolutional neural network (Mask R-CNN), a robust deep learning model for instance-level segmentation, highlighting its growing potential in medical imaging. Methods: Following configuration optimization, the model is applied to mammography images from the CSAW-CC and TOMPEI-CMMDs, which provide masks annotated by breast radiology experts, to be used as a ground truth. To quantify shape and contour discrepancies with respect to the radiologists' annotations, performance is evaluated with both overlap- and distance-based metrics. Furthermore, the model is tested on synthetic mammograms and benchmarked against classical segmentation methods (Otsu thresholding, gradient vector flow active contour, and Chan-Vese segmentation), Fuzzy c-means clustering, and the state-of-the-art Medical Segment Anything (MedSAM) model. Results: By leveraging transfer learning, a limited dataset suffices for stable training, with the network converging by the 10th epoch. The optimal configuration achieves a bounding box average precision (BBox AP) of 0.80 and a segmentation average precision (Segm AP) of 0.58. Evaluated on a test set of real mammograms, the model correctly identifies the lesions, yielding an average Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.87 and an average intersection over union (IoU) of 0.77, performance aligned with the current state of the art. Conclusions: Mask R-CNN has emerged as a reliable and robust model for breast lesion segmentation; compared to the other methods evaluated in this study, it demonstrates superior performance across both overlap- and distance-based metrics. The model exhibits high DSC and IoU scores even on synthetic mammograms with a priori known lesion profiles, which can be used as an objective ground truth to mitigate annotation bias from inter-operator variability among radiologists.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Adjuvant Radiotherapy Use After Simpson Grade I Resection of WHO Grade 2 Meningioma: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) after gross-total resection of World Health Organization (WHO) grade 2 meningioma remains an individualized decision in the absence of definitive randomized evidence. We aimed to identify the clinical, radiological, and pathological factors associated with observed adjuvant RT allocation after Simpson grade I resection and to evaluate the discriminatory performance of proliferative biomarkers in real-world multidisciplinary practice. Methods: This single-center, retrospective cohort included 65 patients, of whom 56 undergoing Simpson grade I resection constituted the primary analytic cohort. Associations with observed RT allocation were evaluated using Firth-penalized logistic regression. Ki-67 and mitotic-index discrimination was summarized using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and Ki-67 threshold stability was assessed in 5000 bootstrap resamples. Brain invasion was evaluated in a documented-case sensitivity analysis. Results: Adjuvant RT was administered to 24 of 56 patients (42.9%). In models adjusted for age, sex, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and tumor size, each 5-percentage-point increase in Ki-67 was associated with higher odds of RT allocation (OR 7.10, 95% CI 2.20-22.94; p = 0.001), as was each increase of 5 mitoses per 10 high-power fields in mitotic index (OR 5.81, 95% CI 2.01-16.75; p = 0.001). Ki-67 showed greater apparent discrimination than mitotic index (area under the curve [AUC] 0.925 vs. 0.801; DeLong p = 0.008). The apparent Youden-optimal Ki-67 threshold was 14%, but thresholds of 12%, 14%, and 15% were selected in 33.4%, 41.9%, and 23.1% of bootstrap samples. Among 44 patients with documented brain-invasion status, Ki-67 remained associated with RT allocation after adjustment for brain invasion (OR 4.53, 95% CI 1.77-11.63; p = 0.002). Conclusions: Ki-67 and mitotic index were associated with observed RT allocation, but both markers were already available to the tumor board. These findings describe institutional treatment-allocation patterns and do not establish RT benefit or validate a Ki-67 threshold for recommending treatment.

articles.title: Graph Neural Network Modelling of Pre-Diagnostic Serum Proteomics for Pancreatic Cancer Detection.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has exceptionally high mortality, largely because of late diagnosis, while established blood biomarkers such as CA19-9 have limited sensitivity for early detection. We evaluated whether modelling serum proteomic measurements as supervised pairwise statistical graphs using synolitic graph neural networks (SGNNs) could provide a useful framework for pre-diagnostic PDAC classification. Methods: We analysed 217 pre-diagnostic serum samples from UKCTOCS, comprising 100 PDAC samples from 75 women and 117 control samples, profiled for 97 proteins. Samples were divided into a development set collected 0-1 year before diagnosis (n = 110) and a temporal holdout set collected 1-2 years before diagnosis (n = 107); 25 PDAC participants contributed samples to both windows. The final SGNN used fold-internal mutual-information selection of 30 proteins, pairwise RBF-SVM-derived edge information, minimum-connected sparsification, and a 10-member GATv2 ensemble per cross-validation fold. Conventional machine-learning comparators were tuned using development data only. Results: The SGNN achieved a mean 5-fold development ROC-AUC of 75.33 ± 10.43%, lower than the tuned Random Forest (81.67%); the other tuned comparators achieved 77.67% (XGBoost), 77.17% (logistic regression), and 73.17% (SVM). Averaging predictions across the five-fold-specific SGNN ensembles yielded a temporal-holdout ROC-AUC of 64.35% (95% CI 52.6-74.6%). In the participant-independent subset of 25 PDAC cases not represented in development and 57 controls, ROC-AUC was 66.04% (95% CI 52.56-78.88%). Conclusions: SGNNs provide a feasible graph-based representation of pre-diagnostic proteomic data but did not outperform optimised conventional machine-learning methods within development cross-validation. The temporal and participant-independent performance estimates warrant further investigation in larger fully independent cohorts. A graph-specific predictive advantage was not directly tested-no such advantage was demonstrated in this dataset-and the clinical utility has not been established.

articles.title: Observer-Related Versus Cross-Modality Variability in Ventricular Quantification by Cardiac CT and Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ventricular measurements from cardiac computed tomography (CCT) and cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) may differ due to modality-specific, physiological, or observer-dependent reasons. We compared cross-modality disagreement with intra-modality interobserver variability. Methods: Fifty-four patients with CCT and CMR examinations within 36 months were retrospectively analyzed. Left ventricular (LV) end-diastolic volume (EDV), right ventricular (RV) EDV, and LV mass were measured on the same platform; 18 underwent independent second-observer measurements. The primary metric was the standard deviation of paired differences [SD(D)], with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: In the repeat-measurement subset, cross-modality SDs were 29.78 mL, 29.19 mL, and 16.72 g for LV EDV, RV EDV, and LV mass, versus 4.83, 7.33, and 6.71 within CCT and 3.57, 3.58, and 4.11 within CMR. Cross-modality variability was 6.16, 3.98, and 2.49 times the CCT and 8.34, 8.15, and 4.07 times the CMR interobserver variability; all 95% CIs exceeded 1. Examination-interval restriction did not materially reduce dispersion, and body-surface-area indexation changed scale but not relative disagreement. Conclusions: Under routine clinical conditions, cross-modality variability in EDV and LV mass exceeded interobserver variability by 2.5- to 8.3-fold. CCT-CMR differences are unlikely to reflect observer-related post-processing variability alone, and consistent modality selection appears preferable to interchanging quantitative thresholds.

articles.title: Photon-Counting Computed Tomography Enables Image-Guided Navigation of the Paranasal Sinuses at Ultra-Low Radiation Dose: An Initial Cadaveric Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) enables substantial radiation dose reduction while preserving high spatial resolution. Its potential for image-guided navigation in endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS), particularly at ultra-low dose levels, remains insufficiently explored. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of PCCT for four different surgical navigation systems at progressively reduced radiation doses. Methods: PCCT datasets of the paranasal sinuses were acquired from two cadaveric specimens using a standard protocol followed by stepwise dose reductions down to 5% of the reference dose. The datasets were used for image-guided navigation with four systems (one optical, three electromagnetic). Registration success, navigation accuracy, and user satisfaction (visual analog scale) were assessed at 100% and 5% dose levels using linear mixed-effects models. Results: Registration was successful for all navigation systems at every dose level. Mean navigation accuracy remained stable despite dose reduction (2.22 ± 1.16 mm at 100% vs. 1.93 ± 1.05 mm at 5% radiation dose; p = 0.364). User satisfaction regarding navigation was consistently high (mean 8.8 ± 0.75) and showed no significant differences between dose levels. Conclusions: PCCT enabled image-guided navigation even at ultra-low radiation doses down to 5% of standard exposure, without compromising navigation accuracy in this initial study. These findings highlight the potential of PCCT to substantially reduce radiation burden while maintaining clinical performance. Further in-human studies are needed.

articles.title: Vitamin A and D Status, Selected Genetic Variants, and Allergy-Related Phenotypes: An Exploratory Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Vitamins A and D are critical regulators of immune function, and genetic variation in their metabolic pathways may influence vitamin status and immune responses. This study investigated the combined nutrigenetic roles of vitamins A and D and their association with allergy-related phenotypes. Methods: In this retrospective study, 80 individuals were included (40 with allergy-related phenotypes and 40 controls). Genetic polymorphisms in CYP2R1, GC, VDR, and BCMO1 were analyzed. Serum vitamin A and 25(OH)D concentrations were compared between groups, and multivariable analyses were performed to assess the effects of age and sex. Genotype distributions were evaluated using chi-square tests, and co-occurring genetic patterns were explored using the Apriori algorithm (p < 0.05). Results: Both serum vitamin A and 25(OH)D concentrations were significantly lower in the allergy-related phenotypes. Genotype differences were observed for CYP2R1 rs2060793 and BCMO1 rs12934922; however, only CYP2R1 rs2060793 remained significant after FDR correction. Although residual confounding cannot be ruled out, exploratory association rule mining identified co-occurrence patterns involving GC, VDR, and CYP2R1 variants with vitamin D deficiency and BCMO1 variants with vitamin A deficiency. These findings should be considered preliminary and hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of established or causal genetic effects. Conclusions: These preliminary findings indicate potential associations between vitamin status, specific genetic variants, and allergy-related phenotypes. Because of the study's retrospective design and limited sample size, these genetic observations should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and warrant validation in larger, prospectively characterized cohorts.

articles.title: Adaptive Liquid State-Space Networks: A Novel Neuro-Dynamic Architecture for Tabular Classification with Application to Anemia Diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Anemia is a complex hematological disorder with various subtypes, and its accurate diagnosis is of critical importance for clinical decision-making processes. Traditional machine learning algorithms and standard deep learning models often struggle to model the nonlinear and typically imbalanced nature of clinical tabular data, which negatively impacts the classification performance and reliability of diagnostic systems. Methods: This study proposed ALSS-Net, a novel deep learning architecture that combines the State-Space Model (SSM), Liquid Time Constant (LTC), and Adaptive Gates mechanisms, with the aim of classifying difficult-to-diagnose types of anemia with high accuracy, robustness, and statistical reliability. Results: Experimental results showed that the Adaptive Liquid State-Space Networks (ALSS-Net) architecture achieved an accuracy of 92.97% on the validation set. Furthermore, on the test dataset, this model obtained an accuracy of 89.13% and an F1 score of 0.8513, outperforming five of the six baseline models by a statistically significant margin (McNemar's test, p < 0.001); the difference with respect to the strongest baseline (MLP) did not reach statistical significance. The ablation studies indicated that the proposed dynamic time constant and adaptive gating mechanisms contributed to the separation of the difficult classes, with adaptive gating accounting for the larger part of the improvement. Conclusions: The architecture also produced better-calibrated probability outputs than the compared models, attaining the lowest Brier score and Expected Calibration Error, and degraded more gracefully under increasing feature noise. These findings were obtained on a single, relatively small open-access dataset without external clinical validation; ALSS-Net is therefore presented as a candidate framework for the future development of clinical decision support systems rather than as a validated diagnostic tool.

articles.title: Ectopic Adrenal Cortical Tissue in the Ovary: A Rare Incidental Histopathologic Finding.
articles.abstract: Ectopic adrenal cortical tissue (EACT) is an uncommon developmental heterotopia and is exceptionally rare in the ovary of adult women. A 52-year-old woman, 6 years after menopause, was evaluated for progressive enlargement of a uterine leiomyoma and postmenopausal spotting. Transvaginal ultrasonography and pelvic magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated multiple uterine leiomyomas but no adnexal mass or endometrioma. During total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, dense adhesions between the sigmoid colon and posterior cul-de-sac were unexpectedly encountered. Histopathologic examination of the adhesion-related tissue revealed neither endometriosis nor significant inflammatory change. Microscopic examination of the ovary identified a 1.9 mm, sharply circumscribed nodule composed of clear, vacuolated zona fasciculata-like cells and compact eosinophilic zona reticularis-like cells. The lesional cells showed diffuse Melan-A immunoreactivity and focal-to-patchy inhibin-α positivity, supporting adrenocortical differentiation. The findings established a diagnosis of ovarian EACT. This case emphasizes that microscopic ovarian adrenal rests may be radiologically occult and should be distinguished from ovarian steroidogenic neoplasms by integrating clinical, morphologic, and immunohistochemical findings.

articles.title: Comparison of Clinical Efficacy and Postoperative Outcomes of Ultrasound-Guided Lateral Sagittal Infraclavicular and Costoclavicular Brachial Plexus Blocks: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The costoclavicular (CCB) and lateral sagittal infraclavicular (ICB) approaches provide ultrasound-guided access to the cords of the brachial plexus. Comparative real-world evidence on imaging efficiency, block dynamics, and postoperative analgesia remains limited. We compared procedural and analgesic outcomes between these approaches. Methods: This retrospective two-center cohort included patients undergoing elective upper-extremity surgery under ultrasound-guided CCB or ICB between April and October 2025. Specialists at both centers had comparable experience with both techniques (approximately 4 years). The primary outcome was total procedure time; secondary outcomes included component times, exact block-onset times recorded during close continuous specialist observation, postoperative pain, rescue analgesia, satisfaction, and discharge time. All patients received the same local-anesthetic dose and volume. Results: Sixty patients were analyzed (29 CCB; 31 ICB). Total procedure time was shorter with ICB (median, 75 vs. 138 s; CCB-ICB Hodges-Lehmann median difference, 65 s; 95% CI, 23-110 s; p < 0.001), as were imaging and application times. Motor- and total-block onset were faster with ICB, whereas sensory-block onset did not differ significantly. Pain scores at 6, 12, and 24 h, rescue analgesia, analgesia duration, satisfaction, and discharge time did not differ significantly. Hemidiaphragmatic paralysis is generally asymptomatic and was not systematically assessed; no local anesthetic systemic toxicity occurred. Conclusions: ICB was associated with statistically shorter procedural and selected block-onset times than CCB. However, the absolute difference in total procedure time was modest, and its clinical importance remains uncertain. The absence of corresponding differences in sensory-block characteristics and patient-centered postoperative outcomes means that these findings should not be interpreted as demonstrating the overall clinical superiority of ICB. Prospective randomized studies incorporating predefined clinically important differences and adequately powered patient-centered outcomes are required.

articles.title: Calibration-Aware Patient-Level Prediction of Source-Defined MSIMUT Status in Colorectal Cancer from Whole-Slide Histopathology Images Using Foundation-Model Embeddings.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Microsatellite instability (MSI) is clinically important in colorectal cancer, but definitive assessment requires molecular or immunohistochemical testing. This study developed a leakage-safe, calibration-aware patient-level framework for predicting a source-defined MSIMUT category from hematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide-derived patches using fixed Phikon foundation-model embeddings. Methods: The TCGA-derived colorectal cohort comprised 360 patients, including 65 source-defined positive and 295 MSS cases, represented by 192,312 pre-extracted patches. Patch embeddings were aggregated using mean, max, and mean-plus-max pooling, and downstream classifiers were evaluated under patient-level cross-validation with calibration, threshold, decision-curve, clinicopathological, source-provenance, and patch-count sensitivity analyses. Results: In the primary random patient-level evaluation, logistic regression with mean-plus-max pooling achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.915 and PR-AUC of 0.809. Fully nested Platt calibration yielded pooled out-of-sample ROC-AUC 0.913, PR-AUC 0.796, Brier score 0.073, calibration slope 1.037, and calibration-in-the-large 0.023. Within the internally cross-validated mean-plus-max framework, an exploratory sensitivity ≥ 0.95 operating point yielded sensitivity 0.969, specificity 0.393, and negative predictive value 0.983. Provenance reconstruction identified source-partition-dependent patch-count structure. In a source-TRAIN to source-TEST holdout, mean-plus-max ROC-AUC decreased to 0.788, while patch count alone was near chance in source-TEST (ROC-AUC 0.517) and explicit patch-count addition did not improve discrimination. Conclusions: These findings support the methodological feasibility of fixed foundation-model embeddings for internal MSI-related pre-screening research, while showing that apparent performance is sensitive to source structure. Independent multicenter validation with clinically adjudicated MSI-H/dMMR endpoints remains necessary before clinical application.

articles.title: Serum Prokineticin-2 and Calprotectin as Potential Biomarkers of Disease Stage and Focal Organ Involvement in Human Brucellosis: A Prospective Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brucellosis is a systemic zoonotic infection with a heterogeneous clinical presentation, and early identification of patients at risk for focal organ involvement remains challenging. This study aimed to assess whether serum prokineticin-2 (PROK2) and calprotectin levels are associated with focal organ involvement in patients with brucellosis and to examine their variation according to disease stage. Methods: In this prospective case-control study, 150 adults were enrolled, including 90 patients with brucellosis diagnosed based on compatible clinical findings together with a Coombs anti-Brucella titer of ≥1:160 and 60 symptomatic non-brucellosis controls in whom brucellosis was excluded after clinical and laboratory evaluation. The brucellosis group included 30 patients each with acute, subacute, and chronic disease; 50 patients had focal organ involvement and 40 had no focal involvement. Focal organ involvement was defined by organ-specific clinical findings supported by appropriate imaging and/or laboratory methods. Serum PROK2 and calprotectin levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay before antimicrobial treatment, while C-reactive protein (CRP) was evaluated as a routine inflammatory comparator. Comparisons were performed according to disease status, disease stage, and focal organ involvement. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to evaluate discriminative performance for focal organ involvement. A parsimonious multivariable logistic regression model including PROK2, calprotectin, and CRP was used to identify factors independently associated with focal organ involvement. Results: Serum PROK2 and calprotectin levels were significantly higher in patients with brucellosis than in the non-brucellosis control group (both p < 0.01). PROK2 levels showed significant stage-related variation, with significantly higher adjusted levels in the acute than in the subacute stage, whereas the acute-chronic difference was not statistically significant. Patients with focal organ involvement had significantly higher serum PROK2, calprotectin, and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels than those without focal involvement (all p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, PROK2 (adjusted OR 3.910, 95% CI 1.526-10.018; p = 0.005), calprotectin (per 100 ng/mL; adjusted OR 2.223, 95% CI 1.208-4.091; p = 0.010), and CRP (per 10 mg/L; adjusted OR 1.662, 95% CI 1.202-2.298; p = 0.002) were independently associated with focal organ involvement. For discriminating patients with and without focal organ involvement, the AUCs were 0.877 (95% CI: 0.794-0.959) for calprotectin, 0.864 (95% CI: 0.783-0.946) for CRP, and 0.807 (95% CI: 0.720-0.895) for PROK2. At the exploratory Youden-derived cut-offs, sensitivity/specificity were 92.0%/70.0%, 82.0%/77.5%, and 82.0%/60.0%, respectively. Conclusions: Both PROK2 and calprotectin were independently associated with focal organ involvement; however, PROK2 showed stage-related variation and calprotectin was not independently associated with disease stage. Further studies are required to determine their clinical and prognostic value in the assessment of focal organ involvement.

articles.title: Competing Risk Prediction of COVID-19 Hospital Mortality with Model Diagnostics and Exploratory Evaluation in Mexico.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We evaluated six-predictor cause-specific models for 45-day in-hospital COVID-19 mortality, including departures from proportional hazards and linearity and transport to Mexican data. Methods: The oxygenation-expanded Barcelona cohort included 1622 adults. Recorded arterial PaO2/FiO2 (P/F) was preferred; otherwise P/F was derived from documented saturation and inspired oxygen using the Rice relationship at SpO2 ≤ 97%. Linear cause-specific Cox models for death and discharge served as a reference. Quadratic and time-varying extensions were assessed by three repetitions of five-fold cross-validation. Frozen Barcelona models were evaluated in a separate Mexican workbook using reconstructed day-45 outcomes and minimum-oxygenation proxies. Historical supplied scores for 634 patients were analysed separately. Results: Barcelona included 325 day-45 deaths. The reference model had apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) 0.822 and bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.820. Proportional hazards (PH) departures persisted within 45 days. Combining quadratic terms and predictor-by-log(1 + time) interactions improved cross-validated AUC from 0.819 to 0.831 and Brier score from 0.12343 to 0.11974, while calibration slope decreased from 0.945 to 0.830. In 171 Mexican records with 12 reconstructed deaths, AUC was 0.967 for the expanded linear model and 0.857 for the combined extension. Excluding one extreme lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) record yielded 170 patients, 11 deaths, and AUCs of 0.964 and 0.935, respectively. The combined model predicted 17.8% mortality against 6.5% observed in that subset. Conclusions: Flexible effects improved some internal metrics but did not establish an adequate replacement model. Residual misspecification, extrapolation and incompatible predictor timing limit transportability. The calculator implements the linear reference model; definitive admission-time external validation remains necessary.

articles.title: Brain MRI Features of Human Neuroinvasive Usutu Virus Infections.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Neuroradiological features of neuroinvasive Usutu virus (USUV) infection are poorly understood, as current knowledge is largely limited to case reports. This study aimed to describe brain MRI patterns, and assess disease severity and vital and functional outcomes in patients with neuroinvasive USUV infection. Methods: This multicentric retrospective observational cohort study analyzed adult patients of both sexes, aged ≥18 years, in the continental region of Croatia who developed symptoms of neuroinvasive disease during the arbovirus transmission season between 2017 and 2025. Patients with serological and/or molecular confirmation of USUV infection were included in further analyses. Only patients who underwent a brain MRI during hospitalization were included in the study. Clinical data and blood/CSF laboratory parameters were also evaluated. The observed outcomes were the severity of clinical symptoms, vital status at hospital discharge, and functional status at hospital discharge. Results: Of 214 arbovirus-positive cases, 8 patients had confirmed neuroinvasive USUV infection, and 4 had a brain MRI. Three patients were male. One patient had a normal MRI, and three patients had abnormal MRIs. All patients with abnormal MRI demonstrated meningeal contrast enhancement (a finding not previously reported), uni- or bilateral hippocampal involvement suggestive of limbic encephalitis, and basal ganglia involvement. All patients required ICU admission, experienced prolonged hospitalization, and were discharged with moderate to severe disability. Conclusions: This study provides important insights into MRI patterns in patients with neuroinvasive USUV infection and addresses the current knowledge gap regarding the neuroimaging of this underdiagnosed disease.

articles.title: Non-Invasive Assessment of SMAD4 Expression Status in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: Diagnostic Value of T1ρ-Weighted Imaging Combined with Clinical Parameters.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a malignancy with poor prognosis, where SMAD4 protein loss is closely associated with increased tumor aggressiveness and metastatic potential. Current assessment of SMAD4 expression relies on IHC of tumor tissue obtained by biopsy or resection, in which limited sampling may not represent intratumoral heterogeneity. T1ρ-weighted imaging, an emerging functional MRI technique, shows promise in characterizing tumor microstructural properties. This study aimed to evaluate the value of T1ρ imaging combined with conventional MRI sequences and clinical parameters for non-invasive prediction of SMAD4 protein expression status in PDAC. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 57 patients with histologically confirmed PDAC who underwent pretreatment MRI with T1ρ imaging between September 2024 and May 2025. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed SMAD4 intact in 28 tumors (49.1%) and SMAD4 loss in 29 tumors (50.9%). T1ρ values were measured and compared between SMAD4 intact and SMAD4 loss tumors. A multiparametric predictive model incorporating T1ρ values, lymph node metastasis status, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) levels was developed. Results: SMAD4 intact tumors demonstrated significantly higher T1ρ values compared to SMAD4 loss tumors (96.34 ± 14.12 vs. 71.93 ± 10.24 ms, p < 0.001). T1ρ achieved an AUC of 0.901 (95% CI: 0.817-0.986), with 82.14% sensitivity and 89.66% specificity, for predicting SMAD4 expression status. A multiparametric model combining T1ρ values, lymph node metastasis status, and CA19-9 levels yielded a numerically higher AUC of 0.932 (95% CI: 0.862-1.000), although the difference from T1ρ alone was not statistically significant (DeLong test, p > 0.05). Conclusions: T1ρ imaging showed potential for predicting SMAD4 status in PDAC.

articles.title: Evaluating a Large Language Model for Emergency Triage Using Synthetic Clinical Dialogues: Toward a Multimodal Clinical Safety Framework.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Prioritizing patient safety through accurate emergency triage is critical during mass-gathering events such as Hajj and Umrah, where high patient volumes can significantly increase the risk of clinical errors. Although the Emergency Severity Index (ESI) provides a standardized triage protocol, it remains dependent on human judgment, while traditional artificial intelligence (AI) models often struggle to capture the nuanced clinical context embedded in patient narratives. To address this gap, this study evaluates GPT-5.2 using synthetically generated dialogues as a step toward a conceptual clinical decision-support framework that bridges structured electronic health records (EHRs) with triage interactions through clinical dialogues. By combining narrative inputs with structured physiological indicators, it explores the potential to support more informed clinical decision-making under controlled simulation conditions. Methods: To evaluate this contribution, we systematically assessed the role of clinical dialogues in triage performance using a balanced and stratified dataset of 1000 simulated Hajj-context scenarios. Results: The results demonstrate that incorporating clinical dialogues can significantly improve triage performance, with a 79.7% relative reduction in under-triage across all ESI levels. A more noticeable improvement was observed in high-acuity cases, with a 91.9% relative reduction in under-triage. In addition, the model achieved a high-acuity recall of 94.5%, highlighting its ability to identify critical "red-flag" symptoms that are often not captured in structured data. These findings suggest that narrative context may contribute to more accurate triage assessment and improved identification of high-acuity cases. Conclusions: Consequently, when evaluated within a controlled decision-support setting, this study suggests that large language model (LLM)-based systems may improve triage reliability and may contribute to safer triage decision-making in high-demand clinical environments.

articles.title: Real-World Validation of the AI-Enabled Vectorcardiographic CSG-Index for Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease: The VECTOR-CAD Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cardisiography is an artificial intelligence-enabled resting vectorcardiography (AI-VCG) system, but evidence for its accuracy in coronary artery disease (CAD) remains limited. We evaluated the AI-VCG-derived CSG-index for obstructive CAD detection, association with stenosis severity, incremental discrimination beyond clinical variables, and concordance with exercise electrocardiography (ECG). Methods: In this two-centre retrospective diagnostic-accuracy study, 721 Cardisiography records from January 2023-December 2025 were screened and 224 patients were included. Invasive coronary angiography (ICA) was the primary reference (n = 172); coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) contributed only reference-negative cases (n = 52) to the hierarchical cohort. Obstructive CAD was defined as ≥50% stenosis and CSG-index ≥ -0.27 as positive. Primary analysis assessed obstructive CAD discrimination in the ICA cohort; secondary analyses assessed severe CAD (≥70%), hierarchical-cohort performance, stenosis severity, incremental value beyond available clinical variables and exercise ECG concordance. Results: Obstructive CAD was present in 76/172 patients. In the ICA cohort, CSG-index area under the curve (AUC) was 0.820, with 80.3% sensitivity and 78.1% specificity; AUCs were 0.843 in the hierarchical cohort and 0.785 for severe CAD. CSG-index increased across stenosis classes. After adjustment for available clinical variables, it remained independently associated with obstructive CAD and increased model AUC from 0.806 to 0.886. In the exploratory exercise ECG subgroup (n = 83), agreement was 66.3%, with fewer false-positive CSG-index classifications. Conclusions: The locked CSG-index showed balanced performance for obstructive CAD, provided graded information across stenosis classes, and added discrimination beyond available clinical variables. These findings support prospective multicentre evaluation as a complementary non-invasive resting test.

articles.title: An Explainable Disease-Aware Intelligent Histopathological Representation Learning Framework for Generalizable Breast Cancer Classification.
articles.abstract: Background: Deep learning approaches, especially convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs), have made substantial progress in breast cancer classification from histopathological images. Yet, previous CNN-ViT-based architectures frequently demonstrate insufficient generalization when evaluated on independent external datasets despite obtaining high performance on internal benchmarks. The key reason is that these architectures learn statistical dependencies instead of precisely identifying disease-specific morphological evidence. During optimization, models may unintentionally depend on non-diagnostic patterns, such as staining variations, scanner characteristics, acquisition settings, and dataset-specific textures, thereby potentially becoming aligned with class labels in the training data but not reflecting intrinsic pathological patterns. This phenomenon leads to inconsistent predictions under domain shifts. Methods: To overcome this limitation, this study proposes a disease-aware intelligent histopathological representation learning framework for generalizable breast cancer classification. The proposed framework leverages CNN and ViT encoders to capture complementary local cellular morphology and global tissue-level contextual information. A disease-aware representation learning mechanism is introduced to distinguish clinically relevant disease-specific features from non-diagnostic fluctuations, allowing the model to concentrate on transferable pathological features. Additionally, an intelligent adaptive decision module is designed to optimize the use of clinically relevant disease evidence for benign and malignant classification instead of relying on the conventional classification head. Results: The proposed framework is evaluated on BreakHis as the internal benchmark (98.10% accuracy) and various independent histopathology datasets for external validation. Conclusions: Comprehensive experiments, robustness analysis, and explainability analyses highlight the effectiveness of the proposed approach in learning generalizable disease-related representations and improving the consistency of cross-dataset breast cancer classification.

articles.title: Real-Time AI-Based ACR TI-RADS Classification of Thyroid Nodules on the Ultrasound Console: A Prospective Agreement Study in a Region with Historical Iodine Deficiency.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To assess the agreement between an artificial intelligence (AI)-based decision support system (DS System), applied in real time directly on the ultrasound console, and an expert panel for ACR TI-RADS classification of thyroid nodules (TNs) in a region with a history of iodine deficiency and a consequently high prevalence of TNs. Methods: A single-center prospective study including 118 consecutive patients (with 276 TNs) referred for thyroid ultrasound between March and May 2024. DS System ultrasound features, ACR TI-RADS classifications (TR1-TR5) and management recommendations were recorded per TN, with and without the 'AI-Adapter' (AI-based modification of the TI-RADS score), and compared to the consensus assessment of a TI-RADS expert panel (paired tests of marginal homogeneity, Cohen's unweighted and weighted κ; all analyses adjusted for clustering of TNs within patients). Results: No malignancy was identified during 24-month follow-up (composite reference standard; cytology or histology in six TNs). The DS System could be applied to all TNs without technical failure. Marginal distributions differed between the expert panel and the DS System for all ultrasound feature categories except echogenicity (p = 0.23). Interrater agreement ranged from poor ("lobulated or irregular", κ = -0.08) to substantial ("cystic or almost completely cystic", κ = 0.62), most frequently slight to fair. TI-RADS classifications showed slight agreement with (κ = 0.04; linear-weighted κ = 0.14) and without AI-Adapter (κ = 0.13; linear-weighted κ = 0.21). The AI-Adapter changed the ACR TI-RADS score by -1.01 ± 1.04 points. Management recommendations showed fair agreement with (κ = 0.23) and without the AI-Adapter (κ = 0.39). Although the number of TR5 ratings was similar (expert panel: 27; DS System: 26 without and 30 with the AI-Adapter), only seven and eight of the 27 TR5 TNs of the expert panel, respectively, were also rated TR5 by the DS System. Conclusions: Real-time application of the DS System on the ultrasound console was technically feasible, but agreement with an expert panel was low. As all TNs were benign, diagnostic accuracy and clinical safety could not be assessed. Validation in cohorts including malignant TNs is required before the DS System can be considered a substitute for expert assessment in regions with a high prevalence of TNs.

articles.title: Cytokine Profiles in Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia: Associations with Lesion Severity and Exploratory Treatment Response.
articles.abstract: Background: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) is the principal cause of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). Cytokines regulate antiviral immunity and tissue remodeling, and cytokine profiling may provide additional information about the biology of cervical lesions. Objective: To characterize cytokine profiles in cervical mucus and serum across grades of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. Methods: The study included 90 women aged 18-80 years: 30 HPV-negative women with negative cytology (Control) and 60 HPV-positive women with histologically confirmed low-grade (LSIL, n = 30; Gr-1) or high-grade (HSIL, n = 30; Gr-2) squamous intraepithelial lesions. Participants were also stratified by minor (grade 1) or major (grade 2) colposcopic findings. An exploratory subgroup of 15 women with HPV16/18-positive HSIL received antiviral and immunomodulatory therapy. Concentrations of 27 cytokines (pg/mL)-FGF, eotaxin, G-CSF, GM-CSF, IFN-γ, IL-1ra, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-7, IL-8, IL-9, IL-10, IL-12(p70), IL-13, IL-15, IL-17A, IP-10, MCP-1, MIP-1α, MIP-1β, PDGF-BB, RANTES, TNF-α, and VEGF-were measured in serum and cervical mucus using the Bio-Plex Pro Human Cytokine 27-plex assay (Bio-Rad, USA) on a Luminex 200 platform. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 23.0 and Microsoft Excel 365. Results are reported as medians and interquartile ranges [Q1-Q3]. A two-sided p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: Exploratory multivariate analyses identified IL-1β, IP-10, MCP-1, and FGF as the cytokines most strongly associated with lesion severity and colposcopic findings. In cervical mucus, HSIL was associated with the highest IL-1β concentration (0.83 pg/mL [0.18-4.91] vs. 0.30 pg/mL [0.04-0.69] in controls; p < 0.001) and the lowest IP-10 concentration (3.07 pg/mL [1.02-13.16] vs. 25.12 pg/mL [5.01-42.40]; p < 0.001). The highest mucus FGF concentration was observed in LSIL (1.73 pg/mL [1.33-2.27] vs. 0.32 pg/mL [0.17-0.59] in controls; p < 0.001), whereas MCP-1 was lower in LSIL than in HSIL (2.38 pg/mL [1.57-3.54] vs. 5.38 pg/mL [3.12-10.55]; p < 0.05). Similar patterns were observed in serum, except that IL-1β was lower than in controls. After treatment, HPV was undetectable in 10 women and remained detectable in 5. The overall cytokine profile changed only modestly. Among the five women with persistent HPV infection, cervical mucus MCP-1 was lower after treatment than before treatment (0.09 pg/mL [0.01-0.41] vs. 0.37 pg/mL [0.08-0.73]; p < 0.01). Conclusions: These findings show associations between lesion severity, colposcopic findings, and compartment-specific cytokine patterns. Because the study was cross-sectional and the treatment subgroup was small and uncontrolled, the results should be considered exploratory and require longitudinal validation.

articles.title: Weight-Independent Cardioprotective Effects of Physical Activity in Patients with Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract: Background: Physical activity is a key modifiable determinant of cardiovascular risk, yet whether its protective association with coronary artery disease (CAD) severity in patients with myocardial infarction (MI) is mediated by body mass index (BMI) remains uncertain. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 294 adults admitted with MI and angiographically confirmed MI. Daily preadmission physical activity, as a score, BMI, cardiovascular risk factors and angiographic CAD extent (single-, double-, or triple-vessel disease) were analyzed. Multivariable ordinal logistic regression assessed independent associations of preadmission physical activity with CAD severity. Mediation analysis evaluated BMI as an intermediary using non-parametric bootstrap resampling with 2000 iterations and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: Higher preadmission physical activity was independently associated with lower CAD severity after adjustment for age, sex, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia and BMI (β = -0.54, p < 0.001). BMI showed no independent association with CAD severity (β = 0.009, p = 0.76). Bootstrapped mediation analysis demonstrated no significant indirect effect through BMI (mean indirect effect 0.00044; 95% CI -0.00184 to 0.00360). Conclusions: In patients with MI, the inverse relationship between physical activity and CAD severity appears independent of BMI, suggesting weight-independent cardioprotective mechanisms. Promotion of habitual physical activity should remain a central component of secondary cardiovascular prevention regardless of body weight.

Divergent Intralesional Enhancement Kinetics in a Primary Ovarian Leiomyoma on Dual-Layer Spectral CT: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Indeterminate solid adnexal masses can remain difficult to characterize on conventional CT. Dual-layer spectral CT provides iodine concentration (IC), effective atomic number (Zeff), and electron density relative to water (EDW) from the same acquisition. We report a histopathologically confirmed primary ovarian leiomyoma and describe its regional multiphasic spectral behavior. Case Presentation: A 37-year-old woman presented with an O-RADS 4 solid right adnexal mass. Retrospective analysis sampled two enhancement-defined intralesional compartments across true noncontrast (TNC), arterial, venous, and delayed phases. On TNC images, ROI-A and ROI-B showed closely similar Zeff (7.39 vs. 7.37) and EDW (103.8% vs. 103.9%). ROI-A showed intense arterial enhancement (102.2 HU; IC 2.95 mg/mL; Zeff 8.78) followed by decline, whereas ROI-B showed low early enhancement and marked delayed fill-in, with delayed values slightly exceeding ROI-A (83.8 vs. 71.3 HU; IC 1.74 vs. 1.54 mg/mL; Zeff 8.25 vs. 8.16). Initial histopathology suggested fibroma; immunohistochemistry established ovarian leiomyoma. Conclusions: The two enhancement-defined compartments showed closely similar baseline spectral measurements but divergent postcontrast behavior. EDW demonstrated substantially lower-amplitude phase-related changes than IC and Zeff. These findings are descriptive and do not establish a diagnostic spectral signature or histologic specificity. When multiphasic dual-layer spectral CT has already been clinically acquired, regional spectral analysis may provide quantitative characterization of intralesional enhancement heterogeneity. In this case, however, spectral CT did not establish the diagnosis or alter management, and definitive diagnosis remained dependent on histopathology and immunohistochemistry.

articles.title: Application Value and Cognitive Challenges of PET/CT in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Visceral Leishmaniasis: A Retrospective Single-Center Case Series and Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: The role of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) in visceral leishmaniasis (VL) remains undefined. We sought to characterize the PET/CT features of VL and assess its diagnostic and therapeutic value. Case Presentation: Four VL patients undergoing PET/CT at our hospital (2022-2025) were retrospectively analyzed as a single-center case series, combined with a literature review of published VL PET/CT cases up to December 2025. Three of the four cases exhibited increased 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) uptake in the spleen, bone marrow, and lymph nodes, with additional tonsillar uptake in one case and hepatic uptake in another; one case presented with isolated lymph node uptake. In three cases, initial bone marrow smears were negative for amastigotes, and PET/CT was performed for fever of unknown origin (FUO). One case was diagnosed within one week via metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) prompted by PET/CT and epidemiological history. In the other two, VL was not suspected; they received chemotherapy/corticosteroids for presumed hemophagocytic syndrome (HPS) or connective tissue disease, and the time from symptom onset to VL diagnosis ranged from 2.5 to 4.5 months. The fourth case, confirmed by bone marrow smear, underwent PET/CT for suboptimal treatment response to exclude other diseases. Among 99 published VL cases undergoing PET/CT, indications were documented in 35, with FUO representing 83%. Initial bone marrow smears were negative in 69% of 64 evaluable cases. Of the 88 cases with evaluable PET/CT findings, 5 showed no abnormal FDG uptake. The predominant pattern was increased 18F-FDG uptake in the reticuloendothelial system (RES), most frequently involving the spleen (73/88, 83%), bone marrow (44/88, 50%), lymph nodes (29/88, 33%), and liver (15/88, 17%); other sites (lungs/pleura, colon, tonsils) were rarely involved. Accompanying enlargement of the spleen or liver was seen in approximately 50% of cases. The most common involvement patterns were combined splenic and bone marrow (23/88, 26%) and isolated splenic (20/88, 23%). Conclusions: PET/CT can provide diagnostic clues for VL, screen for comorbidities, and guide biopsy. Typical PET/CT findings-increased RES uptake without significant other organ involvement-reflect the parasite's RES tropism. However, these findings mimic lymphoma, HPS, hematological disorders, and connective tissue diseases, risking misdiagnosis. Thus, VL should be promptly excluded in such patients using epidemiological history and etiological testing before considering alternative diagnoses.

articles.title: Intracranial Rosai-Dorfman Disease Presenting as a Posterior Fossa Dural-Based Mass Mimicking Meningioma: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Rosai-Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare non-Langerhans-cell histiocytosis that infrequently involves the central nervous system. Intracranial RDD commonly presents as a dural-based enhancing mass that radiologically resembles a meningioma. Posterior fossa involvement is particularly uncommon and may cause cerebellar compression and obstructive hydrocephalus. Case Presentation: A 58-year-old man with biopsy-confirmed systemic extranodal RDD presented with progressive headache, nausea, severe dizziness, gait instability, cerebellar ataxia, and right upper-limb dysmetria despite corticosteroid therapy. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a strongly enhancing right posterior fossa dural-based mass with vasogenic edema, cerebellar compression, fourth-ventricular effacement, and mild obstructive hydrocephalus. A smaller anterior dural-based enhancing lesion was also identified. The radiological differential diagnosis included meningioma, metastatic disease, and an inflammatory lesion. Following multidisciplinary perioperative management of anemia and complex transfusion incompatibility, gross-total resection of the symptomatic posterior fossa lesion was achieved. Histopathological examination demonstrated histiocytic proliferation with emperipolesis. The lesional histiocytes expressed S100 and CD68, showed nuclear Cyclin D1 expression in approximately 30% of lesional histiocytes, and were negative for CD1a, supporting the diagnosis of intracranial extranodal RDD. Postoperatively, the patient's headache and cerebellar manifestations improved. Follow-up imaging demonstrated complete resection of the posterior fossa lesion, resolution of the mass effect and hydrocephalus, and no recurrence at the resection site. Extracranial disease subsequently progressed, emphasizing the distinction between local and systemic disease control. Conclusions: Intracranial RDD should be considered in the differential diagnosis of meningioma-like posterior fossa masses, particularly in patients with systemic RDD. Histopathological and immunohistochemical confirmation is essential. Timely surgical resection can provide a definitive diagnosis, effective decompression, and sustained neurological improvement, while continued systemic surveillance remains necessary.

articles.title: Acetabular Insertion Avulsion Fracture of the Ligamentum Teres in a Child: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Bony avulsion at the acetabular insertion of the ligamentum teres is rare in children and may be mistaken for a loose body. Case Presentation: A 12-year-old boy had persistent left hip pain and restricted motion after a road-traffic accident without documented dislocation. Radiographs suggested acetabular injury, prompting computed tomography (CT), which showed inferior acetabular irregularity and an intra-articular fragment. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), obtained to assess associated soft-tissue injury, showed effusion and periarticular edema but did not establish the fragment's attachment. Arthroscopy identified a 15 × 10 mm notch-adjacent osseous fragment tethered to the ligamentum teres, with an intact femoral insertion and separate labral and chondral lesions. The fragment was excised because reliable arthroscopic fixation was not considered feasible under the operative conditions. After traction release, passive examination showed maintained concentric reduction without gross instability. At approximately 5 years, the modified Harris Hip Score was 100/100, pain was absent, and the patient had returned to sports; no contemporary imaging was available. Discussion: Arthroscopy distinguished a ligament-attached insertion avulsion from a free loose body. Previous excision reports provide a precedent, not comparative evidence favoring excision over fixation. Conclusions: Arthroscopy clarified the injury when imaging was indeterminate. The favorable outcome is limited to clinical and functional recovery, not long-term structural preservation.

articles.title: Antibiotic-Refractory Fever with Pyelonephritis-like Features Revealing Occult Metastatic High-Grade Serous Carcinoma: Competing Causes of Fever and Diagnostic Stewardship.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Occult malignancy is an easily missed cause of prolonged fever when urinary findings suggest pyelonephritis, and repeated empirical antibiotic courses can delay tissue diagnosis. We report such a case with competing explanations for fever. CasePresentation: A 62-year-old woman had six months of intermittent fever and one month of dysuria and right flank pain despite nine outpatient antimicrobial courses. On admission, her temperature reached 40.1 °C; she had pyuria with a non-diagnostic urine culture, para-aortic lymphadenopathy on computed tomography and negative blood cultures. Fever abated during intravenous flomoxef, recurred on the seventh day, persisted after its withdrawal and subsided by hospital day 16 before cancer-directed therapy. A single naproxen dose produced only transient defervescence. Nodal biopsy revealed metastatic high-grade serous carcinoma of the tubo-ovarian type (surgical-pathological FIGO stage IIIA1; clinical stage IVB on imaging, not histologically confirmed). The cause of fever remained undetermined; tumor-associated fever, a partially treated urinary infection and flomoxef-associated drug fever were possible contributors. Conclusions: When fever persists despite empirical antimicrobials and reassessment finds no convincing bacterial infection, clinicians should consider stopping rather than escalating antibiotics in stable, non-neutropenic patients under close monitoring, consider drug fever and other non-infectious causes, and pursue prompt tissue diagnosis.

articles.title: Diagnostic and Management Challenges in Mixed-Source MDR Sepsis in a Kidney Transplant Recipient with an Infected Sacral Pressure Ulcer Treated with VAC Therapy: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background: Kidney transplant recipients are particularly vulnerable to severe infections because of chronic immunosuppression, impaired wound healing, repeated healthcare exposure, and the potential nephrotoxicity of antimicrobial therapy. We report a complex case of multidrug-resistant (MDR) sepsis in a kidney transplant recipient with two concomitant potential infectious sources: an infected sacral pressure ulcer and recurrent urinary tract infection. Case Presentation: A 31-year-old kidney transplant recipient developed traumatic paraplegia following a road traffic accident. Prolonged immobilization was complicated by a progressive sacral pressure ulcer and recurrent urinary tract infections in the setting of neurogenic bladder dysfunction. During hospitalization, wound and urinary cultures identified MDR Gram-negative organisms, including Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Proteus mirabilis. Blood cultures obtained during systemic deterioration were positive for K. pneumoniae. Diagnostic Assessment and Therapeutic Intervention: Severe systemic infection developed with hemodynamic deterioration and markedly elevated inflammatory biomarkers. Because both the urinary tract and infected sacral wound represented plausible infectious reservoirs, the primary source of bacteremia could not be established unequivocally. Management required extensive surgical debridement, negative pressure wound therapy with instillation, culture-directed antimicrobial therapy, and close monitoring of renal allograft function. Gentamicin was used as a culture-directed therapeutic option in the setting of limited antimicrobial alternatives and impaired renal function. Conclusions: This case illustrates the diagnostic and therapeutic complexity of severe MDR infection in kidney transplant recipients when multiple potential infectious sources coexist. Successful management required early source control, microbiological assessment, individualized antimicrobial selection, and multidisciplinary monitoring aimed at controlling infection while preserving renal allograft function.

From Counting Cells to Reconstructing Death: A Commentary on Artificial Intelligence in Forensic Histopathology.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being investigated as a means to advance forensic histopathology from visual description to quantitative mapping, pattern recognition, and multimodal reconstruction of death. Recent developments in human postmortem analysis include validated whole-slide digitisation as foundational infrastructure and task-specific AI applications for diatom detection, glomerular quantification, coronary morphometry, myocardial classification, immunohistochemistry scoring, and virtual staining. AI-based postmortem interval (PMI) estimation remains experimental; the multi-organ study referenced in this commentary utilised an animal model, and human forensic validity has not yet been established. Foundation and vision-language models may ultimately extend these capabilities across organs and integrate microscopic findings with autopsy, toxicological, radiological, and circumstantial evidence. Postmortem tissue, however, is subject to autolysis, decomposition, agonal events, resuscitation, and non-standardised sampling, while the reference diagnosis is often a probabilistic whole-case opinion rather than an objective slide label. This work introduces FORENS-AI (FORensic Histopathology Evidence Network and Safeguards for AI), a conceptual architecture designed to convert computational outputs into traceable medicolegal evidence. FORENS-AI has not been empirically validated and is not presented as a standard, scoring system, clinical decision rule, or practice recommendation. The framework represents findings as an evidence graph, separates the Slide, Case, and Claim Gates, and proposes progressively stronger validation as outputs move from measurement to temporal, mechanistic, or causal inference. The primary aim is not to automate certification of death, but to identify safeguards to evaluate before AI-derived histological findings are permitted to inform expert opinion.
